SetCampaignMode GetCampaignSetup SelectedMission, SelectedDifficulty, SelectedInsertionPoint SetClientLobbyMission and SetClientLobbyDifficulty StartCountdown The countdown brings the campaign's Mission Select up behind it. The game type travels to MJOLNIRLevelLoader as pending_variant.txt beside it. The loader reads it once, when the map starts, and stages variants/<mode>.mglo in place of the level's default variant. The campaign save. The campaign menu warns that a New Game overwrites the save. A multiplayer map never writes it, because it makes no campaign checkpoints. CoreSave_0/1.sav and Progress.sav were compared against a backup after a launch, after spawning and play, and after quitting: all three unchanged. The menu therefore skips that popup.

WBP_MJOLNIRLobby, WBP_MJOLNIRMapSelect and WBP_MJOLNIRGameTypeSelect are MJOLNIR's own Widget Blueprints, cooked into pakchunk984-MJOLNIRUI (unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_mjolnir_ui.py, custom_ui.md). They derive from CommonActivatableWidget, so ContentStack:BP_AddWidget pushes them like any shipped screen: the stack hides the main menu beneath, and Back (Escape, B) pops them (bIsBackHandler).

The lobby: the players (the frontend's player states), START GAME, INVITE FRIENDS, CHANGE MAP, GAME TYPE (opens the current map's mode picker), GAME SETTINGS (host only, since mods-v0.16.0; host_game_settings.md), PRIVATE / PUBLIC GAME, MAX PLAYERS (2 to 16, host only; fireteam_join_and_cap.md), FIND GAMES and BACK, and a card with what the game will be. Since mods-v0.39.0 (with CE runtime 1.16.0's UI container) the card is two tiles, the map (its screenshot, name, game and players) and the game type (its icon, name and format), over the game settings away from the defaults in two columns of at most five lines, the last saying how many more. The tiles and the settings are buttons for the host, with the events of CHANGE MAP, GAME TYPE and GAME SETTINGS; a fireteam client's are HitTestInvisible. An older UI container keeps the one-column card with each part's description. JOIN THE DISCORD, beside the MJOLNIR CORE emblem at the top right, opens MJOLNIR's Discord invite (KismetSystemLibrary:LaunchURL: the browser, or the Discord app, opens beside the game) and writes the link in the footer.

Every menu screen has the emblem, and clicking it opens mjolnircore.com tagged for the hub's Google Analytics as a visit from the game: ?utm_source=game&utm_medium=menu&utm_campaign=logo&utm_content=<screen>, the screen being lobby, map-select, game-type, game-settings, find-games, post-game or map-download (Pick.openSite; UE4SS.log records the link). The emblem's button is cooked HitTestInvisible and made clickable by pushScreen, so with an older MJOLNIRLobby it only shows. A fireteam client without the host's map, or with another release of it, sees START GAME as DOWNLOAD MAP or UPDATE MAP (since mods-v0.20.0; live_map_install.md). Team modes (CTF and Team Slayer) show separate Red/Blue roster sections. These reflect the game's team assignments, with an Awaiting assignment section when the frontend has no simulation team yet. No local team choices or fabricated alternating assignments are written to the game. Free-for-all uses one list. The roster supports up to 16 players and scrolls without moving the surrounding controls. INVITE FRIENDS opens the game's own Friends screen (WBP_Roster_C: Platform and Cross-Platform friends, each with + Invite). It does this by calling BP_OnClicked on one of the fireteam panel's INVITE + rows (WBP_SquadBlankListViewItem_C). Those rows belong to the UI layout's squad widget, alive under every screen. Back returns to the lobby.

That screen also shows START CAMPAIGN, which starts the campaign, not the lobby's map. The last game hosted is remembered in MJOLNIRLobby\last_game.txt. The map select: up to 80 maps in a scrolling list: every installed map, then the hub's maps this PC does not have, marked DOWNLOAD (MapLive.listings, the cached GET /maps). Chips above it narrow the list by game (the hub's game: Halo CE or Halo 2), by source (official or community) and to installed maps; a map the hub does not list passes only the ALL choices. Hovering a map previews its details and game types, and leaving it shows the chosen map again; clicking picks it. The game types are tabs across the panel, the same families as the game type select, on one line each (CTF and King for the two long names). The chosen tab runs into a tray with its description and its variants as buttons. SELECT returns to the lobby with both, or, for a map not installed, opens the download screen and picks the map once it is in. Since mods-v0.39.0 (CE runtime 1.16.0's UI container): A search box over the list has the focus when the screen opens. Every word typed must be in a map's title, code or game's names ("ce", "halo 2"); the best matches come first (a word starting the title, then one starting a word of it) and the best is picked as you type, so ENTER selects it (Pick.score).

Only ENTER leaves the box focused when it commits, which tells it from the focus moving away. CLEAR empties it. Rows are sorted by title and show the map's game (CE or H2) and DOWNLOAD or CURRENT (the map the lobby has). A second click on the same row within half a second selects it. The details panel has a fixed size, with SELECT and BACK at its foot: the screenshot, the title, the hub listing's facts (game, size, players, vehicles) and summary, the author line, and the game types as a row of icon tiles. Hovering a tile describes its mode beside the row. The game type select: the host's current map and its available game types. The list on the left is families (Slayer, Capture the Flag, Oddball, Juggernaut, King of the Hill, Race, Forge), each naming its variants. The chosen family's variants are buttons on the right, under the description, so Team King is two clicks: KING OF THE HILL, then TEAM KING. A family of one has no buttons. Families are what a player would call the game, not the engine it runs on: Juggernaut, Stalker and Reverse Tag run on Oddball's engine and are a family of their own (family in Scripts/modes.lua).

The current game type is marked CURRENT on its family and its button, and its family has focus when the screen opens. Hover previews a game type; clicking chooses a pending one, and the SELECT button names it. SELECT saves that choice and updates the lobby; BACK, Escape or controller B leaves the hosted game unchanged. Availability uses the same map support, installed variant and required runtime checks as map selection. Team Slayer is supported wherever Slayer is, and Forge appears when its editor and runtime are installed. Before confirming, Scripts/gametype.lua rechecks host authority, the map and availability. The UI container ships apart from the mod, so gametype.lua looks for Variant0. A container without it has six tiles, one per engine, and a click on the chosen tile steps through its variants; an older MJOLNIRLobby on a newer container gets the same, since the seventh row and the variant buttons start collapsed. Map select does the same with its own tiles. An older UI container without this screen opens the existing map picker on the current map instead.

The game type icons are original geometric glyphs generated by tools/ue/draw_gametype_icons.py, using Pillow. They contain no extracted Halo or MCC artwork. Screens draw them on round and diamond backings, so the script centres each glyph on its canvas (brand_logo.py does the same for the emblem, ignoring the source's faint outer pixels). Run python tools/ue/draw_gametype_icons.py to rebuild the eight transparent 256-pixel PNGs in unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/GameTypeIcons; add --sheet out/gametype-icons.png for a preview sheet. The UI builder imports them as T_MJMode_<Name> under /Game/MJOLNIR/UI/ModeIcons and cooks them with the screen in chunk 984. The lobby shows the selected mode's same icon beside its game type title, including when following the host's choice as a fireteam client. Missing icon textures hide the lobby emblem and do not prevent mode selection. On a container without the Race and Juggernaut glyphs, those families borrow the flag and the Slayer reticle.

Each button's own graph calls the widget's MJ_Event(<event>): start, invite, changemap, gametype, gamesettings, listing, maxdown, maxup, maxplayers, findgames, discord, logo (every screen), back, select, map:<i>, hover:<i>, unhover:<i>, mode:<i>, modehover:<i>, modeunhover:<i>, search, searched, search_clear, filter:game, filter:source, filter:installed (FIND GAMES and GAME SETTINGS send their own, such as game:<i>, sort:<column> and reset). Lua hooks it and handles the event off the click, in ExecuteInGameThread. No native delegate binding is involved. Only the injected fallback MULTIPLAYER button still needs it (next section). Game type events compare the sender's native UObject address with the active screen, so delayed events from a previous picker cannot change the new choice. tools/tests/test_gametype_picker.lua covers this and the selection, cancellation, availability and older-container behavior. Without the UI container, MULTIPLAYER falls back to the campaign-menu screens described next. The custom screens use a 2560×1440 design canvas fitted as a whole to the viewport, keeping columns together at lower resolutions and ultrawide aspect ratios. Flat translucent navy panels, fine cyan rules, regular weight type and gold primary actions share the scoreboard's visual style. The game's animated background and CommonUI menu stack remain in use.
The main menu's own MULTIPLAYER button

Verified on CU4, 2026-10-02. MULTIPLAYER is a real button of WBP_MainMenu, cooked into the menu's package: It sits after the hidden Remix button, between CAMPAIGN and PLAY CO-OP. It is there the first time the menu shows. It has the menu's own styling, focus, keyboard and gamepad navigation, and Back. Its click pushes WBP_MJOLNIRLobby itself, through the call the menu uses for Customization (HaloUIManagerSubsystem.PushStreamableContentToLayerFullscreen). Remix keeps its slot, its click and its unlock rule. Lua only fills the lobby once it exists (NotifyOnNewObject on the lobby class) and handles its events, as above. mjolnir ue menu-button --out-dir # writes pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU_P tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh builds it into the CE runtime pack, beside the lobby's own container (chunk 984). The defaults are the main menu, MultiplayerButton, "MULTIPLAYER", after RemixButton, opening /Game/MJOLNIR/UI/WBP_MJOLNIRLobby.WBP_MJOLNIRLobby_C. ue_asset::menu_button does the work, and finds everything by name. What a new button takes (all in the one package):
The main menu's own MULTIPLAYER button

added copied from the button a new export in the widget tree, its label changed from the string table entry Menus/main_item_remixmenu to the text "MULTIPLAYER" RemixButton its slot a new HaloUIButtonContainerSlot export, listed in MainButtonContainer.Slots right after Remix's Remix's slot the click function a new BndEvt__…MultiplayerButton… export, added to the class's Children and FuncMap; it enters the ubergraph at the new block Remix's click stub the binding a ComponentDelegateBindings row: MultiplayerButton.OnButtonBaseClicked → that function Remix's row the variable an ObjectProperty named MultiplayerButton, last among the class's own properties RemixButton's the push a block before the ubergraph's EX_EndOfScript: player controller, push, pop the Customization push New exports go at the end of the export map, and the block at the end of the ubergraph, so no package index, jump or entry point moves. Each new export gets a dependency bundle like its template's. Its create and serialize commands sit beside the template's in the export bundle.
The main menu's own MULTIPLAYER button

The class default object has to move too. An unversioned property header numbers a class's own properties first and its supers' after them. The new variable is own slot 35, so every inherited value of Default__WBP_MainMenu_C moves up one slot: its header's skip before slot 87 goes from 53 to 54. Without that the CDO reads garbage, and the game crashed as the frontend built the menu. Rebuild after every game update. The container replaces the whole WBP_MainMenu package. A stale copy would hide the updated menu, so the runtime pack has to be rebuilt from the new build. The command refuses when something it looks for is gone, rather than guessing. Without the container (an older runtime pack), the main menu has no MultiplayerButton, and MJOLNIRLobby falls back to injecting its own button into Remix's slot (next section). The log says which one is in use: MULTIPLAYER is on the main menu (its own button), or ... (injected: ...). mjolnir ue disasm --package <pkg> --export <name index> prints a Blueprint function's bytecode (ue_asset::kismet). That's how the Remix gate (UpdateButtonsEnabled: IsRemixMenuUnlocked) and the pushes were found.

A screen is a WBP_CampaignMenu_C (header, sub-header, a HaloUIButtonContainer, a description and the fireteam panel) pushed with WBP_MeteoriteUILayout_C.ContentStack:BP_AddWidget. Its own buttons are swapped for ours. Buttons are WBP_MeteoriteStandaloneButtonDefault_C, the main menu's kind. Use the container's own slots. Put a button into one with ReplaceButtonContainerChildAt. That keeps the button group consistent. Appending after hidden native buttons left the group's selection on a hidden button, and CommonUI routes Enter through the selected button. Labels. Set a label after the button is in the tree. A label set before construction is lost. Repeat clicks. bInteractableWhenSelected = true. Otherwise a clicked button is selected and ignores the next press. Re-activation. The campaign menu's activation resets its own buttons and texts, so BP_OnActivated re-applies the screen. Main menu entry. Without pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU, the injected MULTIPLAYER takes the slot of the hidden Remix button. A light poll puts it back on each new main menu. Loading classes. UE4SS's LoadAsset needs the asset's object path (/Game/.../WBP_CampaignMenu.WBP_CampaignMenu). Neither the bare package nor the _C class path works. The frontend loads most screen classes only when they are first opened.
Screens from the game's widgets (fallback) › Clicks

A CommonUI button reports a click only through its OnButtonBaseClicked dynamic delegate, and the path to it is native-to-native. Hooks on the button's BP_OnClicked, HandleButtonClicked or BP_OnPressed never fire for a Blueprint that does not implement them. UE4SS's Lua cannot bind a delegate either: the property comes back as an opaque object. UE4SS.dll exports what binding needs: UObject::GetPropertyByNameInChain. The plain GetPropertyByName sees only the Blueprint class's own properties. The FWeakObjectPtr and FName constructors. FMulticastDelegateProperty::AddDelegate, the engine's own add. So mjolnir_lobby_bind binds each button's delegate to a clicker. The clicker is a hidden WBP_MeteoriteHyperlink_C whose Blueprint function SetHyperlinkText takes no parameters and only sets its own text. The Lua hook on that function is the click. The clicker is parked, collapsed, in the button's LeafNamedSlot, so it lives exactly as long as the button. It is armed 300 ms after creation, because construction calls SetHyperlinkText too. Lua has no C API here (UE4SS does not export it), so requests and replies travel as native/lobby_request.txt and lobby_reply.txt. Hook only Blueprint-scripted functions. A hook on HaloUIButtonContainer:HandleButtonGroupSelectionChanged (native, with parameters) crashed the game inside UE4SS's argument marshalling.

The lobby reads the launcher's MJOLNIRMaps\maps.json, rebuilt from every installed map (crates/blam-pack/src/maps.rs). For codes that list lacks, it reads MJOLNIRLevelLoader/maps.json, which mjolnir level bake --install-test writes (Lua cannot list a directory). Each entry has: code title description modes: the level file's modes, else its variant tools/level/gen_ce_level.py names the stock maps (STOCK_TITLES) and lists "modes": ["slayer"], plus "ctf" when the map has a flag for each team. A mode is offered when the map lists it and variants/<mode>.mglo is installed.

Update 2026-10-21: the lobby service is built on the hub, as a D1-backed polled API (hub/src/lib/api/lobby.ts, PR #106). The hand-off is the PlayFab lobby's connection string, given to the game's own Steam join handler (mods-v0.11.0, PR #127; multiplayer_servers.md), and on the Xbox app to the GDK session's invite handler (mods-v0.23.0 and v0.23.1, PR #179 and #181). FIND GAMES lists the hub's games, not Steam lobbies. The session join was verified on two PCs on 2026-10-01 (03fae037). Match chat shipped in the match HUD, not the lobby service (mods-v0.27.0, PR #200). Discord Rich Presence and public-session Join Game are implemented through local IPC (discord_presence.md). Still not built: join codes (JOIN PRIVATE) and Steam lobbies.

A lobby service of our own (Cloudflare, beside the hub), since Game Pass and Store players have no Steam. Planned shape: a game list, join codes, the member list and chat, as a D1-backed polled API first. Live chat may move to a Durable Object. The open question is the hand-off: how a client joins the host's PlayFab session. Steam lobbies, for Steam players only. Steam is live in the process (steam_api64 v1.57), and its flat API can be called from the native half. Pieces: FIND GAMES: a lobby list. JOIN PRIVATE: friends-only and invite lobbies. The friends list's Join Game: GameLobbyJoinRequested, +connect_lobby. Bringing lobby members into the host's fireteam session. Discord rich presence over its local IPC pipe is implemented; see setup and verification. Two-player verification of the session join and of Megalo kill scoring.

Question: how do players find games and host them, and can a game run on a dedicated server that players connect to? Short answer: Every game is hosted by a player: the host's game is a listen server, and PlayFab Party carries the traffic. Public games are built: a host switches its lobby to PUBLIC GAME, the game is listed on the hub, and FIND GAMES joins it through the game's own invite flow (below). A true dedicated server is not possible: there is no server binary, and no way to run the Blam sim outside the game client. A headless host (the real game, windowless) works on a GPU machine, but the idea was dropped on 2026-10-02. The findings are kept below. Status as of 2026-10-02 (CU4); updated 2026-10-21.

A client gets it from /join, which requires sign-in. See the header comment in lobby.ts.
How a game is hosted today

The host's game creates a PlayFab lobby (membership) and a PlayFab Party network (traffic), then opens a PlayFabNetDriver when the first remote player arrives (fireteam_join_and_cap.md). Party traffic goes through Microsoft's relays, so hosts need no port forwarding. The game opens only UDP 57716+. The exe carries DirectPeerConnectivity strings. The game's setting for it is unread. The lobby is Private, with no owner migration. When the host leaves, the game ends. That is the main argument for always-on hosts. Joining needs only the lobby's connection string, which reaches PFMultiplayerJoinLobby through JoinSession or the Steam invite-accepted path. The exe imports PFLobbyGetConnectionString.

Hosting. A host's lobby opens as PUBLIC GAME: MULTIPLAYER lists the game unless the host already picked PUBLIC or PRIVATE this launch (Games.defaultPublic), so a private choice holds through matches and back to the lobby. The button switches between PUBLIC GAME and PRIVATE GAME (host only). FORGE starts private without counting as the host's choice, and the mod check can keep the game private. While public, games.lua: reads the PlayFab lobby's connection string from the native half; POST /lobbies with the map, game type, players, the host's MAX PLAYERS (max_players), its game settings line (settings, host_game_settings.md) and the string; heartbeats every 30 s, and at once after a map, game type or start changes, with players, MAX PLAYERS, game settings, state (open, in_game, full) and the current string (the game makes a new lobby after leaving one); DELETEs the listing when the host goes private or joins another game. A game that quits drops out when its heartbeat goes stale (90 s). The lobby's footer says why a game isn't listed (no launcher sign-in, an old key, the hub unreachable, no online lobby).

Public or private mid-match (MJOLNIRLobby 0.24.0). The HOST MENU has MAKE PUBLIC / MAKE PRIVATE, and chat has /public and /private (multiplayer_hud.md); FORGE matches stay private. Each change and the listing's outcome reach the host's chat as a system line (MJOLNIRLobby\chat_notice.txt, read by MJOLNIRHud). The native half (post_join_state) posts the lobby's joining state at once rather than at the game's next update: Public: membership unlocked and _flags given the join bits (what a game started public keeps). The PreLogin pass and the joiner injection follow the flag live. Private, in a match: the lock and _flags the game itself last asked for (locked, 1344 after a start), so nobody new can join. Going private in the menu posts nothing: the game posts no update on the way back from a match, so its last ask there is the match's lock, which would keep invited friends out.

A host stays online alone (MJOLNIRLobby 0.24.0). As shipped, a match started with one session member leaves the session to play offline (UBlamOnlineSessionSubsystem::SetSessionRunning, exe 0x7abb940), so a game started private and alone lost its lobby. It couldn't be listed later, and RETURN TO LOBBY (a servertravel) never got one back. Only SAVE AND EXIT or a restart did (2026-11-07). Each start from our lobby now writes native\host_online.txt, and the branch patch public games used applies to any host, public or private. FORGE keeps the shipped branch. Where a host still ends up with no lobby (FORGE, or a game update that moves the patched branch), RETURN TO LOBBY with nobody else in the match calls BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem:EndCampaign, SAVE AND EXIT's own exit. About 3 s after the menu loads, the game asks for a new session itself (traced 2026-11-08 through the hooked public CreateSession: exe 0x7ac2790 to 0x7abee20). That function returns early on state bits a solo start leaves set, and only that exit clears them: a servertravel back, or EndCampaign from the menu, makes no lobby. In the menu with no lobby, the footer says how to get one back.

FIND GAMES (WBP_MJOLNIRFindGames, chunk 984) is a server table of up to 40 public games: Columns: server (name, then host account and country), map ("NOT INSTALLED" when missing), game type (teams or free for all), players (and open slots), ping (signal bars and the estimate), status (LOBBY, IN MATCH, FULL, and a different MJOLNIR Lobby version). Columns are fixed-width boxes in both the header and the rows, so they line up whatever the text. Sorting: a column heading sorts by it; again reverses it. Ping, lowest first, by default. Ties go to fuller games, then nearer ones. Filters: GAME TYPE and MAP cycle through the values listed; HIDE FULL, HIDE IN MATCH and MAPS I HAVE are toggles. The count above the table says how many games the filters hide. Details: hovering a row previews it; clicking chooses it. The panel shows the host, map, game type, a pip per player slot, ping, region (country and Cloudflare colo) and version, with warnings for a missing map or another version. JOIN follows the game the details show, and says why it can't join (GAME FULL, MAP NOT INSTALLED). QUICK JOIN joins the best game the filters allow: map installed, a free slot, then the same version, better signal, more players. The list refreshes every 30 s while the screen is up. The sort, game type filter and toggles are kept in MJOLNIRLobby\find_games.txt.

native\lobbies_sample.json (a /lobbies reply) stands in for the hub when present, to try the screen with many games. An older runtime pack's FIND GAMES (one label per row) still works with this Lobby, unsorted and unfiltered; this runtime pack's widget keeps the names an older Lobby fills. Joining. JOIN gets the string from /lobbies/{id}/join and writes it to native\join_request.txt. mjolnir_join queues it, and the next FOnlineAsyncTaskManagerSteam::OnlineTick (online thread) calls the task manager's own GameRichPresenceJoinRequested_t handler with it. That handler is what a Steam "Join Game" runs: it builds FOnlineAsyncEventSteamInviteAccepted; a connect string without SteamConnectIP= is stored whole as CONNECTIONSTRING; the game leaves its fireteam and joins the host's. How the native half finds it, by pattern rather than address: OnlineTick by its body bytes; exe RVA 0x6a7b580 on CU4, the only pointer to it is vtable slot 6 at 0xbc86b00; the handler by scanning the task manager for the CCallback whose m_iCallback is 337 and whose m_pObj is the manager (+0x380 on CU4, m_Func 0x6a7b5d0). The handler converts the connect string as a C string, so Steam's 256-byte limit doesn't apply. Today's strings are 106 characters anyway.

On the Xbox app there is no Steam subsystem. mjolnir_join hands the string to the GDK session's own invite handler, from the GDK subsystem's tick, the way an Xbox join arrives (mods-v0.23.0 and v0.23.1, PR #179 and #181; game_pass.md). join_request.txt may carry the host's SteamID64 or XUID after the string. A website's mjolnir://join/<lobby> link reaches the launcher, which leaves the lobby id in native\pending_join.txt; once signed in on the menu, FIND GAMES opens and joins that game as JOIN would (mods-v0.21.0 and launcher-v0.13.0, PR #166). Auth. Listing needs lobbies:write; /join needs any signed-in key. The native half reads the launcher's key from %APPDATA%\com.devnull9090.mjolnir-launcher\hub_auth.json and sends it to the hub only. Players without the launcher can still host for, and be invited by, friends. An account banned from matchmaking can neither list nor join (403), and a banned host's game drops out of the list (PR #172; player_identity.md). A game on a map you lack: JOIN reads DOWNLOAD AND JOIN. The map installs in the running game first, then the join runs as usual (live_map_install.md). Not built: JOIN PRIVATE by short code (an unlisted registration the hub maps to the lobby).
Dedicated servers › A. An Unreal dedicated server: not possible

The shipping exe is a game target, not a server target. IsRunningDedicatedServer is not in it. PlayFab's own server product (JoinLobbyAsServer, RequestMultiplayerServer) needs the title's server credentials. Those belong to the publisher.
Dedicated servers › B. The Blam sim on its own: not practical

HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll could in principle be loaded by our own process. But clients are Unreal clients: they expect an Unreal server speaking UE replication (GameState, PlayerState, the BlamExperience readiness flags, pawns), with the Blam network endpoints carried inside it; all of it runs over PlayFab Party, under a PlayFab identity of the title. That means reimplementing an Unreal server around the sim. Not worth it.
Dedicated servers › C. A headless host: works with a GPU (dropped 2026-10-02)

The facts come from a static research pass on 2026-10-21. Nobody launched the game for it. Verified means someone read the code, data or file that shows it. Inferred means it rests on names, Reach knowledge, analogy, or a chain with one unread link; the link is named. Precedence. Where reports disagree, the verifier's verdict beats the first report, a follow-up pass that read the deciding code beats both, and the codec's round trip over Bungie's variants beats any reading of the bitstream. Section 7 lists what stays open. Reach is a hint, not proof. Names of Megalo actions, conditions, enums and Reach object types below are ReachVariantTool's. Their CU4 wire format is verified; their CU4 behaviour is verified only where an RVA is given. Bungie's variants are Microsoft content. Sources and how to read this

Notation, as in the Megalo docs: G = engine globals [TLS+0x38]; GG = game globals [TLS+0x60], with the game options at GG+0x10; v = the running variant at GG+0x15f0 and o = v+4 (variant-format offsets are o-relative); P = a player datum ([TLS+0x30], 0x4b0 bytes each); D(h) = an object datum; MP(h) = its multiplayer block at D(h) + u16 D(h)+0x182.

CE's Standard game types are built (section 3.6): Slayer, Team Slayer, CTF, Assault, Oddball, Team Oddball, Juggernaut, King, Crazy King, Team King, Race, Team Race, Rally and Team Rally. This summary was written when only Slayer and CTF ran; the rest of it stands. The engine is all there. It is Reach's game-engine layer, and every Reach mode is data for it. Read statically, a MJOLNIR match runs with the options' mode byte 3 (multiplayer) and 60 ticks a second, and the fireteam runs Reach's distributed simulation over the exe's Party transport: the host is DistributedServer (5) and runs every trigger; a client is DistributedClient (4), runs only the variant's local trigger and receives everything else. The sim knows every team exactly and paints team colours. Unreal never sees them. A flag's owner team (MP+0x19) and a player's team (P+0xad) are exact and replicate to clients. The sim computes change colours from them, but the per-frame snapshot it pushes to Unreal carries no owner team and no colour. It carries the model variant, the region permutations and the unit team bytes. Both colour bugs come from Lua guessing what the snapshot does not say. CTF flags are coloured by a guess keyed to the actor, not the sim object: nearest stand, then the last incident of either flag, then red. Eleven paths pick the wrong team.

The deterministic fix is a second flag tag whose default model variant is blue, read in Lua through GetVariantName(). It needs no native code. Custom armour is a Blam model variant. Every armour except Mk V Classic is a body plus 11 to 17 static armour plates and a static helmet. MJOLNIR tints only skeletal meshes, so the plates and helmet keep the player's own colours over a red or blue body. Timing paths add misses. The fix makes the sim choose Mk V Classic for every Spartan in team games (a hook on sim 0x2f2730, on every machine), then tints on the game's own OnRegionsChanged events. Other modes. Team Slayer is a script and nothing else. After it come the modes that need a player colour channel (Juggernaut, Infection), then carried objects and zones (Headhunter, Oddball, KOTH), then modes whose placements must be authored per map (Territories, Stockpile, Assault), then Race. The common blockers are a 20-entry object type list, a HUD channel for Megalo widgets, objective text and waypoint icons (none reaches Unreal), boundary drawing, and MJOLNIR ending every match at the first round. Proof. The codec round-trips 417 of 417 of Bungie's Megalo variants bit for bit. mjolnir megalo dump lists any variant. A local remap would let Bungie's own modes run as an oracle on this PC. CU4 enforces almost no limits on a variant, so a validator must, before any hub upload.
Every mode is then checked on two PCs, by the user, before release. ---

4. Proving a mode correct › 4.1 The bitstream: Bungie's corpus round trip

The codec and its tests land with branch work/reach-game-mode-support-2eca91; at 772eca0d only the typed builder exists. crates/blam-megalo/src/raw.rs decodes and encodes any variant by the grammar in crates/blam-megalo/grammar/megalo_cu4.json, which was read out of the CU4 decoder (sim 0x392a40 and every callee). It is strict: a read past the buffer or a tree that no longer fits the grammar is an error. MCC_REACH="C:/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Halo The Master Chief Collection/haloreach" \ cargo test -p blam-megalo --test roundtrip crates/blam-megalo/tests/roundtrip.rs checks MJOLNIR's own variants, the 9 fixtures under tools/tests/fixtures, and, when MCC_REACH is set, every Megalo variant in game_variants and hopper_game_variants. Result on 2026-10-21: 417 of 417 round-trip bit for bit, each ending within its last byte with zero padding (55 Firefight, 1 Forge and 1 campaign file skipped). Without MCC_REACH the Bungie test passes without checking. Verified. What it proves: the wire format of every opcode Bungie used (80 of the 106 action types; every condition but 9, 10, 16 and 17). 4. Proving a mode correct › 4.2 Golden dumps

mjolnir megalo dump <file.mglo file.bin> [--out <file>] (crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs:356) lists every field in read order, string text, teams, traits, labels, and the script as triggers with named conditions and actions, and states the round-trip result and its checks (trigger ranges, entry points against attributes, nested calls in range, every condition and action owned by a trigger). Proposed (not built): Commit golden dumps of MJOLNIR's own released variants, built the way the release builds them, and fail CI when a variant's dump changes without its golden file. A reviewer then reads a script diff, not bytes. Compare a new MJOLNIR mode with Bungie's by reading the two dumps side by side on this PC (Bungie's dumps stay local).
4. Proving a mode correct › 4.3 Bungie's modes as a local oracle

Bungie's files fit the loader: the largest payload is 17,816 bytes, under the 0x5000 bound, and both encoding versions (0x6a, 0x6b) decode. Unmapped they are wrong: Slayer (type 76), KOTH (151), Oddball, Territories and Assault are wiped by validation; Bungie's CTF and Headhunter load but create a magnum and a rocket launcher, or shotguns, because CU4's low indices are weapons; Infection loads with wrong trait weapons. Verified from the bitsets. A local remap tool over raw.rs trees would rewrite the object type bitset, the type operands (Create Object, Object Type, label filters, Add Weapon), and trait and loadout weapon and ability indices, with the missing list entries as a local override and Bungie's labels on a test map. Then Bungie's KOTH and MJOLNIR's KOTH can be played on the same map, expecting the same incidents and scores. Design; not built. The boundary is legal, not technical: read the files from the MCC folder at test time; never commit them, their dumps or remapped copies; never upload or ship them.

Safe as it stands: undefined actions 107-127 do nothing; every player, object, team and timer reference resolves to a defined slot; the incident index is bounded by its iterator; action 100 runs only scripts the scenario has. Action 97 (griefer penalty) can get a player booted, so a validator should refuse it. The validator runs at hub upload and again at install, over the decoded tree, and rejects any variant past these caps: file at most 0x5000 bytes; main string data at most 0x4c00 bytes (compressed: the embedded length too) and at most 112 strings; the counts above; HUD widgets at most 4; condition type at most 17, action type at most 106, trigger type at most 5, compare operator at most 5; each trigger's ranges inside the arrays; nested trigger indices inside the trigger count and no cycle; every object type operand declared in the bitset; incident indices from the known list. A native guard in mjolnir_megalo_variant repeats the check (or verifies the validator's hash) before it copies the file and writes the name buffer, and refuses anything larger than 0x5000 bytes.

Every machine must run byte-identical declarations. Fact 7 means a client with a different variant decodes the host's state into the wrong variables. Today that is guaranteed by every machine staging the same file with the same settings line. A game type is only as readable as what Unreal draws. Why the runtime pack is the "min runtime". Object types are indices into the motl, and MJOLNIR's motl is an override that ships in the CE runtime pack (pakchunk990-MJOLNIRMOTL_P, map_distribution.md, "The CE runtime pack"). It adds the CTF flag at 18 and the health pack at 19 to the 18 shipped weapons (tools/level/build_ctf_flag.sh:80-87). A variant compiled against one motl is wrong against another (fact 3). So: a game type names its object types by name in the manifest, and depends on the runtime pack range whose motl has them; the runtime's motl becomes append-only: an entry, once released, keeps its index, so a game type compiled against runtime 1.x keeps working on every later 1.x. deps and compat already exist and the launcher already installs a dependency's floor first (map_distribution.md, "Dependencies"), so no new mechanism is needed. Like a map, type gametype implies the code mods (MJOLNIRCore, MJOLNIRLevelLoader, MJOLNIRLobby, MJOLNIRHud), at a version that understands game type packages.

The level loader patches the host's settings into each machine's copy of the variant before staging it (mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua:5976-5992). Today it walks the variant with a Lua grammar reader (mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/variant_settings.lua), which stops at the first player trait, user option or compressed string table (:75, :155). MJOLNIRHud's reader has the same limits (mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/variant.lua:7-8). Any variant with user options, which is any useful custom game type, breaks both. Instead, the compiler writes the bit offset and width of each field a host may set: score to win, time limit, the respawn and trait fields the settings screen offers, and each user option's current value (a u3 index or an s10 value, re/megalo_variant_format.md). Each has a fixed width in a given file, so writing a new value in place leaves every later bit where it was. Lua then writes bits at known offsets and needs no grammar. The CLI already does this for vehicle-set labels (filters_at in <out>.layout.json, crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs:308-320; read by mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/vehicle_sets.lua). The hub recomputes the offsets from its own decode and refuses a layout that disagrees.

A text language, compiled by blam-megalo, is Phase 3. It is not built. Its principles: Model it on what the community already knows. Reach modders write Megalo in ReachVariantTool's dialect: Lua-like blocks, for each player, event blocks for the entry points, aliases for variable slots, declarations with network priorities, one name per opcode. ReachVariantTool's manual is CC0, so its names and descriptions can be reused freely. Its code is GPLv3 and MJOLNIR is MIT: none of it is copied, translated or linked. The compiler is written from MJOLNIR's own grammar file, grammar/megalo_cu4.json, which already carries Reach's names as hints (reach_names). One source of grammar. The compiler, the decompiler, the validator and the hub's checks all read grammar/megalo_cu4.json. The decoder already does. CU4's vocabulary, not Reach's. Object types resolve by name against the runtime's motl; incidents against CU4's game_incident tag (all 123 incident indices Bungie's variants raise have the same names there, VERIFIED by tag dump); waypoint icons, sounds and widget icons are Reach's names and are not checked for CU4. Seconds, not ticks. Timers are declared in seconds and scaled by the sim (sim 0x408d00). Counting ticks bakes in a tick rate, which is how the CLI's CTF flag reset and health-pack respawn came to run at half length (fact 15). The compiler owns declarations.

It allocates variable slots, sets network priorities and builds the object-type bitset from every type the script uses. Bungie's bitsets are exactly the union of the types their opcodes and labels name (VERIFIED over the corpus), so nothing is lost. Client code is explicit. On fireteam clients only the local, local init and pregame entry points run (fact 6). The language keeps per-player presentation in those blocks, and says so in its errors. An example, in illustrative syntax that is not final: game type team_kills teams 2 score to win 50 score label "kills" every tick, for each player: if current_player died this tick by a kill: killer = killer of current_player if killer.team != current_player.team: killer.score += 1 This is a whole Team Slayer. It compiles to one trigger that runs for each player (trigger type 1), a Killer Type condition with the kill bit (condition 3), Get Killer (action 29), a Compare on the two teams (condition 1) and Modify Score (action 1). The team's total follows from the player scores, because the variant's team scoring is sum (sim 0x2b0180 → slot 2 0x3ef690, mode 0). The engine ends the round at the score to win (fact 14), so the script needs no end check.

It reads MCC .bin files (BLF) as well as bare .mglo, refuses non-Megalo engines, and states in its header whether the file encodes back bit for bit (crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs:356-406, crates/blam-megalo/src/dump.rs:1074). Not committed yet, as above. When the language lands, dump prints it, and the tests require compile(dump(x)) == x bit for bit over MJOLNIR's variants and, on a machine with MCC installed, Bungie's.

One discrepancy to fix in Phase 1. The main string table's offsets are stored per language in 0xe0 bytes, 112 entries (0x738 + 12 × 0xe0 = 0x11b8, where the string data begins). A 113th string writes into the next language's offsets, and for the last language into the string data. The CLI allows 127 strings (crates/blam-cli/src/megalo.rs:298). Shipped variants stay well under 112 (the CTF variant has 76), so nothing is broken today; the CLI limit should be 112.

A map names its game types: the level file's modes (tools/level/gen_ce_level.py:1331: Slayer, plus CTF when the CE scenario has flags), copied into maps.json and the map pack's manifest (manifest.ts:31) and into the hub's map_listings.modes (hub/migrations/0012_maps_and_lobbies.sql:17-18). A hub game type cannot be listed by every map author in advance, so this does not scale. Proposed: labels, as Reach did. A Megalo variant already states what it needs from a map. Each object filter (label) has a name, optional type, team and number constraints, and a "map must have at least" count (re/megalo_variant_format.md, LABEL). Bungie's CTF, for example, requires at least one ctf_flag_return object (VERIFIED, decode of ctf_054). The map side is already there: a scenario placement's multiplayer data carries a Megalo label, an owner team, a spawn order and a boundary shape (defs/hce/tag-definitions.json, scenario multiplayer object struct), and the conversion writes labels for CTF stands, spawns and health spots (tools/level/gen_ce_level.py:1080, :1121).

Distribution › Do clients need the file?

Yes, today and through Phases 1 and 2. Two facts decide it. Each machine decodes the host's per-tick Megalo state against its own declarations (fact 7). Byte-identical staging guarantees they match. MJOLNIR's loader replaces the live variant on every machine at the round reset (fact 1), which overwrites whatever the session delivered (fact 8). A client never runs the host's rules (fact 6), so what it needs from the file is the declarations, its local, local init and pregame triggers, and the options and strings its HUD shows. It may become no. If a client that stages nothing still ends up with the host's file variant through the game-variant session parameter, the client's copy comes from the host by construction and cannot mismatch. One live read settles it: on a client with no .mglo staged, after the first round reset, read the live variant (o = [TLS+0x60]+0x15f4): its encoding version at o+0x5dc0 (the default variant has 0x6b, MJOLNIR's files 0x6a) and its trigger count at o+0x63f4, and compare with the host. The lobby DLL already reads [TLS+0x60] on the sim thread (native/lobby/mjolnir_lobby.c:2776-2790). Even then a client wants gametype.json for its lobby and HUD, which the lobby message can carry instead of a download.
Safety › What a Megalo variant can and cannot do

Lua mods are code: UE4SS Lua has io, os.execute and package.loadlib, which is why the hub ships Lua only from reviewed, signed CI (hub_architecture.md, section 2). A Megalo variant is data for an interpreter with a fixed instruction set: action ids 0 to 106 and condition ids 0 to 17, where 0 is "none" in both. It cannot Evidence Status read or write files, open sockets, load libraries or call native code every action handler acts on sim state (sim executor 0x399110); the only effects outside the match are incidents, kill-feed and sound events, and a theater film marker written only while a film records (0x41e310) VERIFIED raise the engine's own incidents (kill, death, player_spawn, round_over, game_over ...) refused range at sim 0x41e11d VERIFIED unlock achievements, skulls or terminals Unreal's default incident branch only prints debug text for them VERIFIED move a player to another team in a team game sim slot 53 0x3fee90 ignores the script's team byte when teams are on VERIFIED crash the executor with an unknown opcode action types 107 to 127 fall to the switch's no-op default VERIFIED
Safety › What a Megalo variant can and cannot do

It can, inside the match Evidence Status change any score, end the round, kill, heal, give weapons, apply traits, create and delete objects the action table VERIFIED show a HUD banner: any incident it may submit (by index into CU4's incident list) whose name is a row of the banner table default branch, HandleHudBannerMessage VERIFIED flood the kill feed or the sound queue every tick (actions 16, 51) posts engine event 0x1e per recipient (sim 0x5132f0) VERIFIED accrue a griefer penalty on any player every tick (action 97) sim 0x35d530 VERIFIED call; that it can boot a player INFERRED run any HaloScript function the loaded scenario carries (action 100) sim 0x36c1a0, 0x1f6b60, 0x1fcf30, bounded to scripts that exist VERIFIED bound; converted maps are cloned from campaign canvases, so campaign scripts may be reachable (INFERRED) fill the 512-entry megalo_objects pool Create Object what happens when it is full is open Hub game types refuse actions 97 and 100 (Validation). Scores a script sets are whatever the script says, so match records carry the game type release (the matches change above) and are never mixed with official game types' statistics.
Safety › Unvalidated input is not safe data

CU4's decoder trusts the file. A crafted .mglo can do worse than misbehave: The main string table overruns its buffer with chosen bytes. The reader copies the string data into a 0x4c00-byte buffer at o+0x11b8 with no comparison against 0x4c00. Uncompressed, the length is the stream's u15 size, at most 0x7fff bytes; by arithmetic the overrun then stays inside the 0xf860-byte variant object but covers the encoding version and the whole script region. Compressed, the inflater's output length is the stream's own big-endian u32, which CU4 never checks, and zlib can expand the at most 0x5000 input bytes far beyond the buffer. VERIFIED (sim 0x3949c0, 0x32a620); the inflater itself (sim 0x6c7b20) was not read, and whether the overrun can be turned into code execution has not been examined. Treat it as if it could. Counts past the stores overwrite the next field (table under Validation), and a fifth HUD widget overwrites player 0's engine state. VERIFIED (sim 0x392a40, 0x40a130). Indices the runtime trusts: nested trigger calls with no bound and no depth limit (a self-call exhausts the stack), trigger condition and action ranges, object-type operands into the motl, and the six-entry jump tables behind compare operators and trigger types. VERIFIED (sim 0x399110, 0x423a70, 0x41c3b0, 0x421b80, 0x39ed40, 0x423fc0).
Safety › Unvalidated input is not safe data

So "sandboxed like a game type" (map_distribution.md) holds only for a variant that passed the validator. The validator is the security boundary, and it runs at every point where bytes could come from someone else: The hub, on upload. Nothing that fails it is listed or downloadable. The launcher, on install. A tampered cache or a bypassed hub is caught on the player's machine. The native loader, before staging. mjolnir_megalo_variant copies native\variant.mglo to HotReload\mjolnir.mglo with no check (native/map_registry/mjolnir_map_registry.c:1339). Before that copy it refuses a file over 0x5000 bytes, a version other than 0x6a/0x6b, and any string table whose sizes break the rules above, with a log line and no name written, so the sim runs the default variant. That is a few dozen lines of C over the start of the stream. The full validation happened at install. After the round reset, a read-back. The native half reads the live variant's version (o+0x5dc0) and trigger count (o+0x63f4) on the sim thread and logs "decoded" or "wiped", so a game type the sim silently rejected (fact 3) is visible. o is [TLS+0x60]+0x15f4. This is why a game type can live in the content tier, with open upload, signing and review for new authors, rather than with Lua and native code: once validated, what its bytes can do is bounded by the interpreter, not by who wrote them.
Safety › Unvalidated input is not safe data

Runtime patches that bound the sim's own checks are a fallback only. They would track CU4 addresses across game updates like the seven switch patches (mjolnir_map_registry.c:1193-1236), and validating before decode makes them unnecessary. An open risk outside the hub. The game-variant session parameter (fact 8) delivers the host's variant to clients natively. Its serializer was not traced, so whether a modified host can push a malformed variant into a client's sim this way is unknown. The risk exists today, with or without hub game types. It needs its own look before Phase 2 ships.

HCE ships no EULA text in its install, and the Steam EULA was not reviewed. Halo fan content falls under Microsoft's Game Content Usage Rules (https://www.xbox.com/en-US/developers/rules): no selling, a notice that the game is Microsoft's and the item is not endorsed, and nothing objectionable. The hub's terms for game types restate these. Bungie's and 343's own variants are Microsoft content and are never accepted as uploads; a moderator checks, and the hub can refuse an archive whose variant hash matches one of the distinct Bungie payloads (hashes computed on a maintainer's machine, not the files). ReachVariantTool's code is GPLv3 and is not used; its CC0 manual is.
Roadmap › Phase 1: local game types (smallest useful step)

No hub change. Each step is useful on its own: blam_megalo::validate and mjolnir megalo check, with the CLI's string limit set to 112 and its tick-rate default to 60 (or its two tick-counted timers moved to Megalo timers). The game type folder. MJOLNIRGameTypes\<id>\ with variant.mglo, layout.json and gametype.json. The lobby builds its list from it and the HUD its scoreboard modes. Team Slayer can then ship as a folder instead of edits in 13 places (KOTH and Oddball need the object types of Phase 5 first), and a tester can try a variant on several PCs by copying one folder. The game type id travels in the lobby message, and the loader reads it instead of GAME_TYPE_SLOTS, which stays as the fallback for older peers. The native size and structure gate before CopyFileA, and the decode read-back in the log.

The manifest type and scanner rules, the WASM validator, gametype_listings and review, the lobbies and matches columns, the launcher's install, live install and mjolnir://gametype/<id> link, the in-game offer to fetch a missing game type, settings through layout.json, and the website reading game types from the listing. Before it ships: the session-parameter serializer look (Safety). Until Phase 3, authors write variants with the typed builder in crates/blam-megalo, or bring files from other tools that pass megalo check.

mjolnir megalo compile, dump printing the same language, import for an author's own Reach variants with name-based remapping, and the compile(dump(x)) == x tests. Editor support (syntax highlighting) can follow.

What makes Bungie-style game types readable in HCE: a native reader of the sim's scores on every machine (fact 9), feeding the HUD instead of incident tallies; a native reader of objects' owner team (fact 10), the generic fix for any game type's team-coloured objects, CTF flags included; the forced-colour trait (Infection, Juggernaut) and script teams under a free-for-all header, which the BlamGameTeam component does not show (fact 16); Megalo widgets, objective text and waypoints, for example mirrored into the HaloScript navpoint list Unreal already draws (sim 0x473960), which has a priority and a label but no icon (INFERRED, untried); rounds: "variant": let the sim play a variant's rounds, which side-swap modes need (fact 19); three to eight teams: the lobby, armour, HUD and the hub's matches team values are red and blue only.
Roadmap › Phase 5: Reach's roles in the runtime

Append motl entries and tags for the objects Bungie's modes use and CU4 lacks: the bomb, the skull, the hill marker, flag stands and capture plates, respawn zones (multiplayer type 16, which CU4's spawn scoring honours, sim 0x307d10), kill and safe volumes (types 25 and 26, sim 0x424150). Each lands in the runtime pack under the append-only rule, and the language gains the names.

mods/MJOLNIRHud draws the HUD for the classic CE maps that MJOLNIRLevelLoader runs under the simulation's Megalo engine. It uses MJOLNIR's own cooked widgets (custom_ui.md): WBP_MJOLNIRKillFeed: the kill feed at the bottom left, the medal callout and the respawn countdown in the middle, and the score bars at the top (see The kill feed below). The score bars sit above the native shield bar: Red/Blue for team modes, or YOU/LEADER for free-for-all, each filling toward the score to win, with the round clock between them. The local team is marked / YOU. Opening the full scoreboard hides the bars until Tab/View is released. WBP_MJOLNIRScoreboard: shown while Tab (or the gamepad's View button) is held. It has the game type and map, the score to win (or the team scores in CTF and Team Slayer), and up to 16 players with score, kills and deaths. Team games have separate Red and Blue sections, with team totals and player counts; players without a reported team appear under Awaiting assignment. Each section is sorted by score. A gold YOU marker identifies the local player in addition to the row highlight. WBP_MJOLNIRChat: match chat, above the kill feed (see Chat below). The console opens on ~ only. MJOLNIRConsoleEnabler takes Tab out of InputSettings.ConsoleKeys, as Halo CE on PC had it.

Scripts/commands.lua. A chat line starting with / is a command: it is never relayed or recorded. Typing / lists the commands you may use under the box; Tab completes the highlighted one, then a player's name, and again for the next match.
