The host runs every command. A client sends MJOLNIR cmd <line> over ServerExecRPC; the host takes the sender from the RPC's controller and answers them alone with a system line. Host commands run only from the host's own box: a client's /kick is refused whatever it says. A client's /suicide needs a seat that is really theirs (index not the host's, and the controller's BlamAbsolutePlayerIndex agreeing): a joiner reads the host's index 0 for a few seconds after joining. A player is named by hub name or in-game name: exact first, then the only one it starts, then the only one it is in. Kick, ban, unban call MJOLNIRLobby's mjolnir_auto kick ban unban through the console. The Lobby takes an exact name before a partial one. Public, private call MJOLNIRLobby's mjolnir_auto public on off, the HOST MENU's MAKE PUBLIC / MAKE PRIVATE. They say nothing themselves: the Lobby writes each listing status to MJOLNIRLobby\chat_notice.txt while a match runs (<unix time>\t<line> a line), and the host's chat shows each line under 30 s old as a system line. Kill and teleport are Blam script, sent through MJOLNIRBlamConsole's mailbox (native\request.txt, ids from 7000000, one line a poll): (unit_kill (player_get <index>)); a teleport is objects_attach then objects_detach a poll later, so the child is left where its parent stands. /suicide was verified on a host on 2026-10-17.

That player_get <n> is the player with absolute index n is proven only for the host's own seat; the two-PC test must check it before /slay or a teleport is trusted. Six suggestions show at a time (the host has ten commands); typing more narrows them.

Scripts/chat.lua. T opens all chat, Y team chat (all chat in free for all), Home all chat. Enter sends, Esc cancels. The first time, the box shows the chat rules instead (chat is recorded, public matches post their chat, keep it civil): I AGREE or Enter opens chat and is remembered in chat_rules.txt beside the mod; NOT NOW or Esc leaves it shut. A new version of the rules asks again. Lines show for nine seconds, then fade; while the box is open the last ten show on a dark panel. A line is at most 160 bytes. Each line shows the sender's hub avatar, round, as the feed and the scoreboard do; MJOLNIRLobby may cache the picture after the line arrives, so a row asks for it again once a second for its first 15 seconds.

Typing does not move the player. The Blam simulation takes its keys from the game viewport, and a key the text box does not use (W, Space, G) bubbles up to it from the focused box. While the box is open the chat sets UI-only input (WidgetBlueprintLibrary:SetInputMode_UIOnlyEx, the box focused, held keys flushed), which makes the viewport ignore input as the Unreal console does while it is open; closing sets game-only input again. Two things that do not stop it (tried 2026-10-17 on a real keyboard): BlamInputProcessorLocalPlayerSubsystem:SetUIActive, which the pause menu sets (the pause menu freezes the player by pausing the game), and emptying GameInput's keyboard readings, which the game never asks for. The game's own chat (WBP_HUD_Main.ChatWidget, IA_OpenChat on Home) is PlayFab party chat, which never connects in games joined by connection string. It draws nothing. The wire. A client sends MJOLNIR say <a t> <text> over ServerExecRPC. The host names the sender from the controller the RPC came in on, never from the text, and sends MJOLNIR chat <a t> <Red Blue -> <index> <name> <text> to every player, or only to the sender's team for team chat. The host allows five lines in six seconds from one sender, and tells a flooder to slow down. The record.

The host keeps every line it relays, with the sender's in-game name, the hub account MJOLNIRLobby resolved for it, team and channel. It writes chat_<match id>.json beside the mod every few seconds, and at the end of the match names it in match_outbox.txt. MJOLNIRLobby sends it to POST /matches/chat. Private matches are recorded too, because a player report cites the match id whether the game was listed or not. A public match's chat shows on its match page on the hub (GET /matches/{id}), as the chat rules tell players. Otherwise only moderators read it, beside each report on /moderation (GET /moderation/match-chat/{host_match_id}).

Every line is a row: a coloured bar at its left edge, then the killer, the weapon, what made the kill special, and the victim. Event lines have a glyph, a name, and what happened. Noble Six [assault rifle] Kat (o) devnull [sniper rifle] (+) Jorge <- gold rim: names you; (o) avatar (>>) devnull Double Kill (+) Emile joined the game

Weapons are the game's own silhouettes, the ones its weapon cradle shows (/Game/UI/Hud/WeaponCradle/Textures/T_UI_*_WeaponIcon, grenades in GrenadeCradle). They are channel-packed masks, so they are drawn through the game's own icon material: a dynamic instance of MI_HUDCradleIcon_FragGrenade with the mask as InputTexture, Empty 0 and Equipped 1, which gives the HUD's cyan. They are mirrored (render scale -1) to face the victim. Scripts/hudicons.lua maps every Blam.DamageReporting.Type.* to one; a type with no silhouette shows one of our glyphs (melee, fall, splatter ...) or, failing that, its name. Glyphs are MJOLNIR's own: white silhouettes drawn by tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py into unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/HudIcons, imported by build_mjolnir_ui.py as /Game/MJOLNIR/UI/Icons/T_MJHud_* and cooked into chunk 984 with the widget (a hidden IconPalette references them). Lua tints them per line: Headshot, Melee, Assassination, Splatter, Stuck, Explosion, Fall, Guardians, Telefrag, Skull, Joined, Left, Kicked, Flag, Medal, Spree, FirstBlood. Modifiers (DamageReportingInfo.Modifier): a headshot or a stuck grenade adds a glyph after the weapon; an assassination replaces the weapon with the knife; a splatter adds the splat after the vehicle.

Avatars: a player with a hub account has their avatar beside their name, round with a faint rim (FeedLeadAvatar<i>, FeedTailAvatar<i>): the same picture the scoreboard shows, which MJOLNIRLobby caches (player_identity.md). Without an account, or before the picture is cached, the slot closes up. Colours: in team games names take their team's colour; in free for all the local player is gold and everyone else near white. A line that names the local player has a gold rim and flashes warmer as it arrives. A team kill says BETRAYAL. Medals: every multiplayer medal the game raises (100 of them, listed in re/medals.md). MJOLNIRLobby's DLL decides which incidents are medals, what each is called, which one hides another (a sniper headshot hides the plain headshot the game sends with it) and the order one kill's medals come in (native/lobby/medals_core.h); Scripts/medals.lua hands it each incident and takes the settled awards once a drain, after the kill lines that earned them. Multi-kills, sprees, weapon sprees, objective medals and first_blood are feed lines for everyone. Headshots, melee kills, revenge and the other "how" medals come up only in the middle of the earner's own screen, so the feed is not one line per kill again. The local player's own come up with their glyph, the best three of one burst.

On a fireteam client they come from the host: the host relays each settled medal after its drain's kill lines (see On fireteam clients), and MJOLNIRLevelLoader's sound relay carries the ones that have a sound. Without the DLL's medal exports (an older MJOLNIRLobby) there are no medals, and the log says why. Text uses the game's own fonts, set from Lua over the cooked Roboto: Normative Pro for names, Oxanium (the menus' face) for numbers and captions.

The widget has a pool of seven rows at one anchor. Scripts/feed.lua gives each line a row and stacks them with render translations, newest at the bottom: a line slides in from the left as it fades in (0.28 s), older lines rise to make room (0.24 s), and each fades out after six seconds. Past six on screen, the oldest leaves at once. Scripts/anim.lua eases the score bars to a new score (the fill is a SizeBox width), pops a number that changes, and brings medals in with a small overshoot. Every pose is a function of the time alone. The animation runs on a hook of BP_MeteoritePlayerController_C:ReceiveTick, the game's per-frame player controller tick (as MJOLNIRFlyCam does), and on the 100 ms poll as well. A host's tick runs once per controller each frame; the hook ignores calls within 4 ms of the last. The hook is never removed, and is registered again after a level change collects the hooked function.

mjolnir_feed_demo (console, in a match) plays a scripted sequence through the HUD's own drawing with made-up names: kills with several weapons, a headshot, a melee, a splatter, a stuck grenade, joins, a kick, medals with their callouts, the score bars moving, and a respawn countdown. Nothing it shows is counted, and the real scores come back after 14 seconds (Scripts/demo.lua).

The simulation's incidents reach the game state's BPC_MeteoriteIncidentHandlerComponent.OnIncident_Event as a BlamIncident: Field Use Name the incident (see below) CausePlayerAbsoluteIndex, EffectPlayerAbsoluteIndex killer and victim; -1 for none CauseObjectActor, EffectObjectActor the bipeds DamageReportingInfo.Modifier EBlamDamageReportingModifier: Headshot, SilentMelee, CollisionDamage, AttachedDamage, FancyAssassination, ArmorAmplified, ArmorMitigated DamageReportingInfo.Type a gameplay tag naming the weapon: Blam.DamageReporting.Type.AssaultRifle, .FragGrenade, … (.Invalid without damage) CustomValue per incident; flag_scored carries the captured flag's team A player index becomes a name through the game state's PlayerArray. Each BlamPlayerState has a BlamPlayerStateComponent.BlamAbsolutePlayerIndex and GetPlayerName(). Use GameplayStatics.GetPlayerController(…, 0) for the local controller: FindAllOf("PlayerController") lists the frontend's leftover controllers first.

Measured with a split-screen second player (CreatePlayer at the main menu), killed by the first. A kill by player 0 of player 1, one tick, in this order: first_blood technician_comm headshot_kill headshot_comm Kill auto_kill auto_comm death lost_lead (1) gained_lead (0) Notes on that sequence: Kill is capitalised, unlike every other incident name. Every incident in it carries both players, the modifier and the damage type. The medal and commendation incidents (*_kill, *_comm, first_blood, the lead changes) are there for a medal display later. A grenade that killed both players raised suicide + death for the thrower and Kill + grenade_kill + grenades_comm + death for the other player. After a death: respawn_tick three times, a second apart, then respawn_final_tick and player_spawn. The cause is the respawning player. The HUD counts the ticks down from 3. Not seen yet: player_joined, player_quit and player_booted_player. They are for networked players; the host quitting raised nothing. The HUD has feed lines ready for them. The *_comm incidents carry a CustomString not read yet.

The host's incident handler gets every player's incidents; a fireteam client's gets few of them (two-PC notes disagree on which: one run saw only the joiner's own spawn, another its respawn ticks). So the host relays what the feed and the tallies need (Scripts/relay.lua): after each drain, one ClientMessage of type MJOLNIR to every remote player's controller, MJOLNIR feed kill,2,0,0,1,SniperRifle;death,2,0,0,0,SniperRifle name,cause,effect,value,modifier,damage type carrying Kill, suicide, death, first_blood, flag_scored, the joins, quits and kicks, and then each medal the drain settled (the DLL has already hidden the ones another stands for). A message carries 16 at most; a longer drain sends more than one. A client feeds them through the same handlers. It takes each incident once: one that also came from its own handler, or from the level loader's sound relay (which carries the medals), within 2.5 s and with the same name, cause and effect, is dropped. Two from the same source are never merged, so a quick respawn killed twice by the same player counts twice. The host ignores its own relay, which its ClientMessage hook also sees.

The host finds its fireteam's controllers once, three seconds into the match (FindAllOf, ~20 ms), then each new one as it is made (NotifyOnNewObject), never with a scan per message. The round clock's share uses the same list. The first send of a match logs relay: the feed to N player(s). A client running an older HUD ignores MJOLNIR feed messages; a client whose host runs an older HUD still gets the loader's medals.

Scores live only in the simulation, so the HUD keeps its own tallies from the incidents, by the rules of the variants MJOLNIR writes (crates/blam-megalo): Slayer: a point per Kill of another player; suicides cost nothing. CTF: a point to the team per flag_scored. The captured flag's team arrives as the incident's value, so the point goes to the other team. Team Slayer presentation: shows kills in the score column and totals the observed kill incidents by the killer's reported team. Points stay with the team that earned them when a player switches or leaves. The Team Slayer variant still needs to be installed to offer this mode. The team reader accepts only Red and Blue from the simulation's BlamGameTeam. It retries a spawn's biped each second because team assignment can arrive after the spawn incident, and reads a stored biped only while that player still controls it (actors are pooled, and a dead player's old one can carry an enemy). Kill/death actors also refresh known teams. No player index or roster order implies a team.

A fireteam client could not trust that component before MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.2. It showed the team in the client's own player record (P+0xad), which past the second player was the slot number: a red player in seat 2 read Green on both joining copies (test copies, 2026-11-07), so client boards put such players under AWAITING ASSIGNMENT, or a seat-1 player the balancer put on red under Blue (#347, #349). Since 0.23.2 the lobby DLL writes the host's team into each player record on a client every tick, so the component agrees with the host; the game's own motion tracker compares these components too (game_modes.md 2.1, #350). The pawn's BlamGameTeam has no GetGameTeamString at all. So in a team game the host, whose reads are right, sends each human seat's team once a second when it changes, and to each player as they arrive (Relay.TEAMS): MJOLNIR teams 0R;1B;2R A client takes the host's team for every seat it names over its own reads, until its match ends. Bot sides already come with the bot roster (MJOLNIR bots ), and a client drops the roster it heard when its match ends: kept, the last match's bots came back in the next match's seats with no side. The HUD still tallies incidents observed during this session; it cannot recover earlier scores for a late join. This presentation does not add a replicated authoritative score reader.

Install the rebuilt UI chunk and the updated Lobby/Hud Lua scripts together; the scoreboard now has 19 visual rows (16 players and three possible team headings). Scripts/scoreboard.lua must accompany the HUD's main.lua. See custom_ui.md for the build and cook commands. The HUD's glyphs are PNGs in unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Art/HudIcons; change one in tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py (--sheet preview.png draws them all over grey and sky blue), re-run it, then build and cook the UI. The Lua modules scoreboard.lua, variant.lua, buildline.lua, matchlog.lua, hubnames.lua, feed.lua, anim.lua, hudicons.lua, relay.lua, hitches.lua, bench.lua, chat.lua, commands.lua and demo.lua ship with main.lua. The HUD also adds the console commands mjolnir_hitches (the hitch log) and mjolnir_bench (performance.md).

tools/tests/test_multiplayer_ui.lua exercises grouping, a full and uneven roster, sorting, CTF captures, Team Slayer kills, delayed assignment, switching teams, leaving, the live score strip (including tied/leaving leaders), holding/releasing the board, and the kill feed: which silhouette or glyph each kill shows, the rim, medals after their kill and the callout, the stacking, the oldest line leaving, the bars, the feed's model on its own, and the relay to fireteam clients (the wire format, taking an incident once, a client's feed and tallies from the host's message alone). Run from the root with Lua 5.4 or Python with lupa: python -c "from lupa import LuaRuntime; LuaRuntime().execute(open('tools/tests/test_multiplayer_ui.lua').read())"

Split screen: the widgets go on the whole viewport, not on each player's half. The scoreboard's own fonts (only the feed, callouts, score bars and chat use the game's). Medal art: medals use the feed's existing glyphs (Medal, Spree, Headshot, Melee, Splatter, Stuck ...). The game ships no medal icons. Objective medals for killing a carrier (flagcarrier_kill and the like) need MJOLNIR's variants to raise them (re/medals.md, "Gaps").

The first round_over ends the match (MJOLNIR's variants have 31 rounds). The scoreboard comes up as the final standings, the results go to last_match.txt, and the host takes the fireteam back to the lobby (multiplayer_postgame.md).

A custom game ends with everyone still together: the final standings in the map, then a post-game screen on the menu where the fireteam votes on the next game, and the host starts it. Nobody leaves the fireteam. Status as of 2026-10-02; updated 2026-10-31.
What the game does on its own, and why we don't use it

A Megalo variant's EndRound (action 21) with rounds left raises round_over and resets the round in place: everyone respawns on the same map with no travel. At the last round it raises game_over. About 15 s later the host goes back to the menu. That return sends every client ClientTravelInternal("/Game/Levels/UI/Frontend/Frontend", TRAVEL_Absolute, bSeamless=false) (two PCs, 2026-10-02). Each client loads its own menu and disconnects, and so leaves the fireteam. This is Unreal's "host returns to the main menu" behaviour, not an error. A seamless travel to the frontend keeps the clients: servertravel /Game/Levels/UI/Frontend/Frontend on the host sends b=2 c=true, and the client arrives in the client lobby, still connected. The host swaps its controller for a BP_FrontendPlayerController and can start the next game from there as usual. Switching straight to the next map from inside a map does not start a game under Megalo (re/megalo_engine.md, "Rounds, the end of a game, and the next map"). That is why the vote happens on the menu. So MJOLNIR's variants give a game 31 rounds (mjolnir megalo write --rounds, default 31), and a match is the first round. The game never reaches game_over, and the host ends the match itself.

In the map (MJOLNIRHud): the first round_over is the end. Every machine freezes its tallies, shows the scoreboard as the final standings (winner, game type, map, "RETURNING TO THE LOBBY"), and writes them to MJOLNIRHud\last_match.txt (Scoreboard.results). The round the game resets behind the standings does not score. With them go each player's medals (a medals line after the player's, by the medal's incident name: headshot_kill=4, multikill_x2=2 ..., most earned first), their score and kills at 48 evenly spaced moments of the match (series, killsat; the HUD samples every five seconds) and how long it ran (clock). The post-game screen's left side has three pages under the winner (mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/postgame.lua): Overview: the top three as cards (avatar, score, kills, deaths, K/D and their five best medals), the local player's medals by name, and the match's bests (most kills, best K/D, most medals, fewest deaths). Scoreboard: every player, as before; a row still opens the report panel. Timeline: the top four players' scores over the match as lines, each ending in its final score, and the kills of every minute as bars with the busiest minute in gold.

A medal is drawn as a disc and a notched rim in its colour with one of the feed's glyphs on it, or a numeral for a multi-kill (x2) or a spree (5). The art is ours (tools/ue/draw_hud_icons.py); the game ships no medal icons. A medal's title, glyph and class come from MJOLNIRLobby's DLL. A UI container from before the pages has no tabs: there the screen shows the scoreboard, with the local player's medals as a line of text under the winner. The host waits 7 s (FINAL_SECONDS), then runs the seamless servertravel to the frontend. A game_over (an older 1-round variant) makes it travel at once, before the game's own return. On the menu (MJOLNIRLobby), the host finds fresh standings (under 180 s old, not shown yet) and pushes WBP_MJOLNIRPostGame. It holds the standings and the vote on four options: the same game again, then other maps in a random order with the same game type where they have it. The vote lasts 20 s. Everyone votes on their own copy of the screen. When it ends, or the host presses START NOW, the most votes win; a tie goes to the earlier option. With no votes, the rotation moves on to the second option. The host starts the winner through the same calls as START GAME, and the fireteam follows into the map. LOBBY, or Back on the host, ends the vote and opens the lobby to pick by hand.

A chosen game that cannot start (its map is not installed, or its world is in no container) does the same, with why on the lobby's status line. Before MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0 the vote stayed on STARTING THE NEXT GAME with LOBBY disabled (two PCs, 2026-11-07). A host who leaves the match by hand gets the lobby, never a vote: the pause menu's SAVE AND EXIT (its YES calls BlamCampaignFlowGameSubsystem.EndCampaign) or LeaveGame from script. Standings written before the leave (a leave while the final standings are up), or within 30 s after it, belong to the match left (Live.quitEnded). In the two-PC run a host's LeaveGame with a joiner in the match opened the vote, which started another match 20 s later with nobody voting. A host alone who leaves mid-match writes no standings and gets no vote either way. The joiners of a host who leaves by hand come along. Between two PCs (2026-11-07, both SAVE AND EXIT's EndCampaign and LeaveGame mid-match), the joiner follows the host's travel into its frontend, has the host's game state within about 2 s, and stays in its fireteam and PlayFab lobby: the host's lobby screen, the joiner's client lobby. Between test copies on one PC it strands them. With every copy on one account (tools/remote/instances.mjs), the joiner lands in a frontend with no host's game state: a black screen until the PlayFab net driver's ConnectionTimeout (120 s;

121.8 s measured), then CONNECTION LOST, which leaves the host's lobby and makes the joiner a fireteam of its own. Likely because the copies' host listens through the ?listen console command, not the game's MemberAdded flow. In a test copy only (MJOLNIR_INSTANCE; Live.STRANDED_WATCH), MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.1 cuts that short (Live.stranded, Live.watchStranded): A client that had players and then sits in the frontend with no game state, or none with players, for 10 s (Live.STRANDED_AFTER; MJOLNIR_STRANDED_AFTER sets it) cuts the connection's ConnectionTimeout to 1 s. That is the game's own CONNECTION LOST and lobby leave, about 20 s after the host left, then "The host left the match." under the game's dialog. The engine's disconnect is the fallback. It reaches the menu but keeps the joiner in the host's lobby. Not the fireteam's leave: CanLeaveFireteam read through the missing game state and crashed. It also crashes on a stale view model from FindAllOf. It stays off on a player's PC, where its one trigger would be a false one: a client in the frontend ahead of a slow host's game state. On every normal travel seen, on two PCs and on copies, the game state came before the next 1.5 s poll. A client's standings are the host's vote's. Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.1 a client in the frontend marks them seen.

Before, a client back on its own menu within 180 s of a match it played (seen on copies, after the exit above) opened a post-game vote of its own on it, and the vote's cancel put the lobby over the reason it was there. Joiners get our lobby instead of the game's CLIENT LOBBY whenever the host is in it: the host's map and game type, with START GAME, CHANGE MAP and GAME TYPE hidden (and, since they were added, PRIVATE / PUBLIC GAME, MAX PLAYERS and GAME SETTINGS). Since mods-v0.20.0, a joiner without the host's map, or with another release of it, sees START GAME as DOWNLOAD MAP or UPDATE MAP (live_map_install.md). A joiner the host starts without (a map it lacks, or another release of it; starting, or the host's kick) leaves the fireteam, and the game itself says only CONNECTION LOST. Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0 the joiner's own lobby then opens the map's download screen with why: which map and game type, that this PC doesn't have it, and that DOWNLOAD gets it without a restart (Live.leaveFor, Live.showNotice). A kick for another reason shows the host's reason. Leaving the fireteam loads the frontend again, so since MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.1 the screen waits for that fresh frontend (or 12 s) before its 3 s delay;

before, a kick from the post-game vote, where the joiner already is on the frontend, could put the screen up in the world being left, and the joiner saw only the main menu (one PC, two copies, 2026-11-07). The vote, the lobby and their lists offer only maps whose world is in a container here: MJOLNIRLevelLoader's mjolnir_worlds_known answers from the same index a start's travel resolves its world through, so a maps.json entry whose containers are gone (a leftover of mjolnir level bake --install-test) is left out and logged, and START GAME on one fails with why. Each machine shows its own standings. They agree because every machine counted the same incidents (multiplayer_hud.md).

Since MJOLNIRLobby 0.19.0 and the chunk-984 UI container cooked with it (which ships in the CE runtime pack, 2026-10-31), the options are a two-by-two grid of tiles, each of them the button you vote with: the map's hub screenshot, and over its foot a band with the game type's icon (the game type picker's, T_MJMode_*), the map, the game type and the votes so far; a gold bar along the bottom edge, the option's share of the votes; pills for PLAY AGAIN (the game just played), DOWNLOAD (a map this PC lacks) and YOUR VOTE, and a blue ring round your vote. Above the tiles: how many have voted, the seconds left on a disc, and a bar that drains. Both turn gold for the last five seconds and grey while a report holds the vote. When the vote is decided, the winner gets a gold ring and NEXT GAME, the others fade, and the header names the next game. Every text in a tile is clipped to it, so a long map name ends in an ellipsis. The screen before wrote each option on one line ("AGAIN / BLOOD GULCH / TEAM SLAYER"), which ran out of the panel. The tallies moved from the footer into the vote's header, and the leading game's screenshot above the options went, since every tile has its own.

The two halves still mix either way (checked in game, 2026-10-31). An older MJOLNIRLobby on the new UI writes its one-line labels into the tiles, cut short with an ellipsis. This MJOLNIRLobby on an older UI container (one with no VoteMode0) draws the old lines.
Messages between the host and its fireteam

There is no replicated class of our own. Two of the engine's PlayerController RPCs carry the messages (mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/net.lua): Direction RPC Why it is safe client to host ServerExecRPC(Msg) Its body is compiled out of Shipping builds. The host's hook reads Msg; self is the sender's controller. host to client ClientMessage(S, Type, MsgLifeTime), Type = "MJOLNIR" The engine prints only the None and Say types. The client's hook reads S. A message is MJOLNIR <verb> <field>...:
Messages between the host and its fireteam

Verb From Fields vote host, every second id, seconds left, options (CODE:mode:again;...), counts, chosen option, the chosen map's campaign-list index, its hub release id and version, held (below) ballot anyone, the host included id, option cancel host id lobby host, while its lobby is up map code, game type, game settings line (host_game_settings.md), campaign-list index, hub release id, version starting host, as it starts a game map code, hub release id, game type mapstate a client getting the host's map map code, stage, percent (live_map_install.md) where a client joining a match under way map code mapindex host, in answer to where map code, campaign-list index kick host why; the map code when it is a map they lack (MJOLNIRLobby 0.23.0), which the client offers with the reason reporting anyone on the post-game screen 1 when the report panel opens, 0 when it closes: the host holds the vote iam a client its identity ticket (player_identity.md) whois a client with no roster yet none ids host its hub account, the roster of in-game name to hub account The vote's ninth field is 1 while the countdown is held for a report. MJOLNIRHud's feed, clock, match, matchid, say, chat and cmd, and MJOLNIRLevelLoader's event, use the same two RPCs (multiplayer_hud.md).
Messages between the host and its fireteam

Hooks on both functions (native, with parameters) ran on CU4 without trouble (2026-10-02). The host never sends a client RPC to a controller with no player or player state: a controller left over from the previous world would run it locally.

mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/main.lua: finishMatch, the final standings, the host's travel. mods/MJOLNIRHud/Scripts/scoreboard.lua: Board.winner, Board.results. mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/main.lua, "After a match": the post-game screen, the vote and the client lobby. mods/MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/net.lua: the messages. unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_mjolnir_ui.py, build_post_game: WBP_MJOLNIRPostGame, in chunk 984 with the other screens. mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/Scripts/main.lua: a travel that names no scenario (the way back to the menu) leaves the Megalo patches alone. Restoring them under a client's running Megalo game froze it mid-travel.

~~Two PCs: the vote end to end (a client's ballot reaching the host, every screen following the outcome) and the client lobby. Steps: two_pc_test.md, Phase 4.~~ Update 2026-10-21: verified on two PCs on 2026-10-09 (e98d2152): the post-game vote chose The Longest, and the host's pick of a map the guest lacked (Hang 'em High) went the same way; each was downloaded in game and played by both PCs. A client that joins during the vote sees it from the next broadcast; one that joins mid-match is not handled yet. Update 2026-10-21: since mods-v0.12.0 (PR #130) a client can join a public match under way; a private game still refuses a join mid-match. The vote's tiles (2026-10-31) were checked on one PC, as the host only. A fireteam client's view (its clock runs on from the host's last message), the DOWNLOAD pill for a map the client lacks, and the grey clock while a report holds the vote still need two_pc_test.md, Phase 4.
