tools/level/merge_ce_scene.py puts everything static into the BSP's glTF. Scenery: every scenery placement's model goes in at its CE position and rotation. CE's rotation (yaw, pitch, roll) is (Rz(-yaw) Ry(pitch) Rx(-roll))^-1: yaw about z, then pitch and roll about the world's y and x axes, the Halo Asset Blender Development Toolset's order. The collision merge, the lens flares and the sound emitters use the same order. Until 2026-10-08 they pitched and rolled in the object's own frame, so a placement with yaw and a tilt leaned the wrong way: Ice Fields' beacons stood on one edge. Over the 19 maps' tilted scenery, the toolset's order sits a placement's base flatter on the BSP in 58 of the 73 placements where the two differ. Beacons are seated (tools/level/ce_seat.py). CE leaves some beacons rocking on one edge of their base: upright on a slope, or tilted one way on ground that falls two ways. A beacon whose base spans more than 0.1 m over the BSP is turned onto the plane fitted to the ground under its base, keeping its heading, and set 0.03 m above it, as CE's well-placed ones are. The scene and collision merges and the lens flares all seat from the same placement. On Ice Fields 8 of 51 beacons move. Flag bases, which CE puts 0.011 wu (3.4 cm) over the floor on every map, are all set down to 5 mm. Scenery is lit as CE lights objects.
What the command does › The terrain, scenery and sky (step 3)

An object has no lightmap of its own: CE samples the ground under its bounding sphere's centre and four points 0.7071 of its radius out, averages the lightmap colour L, the incident direction and the floor's base colour, and lights the object with an ambient of 0.4 L + 0.03, a light of colour L from the incident direction, and a bounce of the floor colour (times L's brightness) off the ground, which lights the faces that look down. The merge writes each placement's brightest lighting as one texel of object_lighting.png (materials <shader>__lmobj) and gives each vertex an incident direction whose dot with its normal is that vertex's share, so the environment master's bumped-lightmap term (full weight) shades it. Without it, Longest's dark steel barricades drew as flat black shapes. The page has eight columns of the same blocks: the light, CE's reflection tint for the object (clamp(3D + 0.5) × clamp(2L + 0.25), times clamp(1.5 × brightness + 0.25)), then the object's change colours A–D. A change colour comes from the tag's permutations as CE picks it: the weights are running cut-offs against a value drawn from the placement's position, and the colour is a blend between the permutation's bounds. The draw is our own hash, so the mix of colours matches CE but a given crate's colour may not. Machines: placed like scenery, in their rest pose.
What the command does › The terrain, scenery and sky (step 3)

A part a machine's device position animation moves (Infinity's beam emitters: the beam rises 1,089 wu out of the base and grows from half size to full) draws with a material of its own on a device variant of its master (M_CE_Transparent…Device), which moves it as a World Position Offset: the node's offset and scale between the animation's first and last frames, about the node's origin, by the device position. A gear runs its position from 0 to 1 over its position transition time and starts again; any other machine (doors, platforms) is drawn at the position it is placed at, because the simulation moves it and Unreal never hears of it. A part that turns, whose parent node moves, or whose frames leave the line between the first and last stays still, as do opaque parts (no opaque device master yet). The mesh's bounds scale (bounds_scale in the spec) keeps it drawn wherever the part goes. halo2ue stages the machine's device and machine fields, its placement's device flags and the animation's frames in placement.json (device). Sky: the sky model (dome, ring, clouds, horizon) goes in with its origin, the viewer, at the map's centre. It is scaled so its nearest layer is 3 km away (the ring ends up about 46 km out).
What the command does › The terrain, scenery and sky (step 3)

CE draws the sky around the camera, and so do the masters: a sky section moves its vertices with the camera (SkyFollow, World Position Offset SKY_WPO_CODE), the CE origin onto the eye, from where it lies relative to the sky mesh's actor (SkyOrigin, cm; merge_ce_scene.py writes it to scene_sky.origin.json). Left fixed, the sky was seen from wherever the player stood. The map's centre is its BSP's box centre, 525 m under Gephyrophobia's bridge, in its chasm, so the ring stood a few degrees off where CE draws it (2026-10-09). The scene becomes meshes of the map's own: each is a shipped basic shape's mesh rewritten in the game's own serialisation (ue_mesh_write.md) and renamed to a package under the map's root, /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE> (build_terrain_meshes.py). Each is normalised into its donor's bounds, and MJOLNIRLevelLoader spawns it at the position and scale that undo the normalisation. Mesh Donor Package Holds Terrain /Engine/BasicShapes/Cylinder SM_<CODE>_Terrain terrain and scenery Translucent /Engine/BasicShapes/Cone SM_<CODE>_Translucent lights, teleporter fields and the other transparent sections Sky /Engine/BasicShapes/Sphere SM_<CODE>_Sky the sky: kilometres across, it cost the transparent pieces their precision when they shared a mesh Water /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube SM_<CODE>_Water CE water, where the map has it (since 2026-10-10)
What the command does › The terrain, scenery and sky (step 3)

package_add puts a map's meshes in one container, pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMESH-<CODE>_P, so maps install side by side. Only the CE_COOK=0 fallback overrides the shipped cylinder itself (pakchunk989-MJOLNIRMESH); a cooked install removes such overrides of the cylinder and cone (989, and 987 MJOLNIRMESHT) left by older conversions. A rewritten mesh enters Unreal's translucency pass only through its single donor slot (re/fork_renderer.md), so the transparent mesh's slot 0 is its first section. Each mesh carries: one section per glTF material, i.e. per (CE shader, lightmap page); the CE lightmap UVs as a second UV channel (--lightmap-uvs); CE's bump tangents; the incident radiosity vector, in each vertex's tangent frame, as the vertex colour: the unit direction in rgb, and in alpha its length, which weights the bumped-lightmap term. CE's bitmaps import with their own mip chains (DDS). CE's detail maps fade their smaller levels to neutral grey, which is what keeps detail tiling from showing at a distance; a regenerated chain would not.

The terrain draws with real materials that reproduce CE's shaders. How they're built and shipped. The Unreal project in unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials (UE 5.5) builds and cooks them: tools/level/ce_material_spec.py lists every bitmap a surface samples, lightmap pages and cube maps included, and one material per mesh section with the CE shader's fields as parameters. Scripts/build_ce_materials.py builds the master materials. Scripts/build_ce_level.py imports the level's bitmaps. tools/ue/cook.ps1 cooks them. The masters go into pakchunk988-MJOLNIRMAT, which ships in the CE runtime pack (tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh). The map's own bitmaps, under /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>, cook into a chunk of their own (ce_material_spec.py cook_chunk), which the converter copies out as pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>_P. At load, MJOLNIRLevelLoader makes a dynamic instance of a master per mesh slot and sets that slot's textures and parameters. Cooked material instances are not used: the game crashes loading one. What it took to make a stock-cooked material draw in the fork. See re/fork_renderer.md: the fork's uniform buffer layouts; its 44-float4 GPU-scene primitive stride; r.CompileShadersForDevelopment=0. The project's MjolnirForkLayouts plugin recreates the first two before anything compiles. The shading. It is CE's fixed-function math, done in the bitmaps' own gamma space as the hardware did.

Pass What the material does Texture Base map, then the primary/secondary detail blend: by the base map's alpha for blended shaders, by the secondary map's alpha for normal ones. Then the micro detail. Each with its function: 0 2·B·D, 1 B·D, 2 B + 2D − 1. Each step clamped. Lightmap lightmap × material colour × mix(1, N·L, incident weight). N is the bump normal, L the baked incident direction. Plus self-illumination: primary, secondary and plasma channels, each animated between its off and on colour by CE's periodic functions. Frame lightmap pass × texture pass, no 2× Specular lightmap Shaders with the "lightmap" specular flag. mix(parallel, perpendicular colour, N·E) × brightness × lightmap luminance × (R·L)⁸; ³² for "extra shiny", ×2 for "overbright". Reflection The cube map, in D3D face order, sampled along the eye vector reflected about the bump normal (the vertex normal for a flat cube map). mix(c⁸, c, tint) × brightness, where tint and brightness go from their parallel to their perpendicular values by the squared view term. Added, masked by bump alpha × the texture pass's specular mask. Alpha test On the bump map's alpha: > 0x7F passes. Fog The sky's outdoor atmospheric fog, or, where no cluster draws a sky, sky 0's indoor fog (Chill Out, 2026-10-13): max density × saturate((depth − start) / (opaque − start)) towards its colour.

Planar fog Below a BSP fog plane (Damnation's shaft, Gephyrophobia's chasm, the water of Battle Creek, Chill Out and Death Island), as MCC's environment fog shaders: x = depth under the plane / opaque depth, y = distance from the eye / opaque distance, A = (1 − min((1−x)² + (1−y)², 1))², B = (1 − (1−y)²)², Pf = (eye density × (B − A) + A) × max density, the eye density being the eye's own depth under the plane / opaque depth. Everything under the plane's height is fogged, not just what lies under the plane's polygon: CE fogs every cluster of the fog region, which reaches past the polygon (MCC fogs all of Chill Out's lower floor; clipping to the polygon's footprint drew a hard-edged slab there, 2026-10-09). The surface's colour goes to the fog's by Pf, the share Unreal's lights draw included; transparents fade by 1 − Pf. tools/level/ce_fog.py reads the planes and fog tags from the map (halo2ue does not stage them) into fog.json; ce_material_spec.py puts the first plane on every environment and transparent material (PlanarFogPlane, PlanarFogColor, PlanarFogParams). Players, vehicles and weapons, drawn with the game's own materials, are not fogged. Boarding Action's red fog has no plane and is not drawn.

Corners and sun Not CE's: lightmap_bake (crates/ue-texture) traces the merged scene for each lightmap page, at up to 16 times its size (2,048 at most), into a texture of its own (<lightmap>_bake, BC1 with mips). Red is ambient occlusion within 1 m, divided by a knee of 0.85 (--ao-knee) and raised to 1.3 (--ao-curve), so the mild folds between a cliff's facets read as open while a wall's foot keeps its darkness: as traced, every fold took a dark line and the cliffs showed their triangles (Blood Gulch, 2026-10-05). --ao-smooth (world-space smoothing) is off by default; at 1 m it washed out the wall-floor corners and drew dashes along them. The masters read it through a 3 x 3 tent a texel apart. Blue is the sky's visibility: the share of --sky-rays rays that leave the level, smoothed over --sky-fine (0.5 m) of surface. CE's shade is brighter the less sky a surface sees (Blood Gulch: a median of 0.18 open to the sky, 0.53 enclosed, against a shadow level of 0.19, 2026-10-06), so on a level without the solver's SunShare the masters scale the lightmap's shadow level by it, from 1 where the surface is open to the sky up to 2.8 where it is enclosed; that tells a coarse lightmap's sun leak from lamp light. mjolnir_terrain_debug sky (layer 3) shows it.

A bake the loader imports at runtime (mjolnir_terrain_shadows lightmap) goes through M_CE_LinearCopy: ImportFileAsTexture2D is always sRGB, and drawn as it was every runtime bake and sun mask arrived sRGB-decoded (128 as 55), too dark. The lightmap is multiplied by red ^ BakeAO (1.4: Blood Gulch was approved at 2.5, found a little dark across the maps at 2.0, and with the knee and curve chosen at 1.4). Green is where CE's sun reaches: the share of the colour drawn as Unreal sun light (so a player or vehicle shadows the ground) is kept to it, and taken down only as far as the lightmap's shadow level (environment.sun.lightmap_sun, which gen_ce_level.py measures on sun-facing surfaces: the lower quartile of the lightmap's luminance where the bake has shadow, since lamp-lit interiors count as shadow too, and the median where it has sun). A shadow therefore never reaches through a roof onto ground CE had in shade, and a baked shadow is not darkened twice. Object shaders (shader_model: Covenant crates, rocks, trees, vehicles) use the same master with ModelShader on, for the terms that differ:

the multipurpose map's masks, in the PC order: red auxiliary, green self-illumination, blue reflection, alpha change colour; the detail map applies where the detail mask says (none, or one of those four masks, plain or inverted); the object's change colour (from the object lighting page) tints its light where the change-colour mask is set; this is where Covenant crates get their white, teal, red or purple panels; the reflection is the cube map's colour as it is, times the tint and brightness between parallel and perpendicular, masked by the reflection mask, faded between the falloff and cutoff distances, and scaled by the object's reflection tint; "detail after reflection" (flag bit 0) applies the detail function to the lit, reflected colour instead of the base map; self-illumination animates between its lower and upper colour, masked by green. Transparent chicago shaders (lights, the teleporter field) work like this:

up to four maps, each with its own UV scale, offset, rotation and scrolling animation; each stage folds the next map in with its colour and alpha functions (current, next, multiply, double multiply, add, add-signed, subtract, blend by alpha); the result is drawn with the shader's framebuffer blend: alpha blend, add, or multiply. Subtract, min and max have no Unreal blend mode and fall back to alpha blending; a shader with no bitmap on any stage (Danger Canyon's and Ice Fields' light shaders reference none) draws nothing, as in CE: it is added at a zero tint. Drawn with the master's default white map, it was a solid white box; a shader with CE's two-sided flag (bit 2: the Covenant shields, the teleporter shields and cones, the powerups) takes a two-sided master, M_CE_Transparent{Add,Alpha,Mul}TwoSided, since an instance cannot turn two-sided on. With one-sided masters the shields drew from one side only (playtest, 2026-10-03). halo2ue's double_sided is true for every transparent shader, so only the flag decides.

MCC's generic shaders. The Xbox drew many of these with shader_transparent_generic, up to seven register-combiner stages over four maps. The PC port could not, so a classic Custom Edition map carries Gearbox's chicago stand-in: Death Island's teleporter field is two grey dust maps tiled once, a soft green blob, where MCC draws the Xbox's wavy energy. MCC's Halo CE editing kit (HCEEK) ships the original tags, so where it has a shader_transparent_generic at a chicago shader's tag path, ce_material_spec.py draws that instead (MCC_GENERIC=0 turns it off; MCC_TAGS points elsewhere than the Steam install):

tools/level/mcc_tags.py reads the big-endian source tags (the generic shader and its bitmaps) and writes each bitmap as mcc_<path>.png and .dds beside the map's own, with the tag's own mip chain; each map keeps a chicago map's transform and animation fields; the stages go to the same transparent masters as parameters (GenericStages, GenCI/GenAI/GenCO/GenAO/GenK* per stage), where GENERIC_CODE runs them as MCC's transparent_generic_shader.psh does: four colour and four alpha inputs through their input mappings, A·B and C·D (or dot products), their sum or mux, the output mapping, and the three results written to the registers the stage names; the result is r0; a shader whose first map is a cube map, or whose bitmap cannot be exported, stays the chicago one. So does one with a stage whose colour 0 follows one of the object's functions (source A-D out: the field generator's shield, the power-ups, the holo controls, the door blinker): the material cannot read the object's live state, and drawn without it the shield came out white or red where Halo PC's chicago shader and MCC both draw it purple. So does one with no stages (73 of the 97 our maps use: most skies and lights), which MCC's combiner shader would draw black; MCC must draw those another way, still to be checked.

Teleporter fields, the turret's beam tendril, the beacons, the light volumes, the waves and the night sky's ring and planet take MCC's shaders this way (15 of the 24 shaders with stages over the 19 maps). Update 2026-10-21: since 2026-10-04, M_CE_Water follows the water tag field by field (halo2ue's tag): up to four ripple layers (contribution, angle, velocity, offset, repeats, bitmap), faded towards flat by mip level, and the bumped cube reflection as mix(c⁸, c, tint), the tint set by how squarely the camera looks down on the water. The third flag (atmospheric fog) fogs it. The second flag is drawn, as a multiply pass of its own (M_CE_WaterBackground) on a copy of the surface that merge_ce_scene.py puts first, and sky water replaces the frame (M_CE_WaterSky, opaque). Since 2026-10-10 the water is a mesh of its own (SM_<CODE>_Water), which environment.water or mjolnir_water ocean can draw as rolling water (M_CE_Ocean); CE's style is the default, but gen_ce_level.py asks for the ocean on Death Island and Yoyorast Island (OCEAN_MAPS). The list below is the first version. Water (shader_transparent_water: Death Island, Battle Creek, Gephyrophobia, Damnation) is drawn by M_CE_Water, in the transparent mesh:

the reflection cube map, sampled along the view reflected about a normal bent by two panning layers of the ripple map (the shader's ripple angle, velocity and scale); tinted and faded by the view angle, from the perpendicular brightness and tint (looking straight down) to the parallel ones (grazing), on a steep curve (FresnelPower 3); added over what is under the water, scaled by the brightness and, when the shader's first water flag is set, by the base map's alpha: the base map is a mask, never a colour (drawn as one, the sea was an opaque white sheet, 2026-10-02). Brightness is not opacity: Battle Creek's water is 1.0 at every angle and its creek bed still shows. The second flag (the base map's colour tints the background) has no additive form and is not drawn. halo2ue's water parser read every field after the base map at the wrong offset (its tag lookup moves the reader), so brightness, tint, ripples and the reflection map all came out zero; it reads them at their fixed offsets now. Colour reaching the screen unchanged. Each material: decodes its result to linear; divides out the camera's exposure (EyeAdaptationInverse); hands the tonemapper CE's own colour. The level's post-process volume (environment.post) turns the filmic curve, gamut expansion and blue correction off, so the tonemapper leaves it as it is. Where the data comes from. halo2ue-export stages:

the lightmap vertices: in a cache file they follow the rendered vertices in the same blob; cube maps as six faces, plus the specular colours, the three self-illumination channels, every chicago stage and the sky's fog; each vehicle's team and per-game-type spawn flags, from which a match picks CE's vehicle sets (see "Vehicle sets"). Without the Unreal editor (CE_COOK=0) the converter falls back to tools/level/ce_textures.py: one composited texture per shader on a shipped material, with no lightmaps.
What the command does › Ambient sound (step 3)

The game ships none of CE's ambience as Blam sound tags. Its 163 looping sounds are material, vehicle and weapon loops, and the remake's ambience lives in its own Unreal levels. CE's sounds therefore come from CE's files and play through Unreal's own audio engine, which the game runs beside its own. Extract. tools/level/ce_sounds.py <map> <sounds.map> <staging> <out> reads a Custom Edition map (cache version 609). Its sound tags are indexed: sounds.map holds each whole tag as <path> and its samples as <path>__permutations; the docstring has the layouts. The script extracts: the sound scenery (halo2ue's sound_scenery placements), such as the teleporter hum; the looping sounds placed objects carry as attachments (halo2ue's sounds on an entry), each an emitter at its marker: the Covenant shield generator's and uplink's hum, the teleporters' loop, Wizard's klaxons, the beam emitters. A marker on a machine's moving part moves with it (marker_motion, the part's device motion): Infinity's beam loop hangs on the beam, which rises 1089 wu every 15 s, so CE plays it for about a second as the beam fires. Held at the marker's rest it played all the time (2026-10-08). The loader moves it on the world's clock and keeps it PlayWhenSilent: with Restart it did not come back in time; the background sound, the looping sounds the BSP block depends on; each looping sound's tracks and detail sounds.
What the command does › Ambient sound (step 3)

Xbox ADPCM is decoded to WAV and Ogg is kept as is. A loop's permutations are joined into one _loop file, because CE plays them back to back. Import. unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_ce_sounds.py imports them under /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/Sounds, which cooks with the map's own chunk (pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>_P). Loops are marked looping, and the compression is ADPCM: the default, Bink, needs a decoder the game may not ship. Play. gen_ce_level.py --sounds writes environment.sounds, and MJOLNIRLevelLoader plays it: background loops in 2D, map-wide; emitters in 3D at the CE positions, falling off linearly over CE's distance bounds. Volume. The game's volume sliders set its Wwise buses, which these sounds bypass, so the loader applies the sliders itself. It reads them from the game's settings object (MeteoriteGameUserSettings, through GameUserSettings:GetGameUserSettings()) and plays each sound at its gain times VolumeMaster times one category slider: VolumeSFXAmbient (Ambient Effects) by default, VolumeMusicGameplay (Music) for a sound with "category": "music", and VolumeVODialog (Dialogue) for the event sounds below. gen_ce_level.py marks a sound as music when its CE class is music or cinematic_music. Every half second the loader re-reads the sliders, so a change made from the pause menu applies at once.
What the command does › Ambient sound (step 3)

Detail sounds (random one-shots) are extracted but not yet played. Event sounds. The game engine still has Reach's event list: game_engine_globals holds 510 events, each with a sound and announcer line, and megalogamengine_sounds names 95 mode announcements. But 336 of the 339 sound tags the events name were cut from the build, and 94 of the 95 announcements are empty. The events themselves still fire, and they reach Unreal as BlamIncidents on the game state's BPC_MeteoriteIncidentHandlerComponent (OnIncident_Event, which can be hooked), for example: teleporter_used respawn_tick, respawn_final_tick death, suicide, player_spawn ce_sounds.py --events <sounds.map> <out> extracts every CE announcer line (Ogg Vorbis; Unreal's importer decodes it) and the UI sounds the events need, and writes mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader/events.json (event name to waves). build_ce_sounds.py imports them under /Game/MJOLNIR/Sounds/Events, and the loader plays an event's sound on converted multiplayer levels only. Personal events (teleport, respawn ticks, multikills and sprees, and a health pack's lap_complete) play only for the player they concern: the incident's cause or effect must be the local player's absolute index, read from its BlamPlayerStateComponent (BlamAbsolutePlayerIndex: 0 on the host, the joiner's own slot on a fireteam client; 2026-10-01).
What the command does › Ambient sound (step 3)

The waves are loaded when the level is furnished, and the hook only queues the event; a 100 ms game-thread loop plays it. Loading and playing inside the hook froze the game on the first teleport. No game-start event is raised on a converted map, so the game type's announcement ("Slayer", "King of the Hill" and so on) plays once per match, picked by the variant the menu started. It plays when the player's pawn first exists, because the opening spawn raises no player_spawn (only respawns do), or at the first player_spawn if that comes sooner.
What the command does › The level file (step 4)

Spawn points. Under a multiplayer engine players spawn only at scenery whose multiplayer type is player spawn location; the scenario's player starts are not read. One is placed at every position a CE or Halo 2 start some game type uses (neutral team), hidden unless every game type but CTF uses it (see "Spawn sets" below). Vehicles, weapons, pickups through defs/level/ce-tag-map.json; each CE tag maps to the first equivalent the game has a type for (defs/level/palette-map.json). The bake adds a type the canvas palette lacks: the shotgun and the fuel rod (Reach's flak_cannon) are not in B40's. What has no equivalent is reported as dropped: the flamethrower (none ships). Map variant palette (blam.map_variant). Objects with multiplayer data exist only through the map variant, which is built from the placements whose tags a palette lists. A model variant gets an entry of its own. The bake writes a palette per category with every kind the palette map knows, so Forge can place the whole arsenal (forge.md). Grenades, the overshield and camouflage also need the game variant's map options (grenades, equipment and powerups on map), which megalo write sets. Vehicles: every vehicle the CE scenario places (--game-type all), hidden until a match's vehicle set picks it (see "Vehicle sets" below).
What the command does › The level file (step 4)

The rocket Warthog spawns as the chaingun Warthog (VEHICLE_VARIANTS is empty): as the Warthog's rocket model variant (permutation data.variant name) its turret had no Unreal actor Blueprint, so the gun was invisible and the gunner vanished (playtest, 2026-10-03). Banshees and Scorpions start 0.3 wu above CE's height and every other vehicle 0.05 wu (VEHICLE_LIFT), with the at-rest placement flag cleared so they fall into place: at CE's height on Blood Gulch's roofs the Banshees started inside them and were thrown on their sides. Weapons and equipment start 0.05 wu above CE's height (ITEM_LIFT) with the at-rest flag cleared, and fall into place. CE places items 0.001 wu over the floor, and the bake creates objects at rest (placement flag 0x20), so the part of a weapon below its origin stayed in the floor (playtest, 2026-10-03). Levitating powerups (CE's levitate, on Battle Creek, Hang 'Em High, Rat Race and Timberland) stay at rest where CE put them. Respawn times. Each weapon and pickup respawns after CE's time: its placement's, else its item collection's (halo2ue's collection_spawn_time), else 30 s. Vehicles respawn after 30 s and are given back 30 s after being left away from their spot. A map variant object with spawn time 0 never came back.
What the command does › The level file (step 4)

Every respawn time is spread by 0-10 s per placement (RESPAWN_SPREAD): with flat times, every object the simulation had not placed came back in the same tick, and on Death Island that stall reset the round every ~34 s, putting every player at a spawn point without a death (2026-10-08). Teleporters: a sender at every CE "teleport from" flag and a receiver at every "teleport to" flag. The simulation keeps Reach's multiplayer teleporters, which pair ends by channel. CE numbers a map's channels freely (Gephyrophobia uses 2–7, 13 and 14; Infinity 11–24), so the generator renumbers each map's channels from alpha in CE order, across the scenario's 26 (alpha to zulu), and warns about a channel missing either end. Past zulu the field takes the raw number, which pairs just as well: the simulation compares the channel byte. The first version kept only channels 0–5 and dropped the rest silently, which left Gephyrophobia with half its pads. At most 32 teleporters. The simulation keeps a table of 32 teleporters, filled from the map's sender, receiver and 2-way scenery (HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll 0x1803e7670 on CU4). An end past the 32nd sends nothing, and nothing lands on it. Chiron TL-34 placed 60 ends, so about half its pads did nothing. The generator warns past 32. Two-way pads. CE has no two-way teleporter.
What the command does › The level file (step 4)

A pad that both sends and receives is two channels whose "teleport from" and "teleport to" flags sit on top of each other at both ends. All of Chiron TL-34's pads are like this, as are Gephyrophobia's, Sidewinder's, Boarding Action's and others. Where a channel's "from" flag lands within the sender's boundary of another channel's "to" flag, the reverse holds too, and the facings agree, the generator merges the two channels into one. It places a "teleporter 2way" at each pad, at the "to" flag with its facing. That halves the ends: Chiron's 60 become 30 on 15 channels. Room to land. The simulation lands a player at the receiver's (or 2-way's) origin, but only if a Spartan fits there. It tests the biped's shape (radius 0.175, standing height 0.65, from 0.2 up) against the collision. A receiver that fails is skipped, and a sender with none left raises teleporter_blocked. CE has no such test and puts its "teleport to" flags at the back of their alcoves. Every Chiron TL-34 landing spot had 0.17–0.25 to the wall behind it, and pads landing at 0.166 and 0.182 never sent. The generator moves each landing end forward along its exit facing, up to 0.15, until the Spartan clears CE's collision (the staging export's bsp/collision_N) by 0.25. On Chiron 28 of 30 move, by 0.02–0.09.
What the command does › The level file (step 4)

The two games turn the player differently: CE turns the player to the "teleport to" flag's facing. Reach keeps the facing relative to the sender, whose front faces the player walking in. With CE's flag facings, players had to walk in backwards to exit the right way. So each sender is turned 180° from its CE flag, and walking in head-on exits facing the receiver's direction, as in CE. The post-process volume (environment.post): fixed exposure, no local exposure, no filmic curve. The CE materials then show CE's colours (re/fork_renderer.md). "multiplayer": true, blam.active_bsps, blam.single_bsp, the scenario type set to multiplayer.
What the command does › Capture the Flag

A map whose CE scenario has a CTF flag for each team offers CTF in the multiplayer menu ("modes": ["slayer", "ctf"]). No CTF ships in this build: there is no variant, no flag object and no flag mesh, so each piece is ours.
What the command does › Capture the Flag

The rules are a Megalo variant, variants/ctf.mglo (mjolnir megalo write --mode ctf, crates/blam-megalo/src/ctf.rs). The script makes each team's flag on its stand (red's object type on a stand owned by red, blue's on blue's), scores a capture when the carrier stands in their own stand's boundary while their own flag is home, returns a dropped flag when its own team touches it or after 30 s, and ends the round at 3 captures. The reset, like the health pack's respawn, is counted in ticks at the simulation's 60 a second (--tick-rate; at the old default of 30 both lasted half as long). The flag incidents (flag_grabbed 110, flag_dropped 112, flag_scored 116, flag_reset 118, flag_recovered 119) carry the flag's team as their value (Unreal's CustomValue), so the loader plays CE's team lines ("Red team has the flag", "Blue team score", "Red team flag returned"). The action and condition encodings match ReachVariantTool's opcode list; they are checked against the CU4 decoder in re/megalo_variant_format.md. Teams. A spawn point CTF uses is labelled ctf_spawn_red or ctf_spawn_blue by its CE start's team, one every other game type uses ctf_spawn_none, all placed neutral. The variant gives the red and blue spawn points their teams, and parks the rest on a team no player is on.
What the command does › Capture the Flag

The CTF-only ones are hidden, so only CTF and Assault, whose variants filter on these labels, place them (see "Spawn sets"). It waits 2 s before the first spawn (the loadout camera time), so the first tick has set the teams up; a spawn on tick 0 used them neutral. The flags (tools/level/build_ctf_flag.sh) are two weapons cloned from the assault bomb, which ships whole and is carried the same way: objects\weapons\multiplayer\flag\flag for red and flag_blue for blue, entries 18 and 20 of the multiplayer object type list, which the script needs before it can create them. They differ only in their default model variant, default and blue, both variants of the bomb's model. The bomb binds no Unreal actor, so the flags borrow the oddball's BP_SkullActor. MJOLNIRLevelLoader hides the skull, removes its fire effect and whispering audio, and attaches CE's own flag mesh in its team's colours. The team is the actor's own: the simulation computes a flag's team colour but never hands it to Unreal, while an object's model variant does reach the actor (GetVariantName() on its mesh synchronization component) on every machine, because a tag's default comes with the tag (game_modes.md, 2.2). The mesh is exported by halo2ue and rewritten into /Game/MJOLNIR/CTF/SM_CE_Flag; its textures come from tools/level/ce_flag_textures.py.
What the command does › Capture the Flag

The stand needs no mesh: CE's own flag base scenery sits at each flag and comes in with the map. Release order. The variant names every object type it creates, and the simulation wipes a variant naming one the installed list lacks: no rules at all, not a colour bug. The CE runtime pack with pakchunk990-MJOLNIRFLAGB_P and the list's entry 20 ships before, or with, the mods release whose ctf.mglo creates type 20. The lobby offers CTF only when that container is installed, and mjolnir megalo write --mode ctf --single-flag writes the one-type script (entry 18 for both teams) for a pack without it. Armour colours. In a team game the loader puts every Spartan in the classic Mk V armour, whatever the player picked: only its material takes a colour. The others (Chief's default, MkIV, Blamite, Lone Wolf, the coatings) bake theirs into textures, so a Chief-armoured player stayed olive on Blue. Each mesh component's class (BPC_SkeletalMesh_C, BPC_FP_SkeletalMesh_C, ...) names the Mk V mesh it gets. The loader then gives each Spartan's armour, and the local player's first-person arms, legs and shadow, a dynamic instance with Armor Color set to red or blue. The parameter is read at global association with index 0: the plain setter writes index -1, which this layered material never reads, so it must be set by info.
What the command does › Capture the Flag
A respawn reuses the actor and puts the stock armour back, so the loader re-tints after every spawn.
What the command does › Vehicle sets

CE decides a map's vehicles per game type. Each scenario vehicle has a team index (0 red, 1 blue) and spawn flags: bits 0x1-0x8 put it in Slayer's, CTF's, King's and Oddball's default set, bits 0x100-0x800 allow it when a game variant uses custom vehicle settings. A game variant picks a set per team: DEFAULT, NONE, one type (WARTHOGS, GHOSTS, SCORPIONS, ROCKET WARTHOGS, BANSHEES, GUN TURRETS), or CUSTOM (0-4 of each type). Placing every game type's vehicles at once put 46 on Death Island, more than the simulation keeps, and it reset the round every ~34 s (2026-10-08). Reach does the same with Megalo labels:
What the command does › Vehicle sets

gen_ce_level.py places every vehicle with the spawn flag "hide unless megalo required" (0x4), its CE team as the owner team (defender/attacker), and a label ce_<type>_<rank>. The type is CE's set category (a rocket Warthog stays rwarthog). Within a team, a type's vehicles rank by how many game types they are default in, and the k-th of each team share the label. The level's vehicle_sets lists every vehicle's type, team, label and CE's default and allowed game types. The simulation places a hidden object only if the game variant has an object filter on its label; a filter with a team constraint places only that team's (both seen on Death Island, 2026-10-08). The variant holds 16 filters: 17 put every object out of play and lost the GPU device, and so did a filter minimum count above 0. Hence the shared labels: the stock maps' sets are symmetric, and a default set needs at most 9 filters. mjolnir megalo write --vehicle-label-pool writes every label (ce_<type>_1..10) into the variant's string table and a <mode>.layout.json beside it: the bit the filters start at (they end the stream), the variant's own filters, and each label's string index.
What the command does › Vehicle sets

When a match starts, MJOLNIRLevelLoader (vehicle_sets.lua) reads the host's vehicle settings from the settings line (vehicles.<team>, vehicles.<team>.<type>), picks each team's labels, and appends one filter per label: none of a team constraint if both teams take it, else the team's. A custom count takes the lowest ranks CE allows in the game type; filters past 16 are left out, highest ranks first, and logged. Every machine computes the same filters from the same line and level. The host sets them on the RED VEHICLES and BLUE VEHICLES pages of GAME SETTINGS (MJOLNIRLobby/Scripts/settings.lua). A FORGE game has no filters: the sandbox engine builds its own variant. Its map variant still lists the vehicles, with bit 0x20 of an entry's flags as the hide flag (0x2c against a palette placement's 0x0c), and the palette's placed counts include them. So the loader writes the labels a Slayer game would place to forge_vehicles.txt, cut to the room Slayer's variant has, and MJOLNIRForge's DLL clears the bit on those entries before the objects are made: at new-map, on F2 and on F6, for the map's own layout or a saved one. A save sets it again in what it writes, so a host's vehicle sets still decide in a match. Measured in FORGE: Yoyorast shows all 16, Coldsnap 21 of its 47 default vehicles, Death Island 16, with no round reset in 75 s.
What the command does › Vehicle sets

A layout saved there and hosted as Slayer with both sets on NONE placed no vehicles. Not tested with a client joining: a client changes nothing, and its objects are the host's. Filters come after the variant's own, so a map with many labels can run out. CTF and Assault have 6 of their own, Race 2. A map's plan can give vehicles that always go together one label (ce_place_vehicles.py): Yoyorast's eleven hogs and Mongooses share six, so every game type places its whole set, where CTF used to leave out three labels and Race one. add_objectives.py --vehicle-plan applies a plan to a published pack. A shared label moves as one, so a custom set's count takes both. Coldsnap's set is far past any variant's room; the cut keeps it under what the simulation holds. Death Island places Banshees and Warthogs when the round begins, and its Ghosts, Scorpions and Shades only when their respawn time (30-40 s) runs out, with or without labels; Infinity places everything at once. Not yet explained.
What the command does › Spawn sets

CE and Halo 2 decide a map's spawns per game type too (#360). Each player start lists up to four game types: CTF, Slayer, Oddball, King, Race, All games, All except CTF, All except CTF and Race, and on Halo 2 also Headhunter, Juggernaut and Territories. Before spawn sets, a converted map placed every start Slayer or CTF used, and every game type but CTF spawned at all of them: Slayer on Blood Gulch used the 38 CTF base starts beside its own 17, and the Oddball-, King- and Race-only starts were never placed. The vehicle sets' mechanism does it, with no script change:
What the command does › Spawn sets

gen_ce_level.py (spawn_plan) turns each start's game types into families: ctf, slayer, oddball, king, race, and on Halo 2 maps juggernaut. Starts at one position are one spawn point, serving every family any of them lists. A spawn point every family but CTF uses is placed as before, visible: ctf_spawn_red/blue if CTF uses it too, else ctf_spawn_none. A CTF-only spawn point is hidden ("hide unless megalo required") under ctf_spawn_red/blue. The CTF and Assault variants already filter on those labels (filters 2-4), so they place it and no other game type does. A spawn point some, not all, of the other families use is hidden under a label from a pool, spawn_set_0..spawn_set_15, one per distinct set of families. The level's spawn_sets lists each label's families. A start CTF uses as well becomes two spawn points at one spot, one of each kind. A family no start serves spawns with Slayer. mjolnir megalo write --vehicle-label-pool also writes the 16 pool labels into every variant's string table and layout.json (86 labels, string index 91 at most, of 127). Launcher 0.23.0's validator accepts the variants, so no launcher release has to come first. When a match starts, MJOLNIRLevelLoader (vehicle_sets.lua, spawnFilters) adds one filter per spawn set the game type's family is in, before the vehicle filters, so a full variant drops vehicles, not spawns.
What the command does › Spawn sets

Families: Slayer and Team Slayer slayer; CTF and Assault ctf (no filters: the standing ones do it); King, Crazy King and Team King king; Oddball, Team Oddball, Stalker and Reverse Tag oddball; Race, Team Race, Rally and Team Rally race; Juggernaut juggernaut on Halo 2 maps and oddball on CE's (CE's Juggernaut is an Oddball ball type). FORGE shows Slayer's (forge_vehicles.txt, first). Measured on Blood Gulch in test copies (2026-11-08), its shipped spawn points relabelled in place: Team Slayer placed 17 spawn points, all CE's Slayer starts, and every first spawn and respawn was on one of them; CTF placed the 38 base starts, owned 17 red and 21 blue, and each player respawned in their own base. A joining copy places no spawn points in either: the host decides spawns. FORGE was not tried. A rebuilt map needs a loader that adds the filters: on an older loader a game type whose spawns are all in hidden sets has none (Slayer on Blood Gulch). So the mods release comes first, then the maps. Halo 2's starts carry a spawn type per game type (0 both, 1 initial spawn only, 2 respawn only), staged as spawn_types and not used yet: the initial spawn flag the simulation needs for a first spawn is the scenery tag's (player_spawn), not the placement's, so a respawn-only start would need a second spawn tag in the runtime pack.
What the command does › Health packs

This game ships no health pack (no object, no Unreal asset, none placed in the campaign), and its health never recharges, as CE's did not. So every variant the loader ships carries CE's health packs as Megalo script (crates/blam-megalo/src/powerups.rs, on by default in mjolnir megalo write):
What the command does › Health packs

Each CE health pack becomes a spot, invisible scenery labelled ce_health_pack (objects\multi\powerups\health_pack_spot), owned by the eighth team: neutral scenery with a multiplayer block takes respawns. Each tick, a spot with no pack whose countdown has run out creates one: the equipment objects\multi\powerups\health_pack, multiplayer object type list entry 19, which nobody can pick up. A living player whose biped comes within reach of the pack (8 feet, origin to origin, by the Get Distance action) and whose health is under 100% is healed to full (Modify Object Health); the pack goes, and comes back after 30 s. Shields are left alone. The pickup raises Race's lap_complete incident, and the loader plays CE's pickup_health to that player. recharge_health would be the natural incident, but the simulation never hands it to Unreal. The pack is cloned from the battle rifle ammo pickup (no CE map places battle rifle ammo), and the loader puts CE's health pack mesh (/Game/MJOLNIR/CE/Powerups/SM_CE_HealthPack) on that actor in place of its own. The pack is made 0.1 wu above its spot and falls, so the crate can come to rest tipped on its side. The mesh keeps the world's up and the crate's heading, with its base (CE's model origin) at the crate's lowest corner, which is on the ground, and is seated again 2 s and 5 s after the pack appears.
What the command does › Health packs
The actions are Reach's (54/55 get shields/health, 64/65 modify, 66 get distance), at the same numbers in CU4's decoder.

tools/level/ce_objectives.py places CE's HillFlag polygons and OddballSpawn flags as labelled markers and adds koth and oddball to the map's modes when it has them. King and Oddball ship since mods 0.44.0; game_modes.md, section 3.4, has the rules and the tests.

Update 2026-10-21: a converted map is hosted from the main menu's MULTIPLAYER → HOST GAME (MJOLNIRLobby), which starts it through the campaign flow's countdown. The host's game type reaches the loader as pending_variant.txt and takes precedence over the level's "variant", which stays the default; a fireteam client reads it from the insertion point index the host's travel carries. The host's game settings and vehicle sets are patched into the copy the simulation loads. mjolnir_map_registry.dll is built by the mods release and ships in MJOLNIRLevelLoader's native folder. The paragraph below is the first route, from the campaign menu. CAMPAIGN → NEW GAME → the map (the last mission). "multiplayer": true tells MJOLNIRLevelLoader's native half to switch the simulation to the Megalo engine when that mission starts, and back before any other mission; "variant": "slayer" makes it install variants/slayer.mglo (written by --install) where the simulation's variant loader reads it. It needs native/mjolnir_map_registry.dll built from this revision. The patches and why each is needed are in re/megalo_engine.md; the manual form of the engine switch, without the variant, is: mjolnir live engine --launch-engine 2 --map-variant-gate skip --map-variant-reset skip # at the main menu

The level spawns its terrain and sky as soon as the world exists, behind the loading screen (waiting for the player pawn left converted maps black for 20-30 s after it), and fades in once the pawn exists.

python tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py <CODE> takes a converted map through the B30 pipeline, for each map in tools/level/ce_upgrade_maps.json (TST, BGL, DTI, YOY, ICE, SDW, TMB, INF, GPH, BCK, RAT, DCN, and the Halo 2 maps COA, CNT, ASC and ZAN). Its stages, which --stages picks from: land (a Landscape from the ground's heights), foliage (the game's grass and debris), swap (B30's own rocks and trees for CE's natural scenery), collision (their hulls, b30_collision.py, in the BSP through merge_ce_collision.py --extra), editor (the map's Landscape world), cook, bake, assemble (the level file) and install. A map with bake_foliage has its foliage placed in the landscape world (foliage_bake.py, PR #208) instead of spawned at load. pack_remastered.py packs the result as the next version of each map's hub listing (PR #184).

A Fluid Flux river (an upgraded map's flux with a domain) fills from priming sources over about a minute. Baking its settled water makes it start full, as the game's own 343 Guilty Spark water does (PDA_M06_343_FluxState): Host the map and wait for flux: river filled in UE4SS.log, plus a few seconds. Run mjolnir_flux_bake in the console. It writes flux_state/ (height.exr, velocity.exr, state.json) beside the installed level file. Run python tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py <CODE> --stages assemble, then --stages install with the game closed. Assemble copies the bake into the upgrade's work folder and sets level.flux.state; install and pack_remastered.py ship flux_state/ beside the level file. MJOLNIRLevelLoader builds a PDA_FluxSimulationState from the EXRs and sets it as the domain's InitialState before the domain starts. Its ResetRenderTargets then loads that state rather than clearing the water, the priming sources are skipped, and CE's water is hidden at once. A bake for another domain (centre, resolution, cell or height) is ignored, by assemble and by the loader, and the river fills the old way: rebake after changing a map's flux settings or its river mesh. Battle Creek and Timberland were baked on 2026-10-19.

A map must not ship unbaked. Every Flux source costs the render thread about 0.4 ms a frame, and a river that fills spawns all its priming sources for the first minute. Timberland's 42 primers held the median frame at 34 ms for that minute at 4K (13-25 ms after), and Proving Ground's 92 at 54 ms (15 ms with its bake). The river also visibly filled in during that minute. Timberland's and Battle Creek's bakes never reached their hub packs: the scan and the launcher kept only foliage and decals then, and later rebuilds took flux.state out to pass the scan. tools/level/add_flux_state.py <pack.mjolnir>... puts a map's bake (ce_conversions/upgrade/<CODE>/flux_state) into its published pack as the next patch release, after checking that it fits the pack's domain as the loader does, and changes nothing else in the pack. add_bots.py and add_objectives.py carry flux_state/ through their rebuilds.

Weather and model-less skies. ce_fog.py also reads the weather palette's particle systems that the BSP's clusters use, and the weather polyhedra, into fog.json. gen_ce_level.py maps a snow system to the game's PNW falling snow (environment.weather, docs/level_format.md). Weather stops under a roof (2026-10-13): gen_ce_level.py writes a roof map from the collision BSP's ceilings that have a floor below them (weather.roofs), and the loader hides the snow while a ceiling is within 25 m above the camera. CE's own weather polyhedra (mostly single planes over a room's openings) are read but not used. A sky with no model draws its outdoor fog colour past the opaque distance (environment.sky_fog). Only Coldsnap, among the converted maps, has either. Only one fog plane is drawn, and Coldsnap has three: the crevasse's two pit fogs and a "snowyfog night" layer. Since 2026-10-13 ce_fog.py puts first the plane most of the map's clusters draw (Coldsnap: its night fog, in 121 clusters). Visuals. No scenario decals on a plain conversion; CE's decal-flagged surfaces (light panels, moss) are drawn lifted 1 cm off what they lie on (merge_ce_scene.py DECAL_OFFSET, 2026-10-04). A light a placed object carries (the base beacons) is drawn as its lens flare only, never as a light, and the flare's brightness follows the object function that scales the light (Danger Canyon's beacons: a 1 s cosine;

MJOLNIRLevelLoader updates it every 40 ms). On an upgraded map ("Upgraded maps"), CE's scenario decals are drawn as quads over the decal's own texture (2026-10-12), the lights CE's placed objects carry are shadowed point lights (level.lights, 2026-10-12), and a flare's pulse runs in its material (M_CE_Flare Pulse, 2026-10-18). Dynamic lights (headlights, muzzle flashes, the flashlight) light players, vehicles and weapons but not the terrain: its base colour holds only the sun's share of the baked light (object shadows), and it sits on lighting channel 1, which only the level's sun shares. mjolnir_terrain_lights on (an experiment, needing the trial masters in chunk 983) lights it too: the masters top the base colour up to the surface's albedo and take the sun's light on the top-up back out of the baked colour, the terrain joins channel 0, and the terrain's hidden shadow copy, drawn two-sided, keeps the Unreal sun out of CE's shade. The copy's sharp shadow edges and the bake's texel steps never quite meet, so with a bake the sun share is drawn only where the bake is sunlit all round and the top-up only where it is shaded all round (BakeMargin, 1.5 texels; mjolnir_terrain_lights margin <texels>); between them the colour is CE's. At margin 0 Blood Gulch's bases traced their crenellations in black around the wall foot (verified on Blood Gulch and Coldsnap, 2026-10-05).

Since 2026-10-06 the default (MJOLNIRLevelLoader 0.4.0, runtime pack 1.3.0, maps 1.2.0; mjolnir_terrain_lights hybrid brings the mode above back for comparison) hands the terrain's direct light to Unreal: its base colour is CE's sunlit colour (the texel's own lightmap level where CE had sun, the level's sunlit level in CE's shade), CE's bump map is its normal, and its emissive is CE's colour less what Unreal's sun adds, never below CE's ambient. The sun mask (<stem>_sunmask, CE's lightmap seen from above at 1 m, cooked with the map and named by environment.sun_mask, tent-filtered) is the sun's light function, so CE's broad soft shadows stay and objects darken in them. A trial (mjolnir_terrain_lights on trial) reads the trial masters and a bake in the loader's bake\ folder in one respawn (two quick respawns were followed twice by a GPU crash). mjolnir_terrain_debug <layer> shows one layer of the terrain's light at a time. Keep the sun's angular size at the engine's 0.54 degrees: at 3 the virtual shadow maps leaked light in lines across shaded ground and around the first-person gun. Those lights are physical and tuned for the campaign's exposure, so the level's sun and sky are raised by environment.light_scale (256) with the exposure lowered to match (docs/level_format.md); without that a headlight turned what it reached white.

Scenery has CE's object lighting (ambient, dominant light, floor bounce, reflection tint) but not its shadow colour or point lights; a self-illumination colour that takes a change colour does not take it. Scenery collision stops players, vehicles and, since 2026-10-03, projectiles (checked offline, scenery_probe). Update 2026-10-21: in game on Death Island (2026-10-18), shots stop on scenery collision: the swapped B30 rocks' hulls, which reach the collision the same way as CE's scenery (merge_ce_collision.py --extra). The simulation's polygon test for such a crossing takes one winding only (FUN_1802f0170, CU4), so a two-sided surface stops a ray only from the side its plane faces: hulls wound inward stopped shots on their far wall, from inside, until they were wound outward. raytest::tree_game walks by that rule. That test shot a swapped rock, not CE's own scenery. Each node of a collision model is placed by its model node's rest pose: before halo2ue did that, a tree's canopy hull sat around its trunk at head height (Infinity, 2026-10-04), so maps converted earlier need converting again. The trees cost table space: Danger Canyon's 43,646 scenery triangles need 17 scenery instances instead of 6, and the maps that keep scenery in the BSP grow their 2D references several times over (Blood Gulch 55,634 and Boarding Action 58,539 of the 65,535 limit;

a map past it moves its scenery to instances of its own). See ce_terrain_collision.md, "Scenery in the tree". Object light colour. Players, vehicles and weapons are lit by the Unreal sun and sky light. On a map with a real sun (its lightmap at 0.8 or more where the bake has sun) they take that sunlit lightmap's colour, since CE lit an object by the lightmap under it; otherwise the sky's outdoor ambient colour, or the lightmaps' average when that colour lacks a channel. The sky's colour alone can be anything: Infinity's test sky is (0.5, 0.5, 0), which turned everything yellow. Approximations in the materials. CE's noise, jitter and wander functions are a value noise (4, 8 and 1 changes a period: jitter as a new random value 30 times a period strobed Damnation's volume lights); the variable-period functions use their nominal period. The plasma self-illumination band's width and the "add signed" chicago functions are estimates. The reflection's view term uses the per-pixel eye vector where CE used the camera's forward vector.

Water (swat, "Water" above), glass (sgla) and the reflection lightmap mask, once listed here as missing, are drawn: glass in CE's three passes since 2026-10-04 (merge_ce_scene.py extra_passes: the background tint multiplied in, the reflection added, then the diffuse pass, on M_CE_Glass{Tint,Reflection,Diffuse}, two-sided by flag bit 2), and the environment masters dim reflections in dark lightmap areas by the shader's lightmap brightness scale (LightmapReflScale, 2026-10-04). Plasma (spla, Yoyorast's energy beams) draws on M_CE_Plasma, MCC's transparent_plasma (2026-10-12). Maps install side by side. Each has its own scenario, world and mesh containers. The one registration container, pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P (the DT_Scenarios rows and the campaign asset's ScenarioList), is rebuilt from every installed map's record by level bake --install-test or mjolnir level register, whose code the launcher runs after a map install or removal. Only the CE_COOK=0 fallback still overrides the shipped cylinder, one such map at a time. More than 8,191 surfaces (Sidewinder, Infinity, Death Island, ...): the static body lists the terrain as one whole-instance key instead of one key per surface. Verified on Sidewinder: players walk and vehicles rest on it. One BSP per map. A map's second BSP is not converted (Coldsnap's is a copy of its first). The canvas palette.

A type B40's palette lacks gets an entry of its own at the bake (the shotgun, the battle rifle, the SMG, and the fuel rod as Reach's flak_cannon), and health packs are Megalo script ("Health packs"). What the game doesn't ship is dropped: the flamethrower, and custom weapons defs/level/ce-tag-map.json doesn't map (see ce_custom_content.md). No rocket Warthog. Rocket hogs spawn as chaingun hogs until the rocket turret's tag wrapper points at an actor Blueprint (the chaingun turret's, via ue-asset tagwrap, or a rewritten mesh with CE's rocket pod). Extent. Keep a map inside the canvas level's overall extent: lifted 800 wu above B40, Havok flung objects hundreds of wu. Game modes. Slayer and Capture the Flag (mjolnir megalo write --mode slayer ctf; the mods release ships variants/slayer.mglo and ctf.mglo, and --score N --out .../MJOLNIRLevelLoader/variants/slayer.mglo changes the score to win). Without the file the map runs the empty default variant: players spawn, nothing scores. --mode tick scores every player every tick, a smoke test for the interpreter. Update 2026-11-21: the mods release now ships seventeen variants: Slayer, Team Slayer, CTF, Assault, King, Crazy King, Team King, Oddball, Team Oddball, Juggernaut, Stalker, Reverse Tag, Race, Team Race, Rally, Team Rally and Pelican Warfare. The lobby offers a game type on a map whose modes lists it.

Status: 2026-10-22. Lockout and Ascension convert through the same command as the Halo 1 maps and start from MULTIPLAYER (mjolnir_auto host LOK slayer private, host ASC ctf private): their own worlds, the Spartan standing in the BSP, the pickups resting where Halo 2 put them, every material applied. Lockout was played by a person on 2026-10-21; the glass, snow and sky they found wrong are fixed (reflecting tinted glass, the chambers' gas behind it, snow where Halo 2 puts it, cloud banks in place of flat white planes). Ascension was compared side by side with MCC on 2026-10-22: its turning antennas and storm sky match. The Halo 1 pipeline is unchanged; its outputs for Chill Out and TST are byte-identical before and after the Halo 2 work. MCC's Halo 2 multiplayer maps (halo2/h2_maps_win64_dx11/*.map) become standalone Campaign Evolved maps the way classic CE maps do (ce_map_conversion.md): their own collision, render geometry, materials and lightmaps, player starts, pickups and markers, under the Megalo engine. export HCE_PAKS=".../Halo Campaign Evolved/Meteorite/Content/Paks" MCC=".../Halo The Master Chief Collection/halo2/h2_maps_win64_dx11" tools/level/convert_ce_map.sh "$MCC/lockout.map" LOK out/lok --install
shared.map and textures.dat must sit beside the map (they do in an install): every weapon, vehicle and most shaders live in shared.map, every bitmap's pixels in textures.dat.
Which game a map is from

mjolnir cache info <map> reads the header and names the game, the build and the tool that stages it (h2_cache_format.md, "Telling the games apart"). convert_ce_map.sh asks it first: map stager Halo 1 PC or Custom Edition (version 7, 609) halo2ue (HalcyonRing), unchanged Halo 2 MCC (version 13, game index 1) mjolnir cache stage (crates/blam-cache) Halo 1 MCC, Halo 3, ODST, Reach, Halo 4, H2A refused, by name, before anything runs The staging's manifest.json says which game it came from (source: halo_ce or halo2_mcc), and the few steps that are CE's alone branch on it: ce_fog.py and ce_sounds.py (they read the CE .map itself), the lightmap solver (CE's radiosity: LIGHTMAP_SCALE defaults to 0, keeping Halo 2's own pages) and the foliage (CE detail maps: FOLIAGE defaults to 0). gen_ce_level.py takes its tag map (defs/level/h2-tag-map.json), menu name and description from the same field.
mjolnir cache stage writes the files halo2ue writes for Halo 1, in the same units and axes, so every later step reads them unchanged:

Collision. Halo 2's 16-bit tables are widened into the CE element layout (collision_0.bin, layout: "ce_pc_v7"). Instanced geometry, which CE never had, is placed in world space (scale, forward/left/up, position), each polygon fan-split into standalone two-sided triangles that keep their material and flags, and appended as the scenery_surfaces tail CE scenery uses; merge_ce_collision.py adds the props after it. Lockout: 3,162 BSP surfaces, 75 instances (7,312 triangles), 15 crates (840), more than one 16-bit tree holds, so level collision puts the tail behind an instance of its own (as Timberland's trees). Surface materials. A Halo 2 shader names a global material (hard_terrain_concrete), not a CE material type; staging maps it onto the 29 the game ships: the same name, else an alias (concrete is stone, energy is energy_hologram), else the name shortened a word at a time and tried again the same way (hard_metal_thin_hum_grating to hard_metal_thin), else default_material. Each substitution is printed. Render geometry. Clusters and instanced geometry go into one bsp_0.gltf, a primitive per (shader, lightmap page), with each cluster's and instance's page from the lightmap tag and Halo 2's lightmap coordinates. Halo 2's triangles already wind counter-clockwise, so their order is kept (CE's are flipped). Shaders. MCC keeps no shader parameter names;

each template's bitmap slots and tiling are read in the template's order (h2::render::template), and what the compiled shaders do was read back from the DXBC in the shader pass tags (h2_cache_format.md). Opaque shaders become environment-master summaries (base, detail, second detail blended by the base's alpha where it is high, the reverse of CE's, bump, self-illumination; alpha tested for the alpha-test templates. The single-pass ones' compiled lightmap pass discards where the bump map's alpha rounds to 0: Zanzibar's palm fronds, beach bushes and tree foliage keep their outline only there, so their base map is staged with the bump map's alpha as <stem>__cut.png. The other tex_bump_alpha_test* shaders keep the outline in the base's alpha, the bump map's, or both (of the 26 stagings' fourteen: grates on Zanzibar and Foundation in the base; the temple vines on Sanctuary and Warlock, Derelict's vines, Headlong's girders, Midship's torn pillars and Terminal's generator in the bump map; Lockout's grate in both), so <stem>__cut.png takes the product of the two. Cut on the base alone, the bump-map ones drew as black quads, 2026-11-21 playtest). tex_bump_plasma_one_channel_illum (Zanzibar's fusion coil cores) is a lit base and detail plus the plasma pass's glow from bitmap 3: red times a band of its alpha around pixel constant 2's, plus green and blue each times a pink pixel constant.

It becomes CE's three-channel self-illumination (<stem>__glow.png: green, blue, and red x the band baked at the shader's level, tinted by pixel constants 3, 4 and 5; a colour image in one channel drew white). Read as a detail map, its magenta channels drew a pink and black grid. overlay (Zanzibar's Camp Froman sign, the military crates' stencils) is 2 x base x tint, drawn as a double multiply. On Zanzibar the multiply master draws nothing in the after-DOF translucency pass (a black multiply on the sign stayed invisible, and appeared with r.SeparateTranslucency 0; the same black multiply draws on Chill Out's glass, cause not found), so the multiply is baked into an alpha-blended copy, <stem>__overlay.png: black at 1 - m where the overlay darkens the frame by m (exact), clear at neutral grey and where it brightens: no blend brightens whatever lies under it, and as its hue at (m - 1) / 2 a crack map's near-grey laid a pale sheet over Sanctuary's dark ceilings. water_edge_blend (Zanzibar's flat plane at sea level) writes its map's alpha into the frame's alpha only, a mask the water fades by; its geometry is left out (drawn opaque without a map, it was a big white patch on the beach).

Water (water_pool, water_pool_cube: Beaver Creek's creek, Coagulation's cave pool, Sanctuary's streams) mixes the rippled frame behind with its reflection map by a fresnel term (its fresnel map's alpha: 0 looking straight down, 0.72 at a grazing angle). It goes in as CE's own water (swat, M_CE_Water): the reflection (a cube, or a 2D reflection map on all six faces) along the normal rippled by its ripple map (bitmap 0, a normal map as CE's ripples are, in two scrolling layers), added into the frame, weighted from 0 straight down to 0.72 at the edge (flag 0 over the master's white base). Drawn as a chicago cube blended over the frame, Beaver Creek's creek was an unmoving glossy picture of its reflection map. Waterfalls (waves) are min(1, mask x A + mask x B) x C, each scrolling: CE's four-stage chain as (A + B) x mask x C. tex_bump_illum_3_channel (Backwash's blue lights) has a grey detail before its base, and its glow map's channels tinted by pixel constants 4, 6 and 7 as CE's three self-illumination colours. An alpha-tested template that cuts out on its bump map keeps a placeholder base (Backwash's canopy, color_black), taken to the bump map's size. tex_detail_blend (Sanctuary's ground, the Mombasa trees) is a base and two details blended by its alpha, the details' scales in vertex constants 2 and 3;

tex_illum and tex_illum_bloom (Backwash's fungus, Triplicate's lights) a base, a detail and a glow map; decal_simple (Street Sweeper's road stripes, Headlong's signs) its one map alpha blended. A template with no slot layout falls back to the shader's runtime diffuse map, drawn opaque, which is how these lost their details, glow and cut-outs. Halo 2 tiles each map by a u and a v scale, and many are uneven (the palm bark's detail and bump 2 x 12, the beach's sand 128 x 64); CE's environment shader takes one scale per map. The base map's tiling is in the UVs; a detail or bump map tiled unevenly relative to it is staged as a copy repeated to the ratio (<stem>__x<nu>y<nv>.png, at most 16 a side) and drawn at the smaller scale. Read as u alone, the palm's detail was stretched six times along the trunk. Decals. The scenario's decals (Zanzibar's 40 caution, safety and warning signs, the CAUTION over the beach gate) go to the placement's decals with their bitmap, radius and the bitmap's aspect. tools/level/gen_ce_level.py lays each as a quad on the nearest surface within 3 m, by true distance over every triangle whose bounds come that close (by centre, the flywheel room's sign missed its big wall triangle and went onto a slanted face, tilted and half buried), its longer side twice the radius, drawn with the transparent alpha master over the cooked bitmap;

tools/level/ce_material_spec.py cooks the bitmaps with the map's. By layer: lit alpha blend (0, 1) as it is; multiply (3) and double multiply (2: bullet holes, scorches, Desolation's and Warlock's team emblems) with the multiply baked into an alpha-blended copy (<stem>__mul<gain>.png, as the overlays, times the bitmap's alpha); max (4) and add (5) on the additive master. Drawn as plain alpha, the rust decals were orange blobs and the emblems solid bars. Glass (one_alpha_env) becomes CE's glass shader: the base map tinted by the albedo and facing tints, blended by its alpha, unlit, and the environment cube map reflected through the specular mask with the environment tint; the cube's six faces are staged in D3D order. The two-layer glass (two_alpha_env_illum: Turf's storefront and stairwell doors, Triplicate's glass rails, the medical tent's panels) has the same slots and pixel constants, a second glass layer in slot 4, and goes in the same way; two_alpha_env_detail (the Forerunner "invisible" glass) has only placeholders and draws nothing. Read through the transparent catch-all, slot 0's reflection cube was drawn as a picture: Turf's stairwell door was an opaque dark sheet with nothing behind it to stop a player.

tex_bump_env_alpha_test_combined cuts out on the base's alpha times bitmap 1's (Turf's damaged stucco: a solid door base, the splintered boards in base_stucco1_damaged_01_alpha; the chainlink fence keeps its holes in the base, alpha_white in slot 1). Change colours (tex_bump_one_change_color: Turf's panel trucks and crates) are base x lerp(1, the object's colour, bitmap 2) in the compiled lightmap pass; the mask goes in as CE's shader_model multipurpose alpha (<stem>__mp.png) and each prop placement carries its object's colour permutations (obje +0xAC) as change_colors, Halo 2's weights (shares: the truck's off-white 0.4, red 0.2, tan 0.2) summed into CE's running cut-offs, so tools/level/merge_ce_scene.py draws one per placement into the object lighting page as it does for CE scenery; a placement's own colours (active bits at +0x38, ARGB at +0x3C) win. Read without the mask, every truck drew its untinted off-white base. Self-illumination (tex_bump_illum and its kin) is a pass of its own, default_self_illumination: saturate(glow map x pass constant 1), added over the lit surface, not lit with it (Turf's light fixtures are black where they glow). The template's remapping table names the pixel constant (2 for tex_bump_illum, 0 for tex_bump_illum_no_specular);

an animated parameter on descriptor 0x81 drives it instead, a periodic colour function going in as its wave between its darkest and brightest non-zero colour (the storefront signs jitter between 0.46 and 0.5). The environment master adds it after the fog when SelfIllumAdd is set. The "two plus two" shaders (the sky's cloud banks, the containment gas) are mask x layer x layer, tiled and scrolling as the shader animates them, alpha blended; the plasma shaders (plasma_alpha: Zanzibar's flywheel lightning, the teleporter beams, Lockout's grav lifts) draw with M_H2_PlasmaAlpha (unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_h2_materials.py, /Game/MJOLNIR/H2, chunk 981 beside the runtime pack), the compiled shader as it is: noise A's blue and noise B's red, each scrolling, banded into a sharp ridge where they meet and twice more inside it, coloured between pixel constants 1 and 0 by the second band plus 3 on the innermost, faded by the mask's alpha, added. The staging keeps a chicago approximation beside it (h2_plasma in the shader summary; without the master, noise x noise x mask in the bands' mean colour drew soft clouds). All of these draw in the translucent mesh.

Opaque env templates (the tex_bump_env family) reflect their cube map as Halo 2's lightmap pass does: the cube along the reflected eye vector, times a colour and a brightness each between the glancing and the facing value, masked by the albedo's alpha and dimmed with the light, added to the lit surface. The cube is whichever of the shader's bitmaps is one; the template's black placeholder cube reflects nothing. 22 of the 24 maps have such surfaces (Lockout only its grav pads; Ascension its Forerunner windows and panels). Sky layers. Besides the alpha and "two plus two" layers, Ascension's sky uses two more templates, read back from their compiled shaders: the cloud cover (sky_two_alpha_clouds: a cloud map tiled 8x and scrolling, times a cover mask, colour and alpha, alpha blended) and the sun shafts (sky_one_add_illum_detail: a mask's colour times its alpha, times a scrolling detail, tinted, added). Drawn as one map each, the cloud map covered the whole dome in flat grey and the shafts were white wedges. Additive clouds (two_add_clouds, sky_two_add_clouds: Tombstone's sky dome, Gemini's sky, the recharge stations' glow) are min(1, 2 x bitmap 0 x bitmap 1), faded by pixel constant 0's alpha: CE's double multiply, or bitmap 0 alone where bitmap 1 is default_multiplicative (50% grey).

The Covenant holo panels (two_add_detail_masked: Midship, Desolation, Gemini) compile to the same product of the panel map and a static map, plus a readout tiled 4 x through the panel's alpha; they go in as the clouds do, without the readout. Drawn from the static alone, they were solid white blocks. Lightning (Colossus, Triplicate) has that alpha at 0 and flashes by an animation the conversion doesn't carry, so it isn't drawn. The fusion coils' bloom (two_add_env_illum) is bitmap 3 tinted by pixel constant 3, added; the storm layers and horizon gradients (sky_one_alpha_env_clamped, Colossus, Containment) take one_alpha_env's slots. Read with the catch-all additive slots (bitmap 1), these drew nothing or only their mask. add_illum_detail (Gemini's hologram halo: a ring map through scrolling scanlines) and one_add_illum_detail (the light volumes of Gemini, Containment and Waterworks) are the sun shafts' template outside the sky, drawn the same way; the facing colour's alpha (vertex constant 6.w: 1 on the sun shafts, 0.15 on Gemini's white volumes) scales the tint, and add_illum_detail, whose five constants are only the maps' transforms, has no facing colour. Drawn from bitmap 1 alone, the halo was a solid grey ring of scanlines. These and the holo template fade by view angle: the vertex colour's alpha runs from a glancing alpha to a facing one by N.V (constants 7.w and 6.w;

the holo template's 11.w and 10.w), so where the facing alpha is higher a volume seen edge-on vanishes. That goes in as CE's framebuffer_fade_mode 2 ( N.V ); without it Desolation's light shafts (a holo-template volume with a white mask) were solid white slabs. A transparent template's textures, transforms and scrolls are read the way halo2.dll reads them: a constant's descriptor names its texture slot (bits 10-12) and row (bits 5-9: 14 and 15, the 2D affine rows), the template's remapping table names each slot's bitmap, and an overlay's function is evaluated as the engine's evaluator does (identity, transition, periodic slide, linear with its own slope; the engine adds the translation, as CE's masters add their animation). Sky. The sky's lights (yaw, pitch, colour, power, diameter, whether the lightmaps used them), outdoor ambient and atmospheric fog go to the placement as halo2ue puts a CE sky's, so the level's sun, sky light and fog follow them. Halo 2 stores the ambient as a colour alone; it goes in at CE's usual power, 0.2 (at 1, Ascension's lit the player and weapons 3.8 times too bright). Lockout's light lit nothing (its radiosity flags are clear; the sky model lit the lightmaps), so its sun comes from the lightmaps' incident directions, as for a CE map without one.

Halo 2's atmospheric fog covers the sky as well: one at full density (Backwash's swamp, opaque at 20 world units) also gives the level sky_fog, so everything past the opaque distance, the black sky dome included, is the fog's colour (gen_ce_level.py sky_and_weather; Backwash's sky drew black above the fog). Placements. Halo 2 spawns every multiplayer pickup and vehicle through netgame equipment (item and vehicle collections): each becomes halo2ue's netgame_equipment or vehicle entry naming the collection's item. Netgame flags take CE's names where CE has the thing (CtfFlag, OddballSpawn, HillFlag with its hill index, TeleportFrom/TeleportTo paired by identifier); assault, territories and headhunter keep names the tag map leaves out. Halo 2 spawns by influence, so its player starts carry no CTF side (Lockout's are all team 0); each start takes the side of the nearer CTF flag spawn, so a CTF game has red and blue spawns. A start (0x34 bytes) lists four game types at 0x14 (CE's numbers, plus 6 Headhunter, 7 Juggernaut and 8 Territories) and a spawn type for each at 0x1C (0 both, 1 initial spawn only, 2 respawn only), staged as game_types and spawn_types. A start that lists no game type serves every one: Containment, Relic, Sanctuary and Warlock list none on any start, and Terminal's 88 untyped starts stand beside 61 All games ones.

The level generator places them by game type (ce_map_conversion.md, "Spawn sets"); spawn types are not used yet. Props are scenery and crates (bloc), staged with their render and collision models. A prop with no collision model collides in Halo 2 by its physics model's solid shapes alone (the boxes, polyhedra and pills whose material is not a phantom's): Burial Mounds' and Elongation's and Gemini's invisible boxes, Zanzibar's beach bushes. The stage writes those as its collision (crate::h2::phantom::solid_triangles, each shape's planes closed into a triangle mesh; a pill as the box round it). The surfaces are in the built level (Elongation gains 96), but no difference has been shown in play: dropped on Elongation's first box a player lands on a real surface 0.2 world units above its top, with or without it. A prop with both keeps its collision model, which is what projectiles hit in Halo 2. Game-type props (the CTF and territory flag bases) are left out: the level's own CTF stands replace them. Planar fog. A BSP's fog plane (Ascension's cloud deck, Lockout's haze below the map, the water of Dune, Needle and Zanzibar) goes to fog.json as ce_fog.py writes a CE map's, so the masters fog what lies below the plane by its depth under it and its distance, as CE's planar fog does. Halo 2 draws planar fog per surface only (every opaque template's fog_planar pass;

no fog-plane mesh, no full-screen pass), so that is all there is to it. The cloud sea MCC shows under Ascension's island, wisps drifting through it, is not fog: it is a transparent cloud plane in the BSP 12.6 wu under the fog plane (ascension_clouds, a two_alpha_clouds shader), a static disk of cloud puffs times a cloud tile scrolled over it, drawn unfogged over the sky's lower half. Drawn as one static grey map, it was the flat pale plane the rocks stood in. Halo 2's transparent templates other than glass have no fog in their compiled shaders, so they go in fogged: false and the material spec leaves their fog out. Where the view passes below the plane and finds no surface, MCC draws the fog's colour (its fog pass lays a depth copy for the engine's full-screen fog shaders): the rocks' fogged lower ends vanish into it, where ours stood out against the sky's dark lower edge. A level plane gets that as the loader's height fog at the plane, in the fog's colour, starting 1.5 km out past the cloud plane (gen_ce_level.h2_fog_fill, environment.haze). The plane names its fog through the scenario's planar fog palette; Beaver Creek's names an entry the scenario does not have and gets none. Machines.

A gear whose device animation turns its one node about one fixed axis is placed like scenery, with its turn: the axis and the keys of its device:position animation as (seconds, degrees) over its position transition time, read by crate::h2::animation (the keyframe codecs 4-7, and codec 3, which stores every frame).
