That covers Ascension's three antennas (the big arms that swing around the central pillar every 40 s, about +Z), Zanzibar's big wheel, its blades and three flywheels (+Y; two flywheels are placed tilted) and Foundation's two fans. merge_ce_scene.py --machines writes each such placement as a mesh of its own (scene_machine_<k>.gltf, built as SM_<code>_Machine<k>; its transparent parts, such as the flywheels' lightning, as scene_machine_<k>t.gltf, since a rewritten mesh enters the translucency pass by its slot 0) with its pivot, keys and, when the axis is not the world's +Z, the axis in Unreal's axes beside it (.motion.json); the level's decor entry carries them as motion, and MJOLNIRLevelLoader turns the actor about the pivot. Every other machine's motion (doors, lifts, Triplicate's train, Backwash's monitor) is left out as before, listed in staging's notes: still, a closed gate or a parked train would block a way Halo 2 opens. A lift's push does not need its motion; see the next item. Lifts, jump pads and vents.

Halo 2 pushes through physics model phantoms (crate::h2::phantom): shapes nothing collides with, each with a phantom type (accelerations and top speeds along a render model marker's forward, towards its axis and towards its point, and whether it holds off gravity). The stage writes every placed object's phantoms that push players to placement.json lifts (object space, whether or not the prop is drawn), gen_ce_level.py puts them in the level file in Unreal space (lifts: planes or a pill, a bounding sphere, the marker, the pushes in cm). MJOLNIRLevelLoader's lifts.lua hands them, in the simulation's units, to MJOLNIRLobby's DLL once a map, and the DLL sets the velocity of a player inside one through (object_set_velocity (player_get N) ...) on every simulation tick (native/lobby/lifts_runtime.h, re/lift_push.md). Each game pushes its own players only: a joiner's motion is its own game's, and a push the host sends a joiner's unit does nothing (two PCs, 2026-10-25). Maps with player lifts: Lockout, Midship, Cyclotron (Ivory Tower), Colossus, Coagulation, Headlong, High Plains (Tombstone, hvac), Backwash, Foundation, Warlock, Derelict (Desolation), Dune (Relic, watchtowers), Ascension and Gemini (jump pads).

lifts is a key only the loader reads, so a published pack gets them without a rebake: tools/level/add_lifts.py stages the map, adds the block to the pack's level file and packs the next version, and checks nothing else changed (the bots stay as baked). Those 14 maps shipped this way at 1.3.0 on 2026-11-04, with the gaps in testing listed in docs/h2_lifts_release.md. The other 11 maps have no phantom that pushes players and stay at 1.2.0. Moving collision. The simulation does all collision, never reads Unreal geometry, and its structure BSP cannot move: an arm's collision baked at rest stood where the arm only sometimes is. Rewriting a live object's transform moves the object but not its Havok body; a device machine moves its collision with its animation. So each turning part becomes a machine of the simulation's own (tools/level/h2_machines.py, run by convert_ce_map.sh), five tags cloned from B40's elevator, whose nodes and Havok layouts agree, each a container pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-<k><g> under objects\mjolnir\<code>\: an animation graph whose one resource member turns the root by the part's keys, every frame with codec 3 (the shipped turning props' own; its header is Halo 2's), beside the static pose, node flags, an uncompressed copy and object-space frames the resource carries;

a collision model holding the part's own Halo 2 collision BSP, which staging writes as collision/<part>.bsp.json and mjolnir level machine-collision packs with its Havok MOPP. Bipeds meet a machine's collision model, not its physics model's shapes: a player dropped on an arm built of physics boxes alone fell through it; a physics model of boxes over the part's triangles, for what moves through Havok (the elevator's lift phantom goes with it); a model, and a gear machine whose "position transition time" is the rate 1 / period (the engine reads it as a rate: 40 ran the antennas 40 times a second, aliased into a seven-second wobble). The engine shows a gear at frame position x N, held at the last frame (Halo 2 used N - 1), so frame f is the angle at f / N of the turn, one every 0.1 s: with Halo 2's five frames Zanzibar's wheel turned a full circle in 24 s of its 30 and stood still for 6.

The generator places each machine where its part is, with its full rotation (blam.objects, group machines), and gives the part's mesh motion.follow; the merge leaves the part's collision out of the BSP (merge_ce_collision.py --sim-machines). The machine draws through the elevator's Blueprint, whose turning part follows the root; the loader hides that part's mesh, attaches the Halo 2 mesh to it, and fits the turn's phase (the simulation starts its gears about 25 s off the world clock) for the sounds. Checked on Ascension: a player dropped on an arm stands on it and is carried round as it turns. Props that move and break. A crate (bloc) whose physics model has a rigid body that is neither keyframed nor fixed moves in Halo 2; one with constraints (Zanzibar's hanging lights, crane, awnings) is held and stays still. crate::h2::props reads it from the tags and the stage writes it onto the placement: h2_physics (mass, motion type, bodies, constraints), h2_damage (the model's damage info, 0x60: vitality and every instant response with its effect, damage effect, and the sounds and decals the effect references, the sounds staged as one-shots) and h2_functions.

tools/level/h2_physics_props.py turns every movable type into crate tags (a physics shape of the model's box, mass from Halo 2's, and a death response when Halo 2's kills it: the fusion coil's 15 vitality), takes the props out of the merged meshes and builds their meshes; the level loader (props.lua) dresses each crate as the prop placed nearest where it first appears, so every type shares one crate actor class. Zanzibar: 11 types over 55 placements. A dying prop plays our fuel-rod explosion and fire, a plasma scorch and Halo 2's own death sound (sound\visual_effects\fusion_coil_destroyed, 13 variants; this game's Wwise events cannot be posted from a mod), and stays, burnt. A coil's core (tex_bump_plasma_one_channel_illum) is a one-channel mask lit by a colour running from its damaged pink-red (pixel constant 3) to its healthy orange with the object's health function; read as a picture its green channel drew the coils green. A prop's overlay stencil (the crates' MKT1 EMERGENCY FOOD) is drawn as masked paint on the prop: the level's darkening copy loses text that brightens. A door (machine type 1: Zanzibar's house gate) opens from its control (the keypad, staged as a ctrl placement; the two share position group 0).

crate::h2::door reads its render model's nodes (0x48, 0x60 each: parent 0x04, default translation 0x0C, rotation 0x18) and decodes device:position for every node: keyframe codec 6, four turning and ten sliding nodes named by the three node bit fields that end the frame data, their frame info in node order (read last node first the gate's doors stayed shut while its bars slid across), sliding keys offsets added to the default translation. A vertex's node is its rigid-boned vertex's index byte through the section's node map (resource locator 0x68), staged as _NODE. h2_physics_props.py splits the door into a mesh a node (doors.json). The simulation opens it and Unreal moves it: every node with a collision BSP (staged h2_door.collision, one BSP a node; the gate's 14, its frame and four ramps among them) becomes a device machine with tags of its own (h2_door_machines.py: animation, collision, physics, model and machine, written into the layout of B40's elevator family). Its root follows the node exactly, turning and sliding at once (h2_machines.pose_resource: codec 3 with the root's rotation and translation both animated, so a ramp swinging about its hinge is one machine); its collision is the node's own BSP, its physics boxes cover the BSP's triangles. Each machine stands on a grid about the door's origin, 0.05 wu (15 cm) apart, every machine of a map on a cell of its own.

Each placed machine draws its own part. Its machine tag (one a placement; the animation, collision, physics and model tags are shared) names an actor of its own (--asset-reference): B40's elevator Blueprint cloned by write_actors (crates/ue-asset/examples/ vehicle_actor.rs, which renames the package, its generated class and default object) into /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/Machines/ BP_<CODE>_Machine<n>, all in pakchunk987-MJOLNIRACT-<CODE>_P. The Blueprint's mesh list (BlamMeshSynchronizationComponent RuntimeRegions {default}.Permutations{default}.StaticMeshes, which held the elevator floor on bone platform) names the node's part meshes instead, each on bone Root (the simulation's root node, bones elevator_world, Root, Platform) at its rest offset from the actor, turned by the placement's yaw. So Unreal draws and moves the part with no elevator to hide and no script attaching anything; the part meshes are not spawned as decor (the level's doors parts carry their mesh and materials instead). The loader (doors.lua) only finds each machine's actor by its class (one scan of the Blam object actors); it hides the keypad's switch panel's components (the actor's own hidden flag is reset by the game) and watches one machine at 4 Hz (10 Hz while moving) only for Halo 2's sounds.

The parts' materials are cooked, as the custom vehicles' are (machine_instances.py): when the map's cook runs, build_terrain_meshes.py gives each part mesh real slots (mesh_rewrite --asset-imports) naming a material instance per slot, <root>/MachineMaterials/MI_<mesh>_n<slot>, of the slot's prop_lit material; ce_vehicle_instances_editor.py makes them after build_ce_level.py and the cook ships them in the map's chunk, and machine_instances.py check reads every one back (in the chunk, no static permutation, its textures cooked beside it). The level's parts then carry no materials, so nothing is dressed at spawn. The Blueprint's own MaterialOverrides cannot do it: they match slots by name, and a mesh rewritten from the engine's cube keeps the cube's one slot (WorldGridMaterial) unless --asset-imports writes its own. Without a cook (CE_COOK=0), and on a level built before this, the loader dresses the parts once a world, as before.

An upgraded map (upgrade_ce_map.py) does the same from its own stages. h2_physics_props.py --instance-root /Game/MJOLNIR/MachineParts/<landscape> builds the turning parts and the door parts naming instances in that folder and lists them in <scene>/machine_instances.json. The editor stage finishes each entry as assemble finished a part the loader dressed (the redrawn textures, detail_fill: machine_parts_plan, the same two helpers) and makes the instances after the landscape world, under a label of the folder's own (PAL_MJOLNIR_<landscape>Parts, the landscape's chunk, not recursive: the landscape's own labels are, and would take the masters into the chunk). The cook stage runs machine_instances.py check on the chunk (the conversion's cook container named for the textures it carries), and assemble leaves those gears without materials. Zanzibar: 21 slots, each equal to what the loader set before, checked entry by entry; in game all 21 draw MI_ZAN_* instances, in a second match on the map too.

The cook stage also refreshes the map's own cook container (refresh_map_cook): textures imported into the map's folder after its conversion cooked (the door parts' and the props' stencils, by h2_physics_props.py) are in this cook's chunk, not in the conversion's container the install took, and Zanzibar's gate had drawn textured only beside a test container installed by hand. When the staged chunk holds everything the conversion's does and more, a copy in the work folder becomes the map's MJOLNIRCOOK-<CODE>. Run the stages with HCE_PAKS, MJOLNIR and EXAMPLES set (release builds): the bake's defaults are the debug examples, which may be older than the level schema.

The map's own tag containers (its machines and control, their actors, the gears' and the movable props' crate tags) are one list, machine_containers.py, read by the install stage and by both pack tools (pack_local_map.py, pack_remastered.py), so a pack carries what the tested install did. The tags go in the pack folder's machines/, named -MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-... (a prop's -MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>-PROP-<leaf>-<g>), where mjolnir map pack takes a map's tags from; the actors' containers end -<CODE>_P beside the map's own. Before this the packs carried none of them and the props' tags were in the game only as local builds installed by hand. Zanzibar: 123 containers, every one in a test pack (not signed, not published), and the map played from the pipeline's install alone with its 14 gate machines, 8 gears and 55 props. Two copies of the game (tools/remote/instances.mjs) agreed: every slot cooked and every prop present in both, and the gate opened by the host stood open in the client's own simulation and its own view.

A placement's own flags go with it (scenario machine +0x38 device flags, +0x3C machine flags; the simulation's bits are Halo 2's). Containment's base gates are door-type machines (type 0) with no activation radius, so the simulation's door logic opens one for any unit within its bounding radius and shuts it after its open time. Halo 2 places them with machine flag 1, "does not operate automatically", so only their switches move them. Without that flag they stood open (2026-11-15). Zanzibar's gate parts are platforms (type 1), placed with no flags. Before, the fields were whatever B40 placement each map cloned (the one nearest its origin), and some of those are "initially open", "position reversed" or "does not close automatically". Of the Halo 2 machines, only Containment's carry a flag (h2_machine_placements <map> lists them); Gemini's, Triplicate's, Colossus's and Backwash's doors carry none and open for a unit nearby, as in Halo 2. Dressing state belongs to the world: a second match on the same map has the same world name and new actors, and parts kept from the first came back as bare grid (fixed 2026-11-15).

The keypad gets B40's switch panel; machines and switch share one device group (zan_group0, Halo 2's position group 0, baked into the scenario), so a player pressing the keypad opens the gate, collision and all, for everyone in the match. The install stage installs every machine's containers (machine_containers.py). device_group_set none zan_group0 1 opens it from the console.

Every machine that moves in parts is staged the same way, whatever its type. Staging tries a one-node gear first (gear_turn); any other machine whose device:position decodes (keyframe codecs 4-7, and codec 3, which stores every frame) is staged as h2_door with its own behaviour (machine: type 0x11C, flags 0x11E, door open time 0x120, automatic activation radius 0x118). A machine with no animation never moves and is staged as scenery with its collision (Dune's watchtowers). h2_machine_census <maps> lists every machine and whether it decodes. In MCC that is Containment's base gates, shields and switches, Gemini's High Charity doors and gravity columns, Triplicate's garage gates and train, Cyclotron's elevator, Waterworks' crusher, Backwash's monitor and Dune's collapsing teleporters; all seven maps build their machines (h2_door_machines.py). The rules, from the tags: one machine a collision BSP, and one a node that moves without collision (no collision or physics model: Dune's teleporter legs); the machine tag's type is Halo 2's: a door (0) opens by itself within its activation radius (proven on Zanzibar with Triplicate's garage gate: a Ghost parked inside its 5 wu opened it, as Halo 2 does), a gear (2) runs round by itself (Triplicate's train: all six parts' positions agree, 0.732 then 0.936 three seconds later), a platform (1) goes where its device group sends it;

a placement's machines stand on a 15 cm grid about its origin, so a door's parts measure its radius from nearly one point, every machine of the map on a cell of its own (Triplicate's train and its deathball are placed 3 cm apart; on shared cells the loader bound one actor twice and an elevator mesh rode the train's nose). The loader claims each actor once, nearest first; a machine tag is built once and placed per placement (Triplicate's three garage gates); Halo 2's position group number is the device group (<code>_group<n>), shared by every machine and control of that number (Containment's gate and its switch), each control placed once.

A fresh conversion (convert_ce_map.sh) does the same as the upgrade pipeline: after level collision, h2_door_machines.py <staging> <CODE> <out>/machines --transform <name>.sbsp.transform.json builds every placement's machines (positions moved with the map) and writes doors.json; merge_ce_scene.py --doors takes the machines out of the static scene as a mesh a node (scene_machine_d<k>n<node>.gltf with a .door.json naming its staging entry and node, which build_terrain_meshes.py turns into a decor id); gen_ce_level.py --doors adds the machines, controls and device groups to the scenario and the level's doors for the loader (level bake keeps doors as opaque, as it keeps lifts). The machine containers sit with h2_machines.py's in <out>/machines and install with them. Triplicate (TRI, 2026-11-15): seven placements, 20 machines, 18 part meshes, all bound and attached; a garage gate rolled up when the player was teleported into its 5 wu radius. Halo 1 conversions (Chill Out) and Halo 2 maps without such machines (Lockout) merge byte-identically. The published Containment, Gemini, Waterworks, Backwash and Foundation will gain their machines the next time they are converted.

A moving part is lit by Unreal (prop_lit.py's M_CE_PropLit, both pipelines): lit by the light baked where it was placed, Triplicate's trains, parked in a dark tunnel, drew black through the station. The trains themselves run as the tag says: a 15 s loop, moving for about 5 s, 427 m at up to about 107 m/s. (A reading that looked frozen was the train parked at the end of its run for the other two thirds of the loop.)

The game hides the actors of machines the player cannot see (bHidden, the skeleton not rendered) and gives them no pose until the player can; then it poses them at once where the simulation has them (Zanzibar, 2026-11-15: all fourteen gate machines hidden with the player at spawn, the gate opened, nothing moved; the player teleported to the gate, all fourteen shown and every part open). FlyCam does not count as the player's view: a part that stands still in a FlyCam shot while the player is elsewhere is this culling, not a fault. Judge machines from the player's own view. (This explains every "stuck" ramp, bar and "frozen" train reading earlier that day; un-hiding an actor by hand does not pose it, the game's own visibility does.) It is distance culling, as for every Blam object, judged by the object's bounding radius: with the player 20 wu from the gate none of its machines hid, at 35 wu 11 of 14, from 45 wu all. Since the parts are the actors' own meshes now, a culled part is not drawn, as a culled crate or weapon is not; Halo 2 culls the gate as one object (bounding radius 2.56 wu, object +0x04, offset +0x08), so every machine of a placement takes the placement's largest reach as its radius and the parts go and come together. Gears (h2_machines.py) were never hidden within 75 m of the player.

Two copies on PC 1 (tools/remote/instances.mjs up 2, one simulation): each found and dressed all fourteen actors; the gate opened from the host's console showed open on the client; each copy culls by its own player, and each showed every part open once its player was at the gate. Opaque shaders that scroll their base map are staged as base_scroll (Zanzibar's rotating_metal, the drum under the spindle grates: one repeat in u every 2 s); the h2_staging map setting applies it to the level's slots as CE's environment scroll (BaseUAnim). Turning machines are lit by Unreal (their object page drew black, and a black flywheel turning read as one standing still); one riding a simulation machine whose Unreal part stops updating (the big wheel and blades: the simulation's position advances, the game stops copying its pose) leaves the part after 2 s and turns by the clock. Teleporters. Halo 2's teleporter scenery (Ascension's 2way_teleporter bases) is placed like any other prop: the generator's working pads on the teleporter flags draw nothing. Its beam is a plasma_alpha shader, its glow a one_add_illum (the base map times pixel constant 0, added). The bases have no collision model. Sound. Halo 2's samples are not in the maps but in headerless sounds_*.dat files beside them (Opus and Xbox ADPCM; docs/h2_cache_format.md, "Sound").

crate::h2::sound stages them as ce_sounds.py stages a CE map's, staging/sounds_out (sounds.json and its files), which convert_ce_map.sh imports with build_ce_sounds.py and the generator plays: the BSP clusters' background loops (2D), the sound scenery and the loops placed objects carry (3D, at the object's origin), and the one-shots a turning machine's animation raises (Ascension's 12 antenna cues, at their frames). Opus packets go into an Ogg Opus file as they are, which the editor imports (Ascension's antenna1 came in at its tag's 2.240 s); ADPCM is decoded to WAV. A sound's playback gain (dB) and random pitch bounds (cents) become the entry's gain and pitch (Ascension's humming light plays 5 semitones down); a loop's distance bounds come from its lsnd (most loop samples carry none) unless the sound scenery overrides them. Halo 2 adds its sound class's gain to the sound's own (halo2.dll 0x6e5bd0: the class's upper gain bound and the sound's scale bound at scale 1; -7 dB for the ambient classes, -11 dB for machinery), so the entry's gain carries it. The class also caps how many of one sound play at once ("max sounds per tag", 4 for these classes), which becomes the emitter's max: the loader gives each such sound a concurrency group that keeps the nearest playing (Elongation places its belt hum 100 times with two tracks;

all 200 played, at the tag's gain, with every cluster's background on top). A background loop belongs to BSP clusters: zones are the clusters' bounds with the set of loops each plays, and the loader fades to the set of the box the camera is in or nearest to, the smallest when boxes overlap (the clusters themselves are not boxes). An attachment scaled by an object function (the jump pads' launch loop, phantom_power) is left out: it sounds only while the object drives it. Lightmaps. Halo 2 keeps its pages at half their light and doubles them in the shader; the CE masters take a page as it is, so the pages are staged doubled (clamped). Without that Lockout's interiors were nearly black. Its 65 small pages would each bake at 2,048 under lightmap_bake's default 16x, so Halo 2 maps bake at most 4x (BAKE_ARGS default). Render models (the sky, props) store positions and texture coordinates in -1..1 across the model's compression bounds; read raw, Lockout's sky was a 3 m knot at the origin and drew nothing. Weapons the game lacks take the nearest role (defs/level/h2-tag-map.json): the battle rifle the assault rifle, the brute shot the fuel rod gun, the carbine, brute plasma rifle and sentinel beam the plasma rifle.

A Halo 2 template's postprocess definition (stem +0x58) lists its passes, each pass's implementations and what each implementation feeds its shaders (specular_constants in render.rs reads it; the example h2_template_blocks prints it). Most opaque templates draw default_light_combined_tangentspace_specular_sphere. Its vertex shader passes vertex registers 10 and 11, fed from two of the shader's vertex constants, to the pixel shader, which adds sat(R.L)^8 x the light x lerp(register 11, register 10, sat(N.L)) through the frame's alpha (R the view reflected about the bumped normal, L the light's direction). The template's lightmap pass wrote that alpha first: min(1, 2 x base alpha x the light) for lightmap_tex_detail and nearly every other lightmap pass (tex, the detail blends, two and three detail, illum, shiny, tiling, change colour, honor guard), so the base map's alpha is a specular mask; 0 for the env passes, detail_overlay and detail_no_specular: those surfaces never shine, whatever their passes; the cut-out or other terms for the alpha-tested passes. Only alpha_test_no_bump's (the cut-out, which is the base alpha) matches what staging writes; the others are left without.

That is CE's lightmap specular (SpecLightmap: the lobe from the lightmap's incident direction, masked by the base map's alpha), its colour going from parallel to perpendicular by N.V rather than N.L: perpendicular takes register 10's constant, parallel register 11's. A template that cuts out on another map's alpha has the cut staged in the base's alpha, so it would shine all over; it gets none. Nor does a base map with no authored mask (alpha 1 everywhere): 157 of 552 specular shaders on the 25 maps, Coagulation's cliffs, Turf's stucco garage doors, Backwash's tree trunks, shone all over like plastic where Halo 2's surfaces read flat; the shaders with an authored mask (Turf's brushed door frames) keep it. Turf's door frames and posts (metal_grey_dark on matte_grey, brushed streaks in the alpha: vertex constants 7 and 8, 1.0 and 0.75 grey) drew flat grey without it. Placed objects (lit from the object lighting page) are left without: they have no incident direction per texel, so a flat face took one and saturated white (Turf's dumpster). 25 templates take it, 61% of the multiplayer maps' triangles (docs/h2_shader_census.md).

Halo 2 scatters grass, rocks, debris, litter and decals from its scenario's decorator sets (DECR) over each structure BSP (crates/blam-cache/src/h2/decorator.rs; the example h2_decorators prints a map's). The BSP's decorators block (+0x234) is an octree of 8-unit cells around a centre (cells per side x 8 units across); each leaf names groups, and a group a run of placements in a raw cache block, six words each. MCC's halo2.dll decodes them (0x979eeb; no tag carries the finished geometry, so the decode was read from there): position: the leaf cell's corner + (bits 0-9 x 8/1023, bits 10-19 x 8/1023, bits 20-31 x 8/4095) world units; internal word: bits 0-2 the class, 3-8 the permutation, 9-12 the yaw (v/15 of a turn), 13-15 the tint blend, 16-19 the scale (v/15 across the permutation's range), 20-31 an up vector the "align to normal" permutations turn to: the yaw then turns from Halo 2's own perpendicular to it (0x6fcf30: the smallest component zeroed, the other two swapped, one negated), and any other perpendicular turns every aligned piece by a fixed angle (Turf's cans lay 180 degrees round); tint and lightmap colours, two light directions.

On Zanzibar, Turf and Beaver Creek the decoded placements lie on the BSP's surface (median 0.1 units). The 20 maps with decorators hold 38,600: 31,000 models, 6,300 floating decals and 1,300 camera-facing sprites (Zanzibar's, all). A group's own type byte disagrees with its class's on Turf, so the class's (DECR class +0x04) decides. DXT1 bitmaps decode with their one-bit alpha (a three-colour block's index 3 is transparent black, as D3D samples it). Read opaque, the debris atlas drew each piece in a black box where Halo 2 cuts it out; elsewhere one to five textures a map gain transparent texels (Coagulation's light bands, Ascension's light strips, Zanzibar's hazard strips). Model decorators are staged as scenery: each set's model (models/<set>__decorator<k>.gltf, its run of the set's indices, double sided, decorator_tex cut out on its base map's alpha), one placement entry each with its rotation as basis (forward, left, up) and scale, which merge_ce_scene.py places like any object, and its light.

Every decorator is lit and coloured as Halo 2 colours its vertices (halo2.dll 0x7fa1d0): the permutation's tint 1 to tint 2 by the placement's blend, times the placement's tint by the base map tint percentage; times its light, the placement's lightmap colour by the lightmap tint percentage, grey (0.5) for the rest. The decorator pixel shaders draw 2 x texture x that colour. A model's entry carries the doubled product as light; a decal's or sprite's vertices already hold the product (their stored colour equals it on Turf and Coagulation to 8-bit rounding), doubled into the mesh's _LIGHT. merge_ce_scene.py lights each from that in place of the ground under it: one object page block a distinct colour (in 32nds), the incident direction along the normal so it draws flat, as Halo 2's does.

Decal decorators need no decode: the map stores them as geometry. Each cache block carries decal vertices (locator 0x08: 0x20 each, position, texture coordinate, a second coordinate, colour) and indices (0x10), 4 vertices and 6 indices a placement over its group's run (+0x0C vertex start and count, +0x10 index start and count); halo2.dll draws them as they are (0x9795c0). Their coordinates already point into the decal bitmap's atlas. decorator::decals reads them; staging writes one mesh a group and shader (models/<set>__decals<group>_<shader>.gltf, at the quads' centre): decorator_decal_paint alpha blended, decorator_decal_paint_multiply (stains, blast scorches) multiplying the frame by the map where its alpha covers, baked into an alpha blend as the overlay's is. Turf's 322 (posters, rubble, stains) draw in game. A group's own type byte calls Turf's posters and rubble models; their class and their decal vertices say decals.

The axis-rotating sprites (grass: Coagulation's 14,362, Relic's, Beaver Creek's, Containment's) are stored the same way, in the block's sprite vertices (locator 0x48: 0x30 each, base position, the corner's offset across and along the axis, the axis, texture coordinate, colour) and sprite indices (0x50), 4 and 6 a placement. Halo 2 turns each about its axis to face the camera, and so does ours: each comes out as one card in its rest pose (across Halo 2's perpendicular to the axis turned by the placement's yaw) on M_H2_Billboard (unreal/MJOLNIRMaterials/Scripts/build_h2_materials.py, chunk 981), the masked two-sided environment master with a World Position Offset that turns it. The vertex normal is the axis (the card draws flat lit, so it needs no face normal), and two extra UV channels carry, in Unreal centimetres, the way from the vertex to its base point on the axis (TEXCOORD_2 x, y and TEXCOORD_3 x) and its offset across (TEXCOORD_3 y): _BILLBOARD in the staged mesh, converted by merge_ce_scene.py, written by mesh_rewrite as channels 2 and 3 when a mesh has them. A runtime pack without the master draws the cards unturned (the level loader falls back to M_CE_EnvironmentMaskedTwoSided). A group draws from the sprite buffer when its block has one and its type says quad, or it has no decal buffer.

Zanzibar's "screen-facing quads" (group type 3) are foliage_earth models by their class, and are placed as models. merge_ce_scene.py merges every decorator primitive of a material into one: each glTF primitive becomes a section of the terrain mesh, drawn in every pass, and Coagulation's 2,639 pieces as their own sections drew 14,808 draws a frame (1,623 merged). Measured on PC 1 (RTX 5090, 3840x2160, Epic, mjolnir_bench at a held view over the grass, 2026-11-11): Coagulation without decorators 9.21 ms (GPU 6.53); with them as sections 10.34 ms; merged 9.63 to 9.84 ms (GPU 7.02), so the decorators cost about 0.5 ms, on the GPU. Their World Position Offset costs nothing measurable (off: same frame, GPU -0.2 ms). All three were benched in sessions in PC 1's slower state (the game thread on its V-Cache cores, by the 9 ms baseline; docs/performance.md, "Reading the numbers"); a control in the faster state read 7.80 ms.

Halo 2's glass (Turf's stairwell doors) is solid until shot, meleed or hit hard, then breaks and lets players through, as in Halo 2. Collision. mjolnir level collision (Halo 2 sources only) makes the glass breakable surfaces of the sim's own kind (blam_sbsp::convert::rebuild_breakable): each polygon is a pane (its front and back), each connected sheet a set, closed at its edges so the sim's flood fill never reads a missing surface. brittle_glass takes the brittle_glass_reinforced material: plain globals\glass breaks at any touch, so walking into it broke it. Drawing. The sheets go beside the BSP (<map>.sbsp.breakables.json, world units); tools/level/split_breakable_glass.py moves each sheet's transparent triangles into mesh slots of their own, and the level entry lists them (breakables: sheet, box in cm, slots). The level loader hooks the game's break effect (BP_BaseBreakableSurfaceEffect_C:Spawn, which names the point it broke at): the sheet there loses its slots (M_CE_Hidden) and throws glass chips (NS_Impact_Glass_Lrg without its crack decal, over a 3 x 3 grid). A sheet stays broken until the map loads again. Not done: the break's sound (the game's HaloAudioSound has no script call to play it), and glass in the structure BSP itself (the world shell's packing drops the breakable bit; Turf's is all instanced geometry).
How the open items were closed

A prop's collision on a child node (Zanzibar's crane and hinged lights, Derelict's trees) is placed by the render model's rest pose; a scaled placement (Zanzibar's bushes at 2x to 4x) gets a copy of the model and collision with the scale baked in (<name>_x2__scen.gltf). Every instance's incident light direction, and the light of vertex-lit instanced geometry (Lockout's 26 light fixtures), come from Halo 2's lightmap vertex buckets. A vertex-lit instance draws its vertices' mean light from a texel of its own on a page after the last (the CE masters sample light through lightmap coordinates, so per-vertex colour has no slot); the incident direction still varies per vertex. Cube maps and the scrolling shader animations (cloud banks, gas, grav lifts) are converted; see Shaders above.

Only BSP 0 is converted (every multiplayer map has one). Placed object models take each region's first permutation at its most detailed level. Specular's colour blends by the view (N.V) where Halo 2's blends by the light (N.L), and alpha-tested templates other than tex_alpha_test have none (see Specular). The sun shafts' fade towards edge-on (the vertex colour going from the facing colour to black as (N.V)^2) has no CE chicago equivalent; they draw at their facing colour. An env reflection's colour is one hue (the mean of the facing and glancing colours) baked into a copy of the cube, and its facing-to-glancing blend uses CE's squared view term rather than Halo 2's linear one. plasma_alpha's fade comes from its vertex shader (transparent_generic_reflection), not read back: M_H2_PlasmaAlpha takes it as the facing term N.V , weighted by pixel constant 2's alpha as the pixel shader weights it. The level needs chunk 981 (pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2-Windows) installed: without it the level loader finds no parent for the plasma's slots ("parent material not found"). The loops' detail sounds (Ascension's thunder and wind gusts, at random periods and directions) are staged in sounds.json but not played; a loop attached to a marker plays at the object's origin. On maps other than Lockout, CTF sides and vehicle teams come from the nearer CTF flag and vehicle game types from Halo 2's;

Lockout and Ascension have been started, Ascension only by a test camera. Install the way a local test map is installed (level bake --install-test and the map's 985/986 containers): --install also copies this project's material cook over chunk 988, which on a box with the hub's runtime replaces the runtime's masters. All 24 multiplayer maps stage; Lockout, Ascension and Zanzibar have been converted end to end and started.

A converted Halo 2 map goes through the same pipeline as the CE remasters (tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py, configured in tools/level/ce_upgrade_maps.json). Coagulation (COA) is the first, built 2026-11-12 and seen in game on PC 1 as local builds; it is not published. Convert from the .map itself, not from a staging folder elsewhere: the pipeline reads the staging beside the conversion (<conversion>/staging), and the level takes the map's name.

Stages: land, foliage, swap, editor, cook, bake, assemble, install. collision is skipped, so the bake uses the conversion's own BSP with its glass and physics-model surfaces; a swapped tree keeps Halo 2's collision. Ground and cliffs by name. Halo 2's detail bitmaps are not named detail_grass or detail_cliff, so the config names them: shaders, cliff_shaders (Coagulation's boulders, coag_rocks, among them, which draws them in the game's rock) and details (ground_dirt_pebble as sand, coag_grass as grass: the base map's alpha then says where each grows, as on a CE map). A look of its own. A landscape with no MAP_LOOKS entry in build_landscape.py gets Death Island's beach. Coagulation (LCO) takes Blood Gulch's: packed earth, stones on soil, its cliff mix. A pond is not a sea ("sea": false). The pipeline and the loader take any water mesh for the sea. Coagulation's pool by the cave sits 7 m up: grass grew only above it, so 1.8 of 2.2 million clumps stood on the plateau and none in the valley, and the valley floor drew as a beach (sand, ripples, shells). foliage_ceiling (cm): nothing is scattered on ground above it. Coagulation's plateau, 50 to 107 m up and out of sight, is left bare; the valley keeps about 290,000 clumps, Blood Gulch's count. Light. The conversion's sun stood at 28 degrees and the cliffs shaded the valley floor;

the config raises it to 55, turns the baked sun mask off (sun_mask: false, as Blood Gulch) and sets sun.lightmap_sun to [0.35, 0.62]: Halo 2's ground lightmap is a lavender 0.6 where CE's sunlit ground is 1.0. Blood Gulch's skylight, exposure and clouds, and haze: "ce" (a Halo 2 slot carries its fog as a CE one does). Halo 2's grass sprites are hidden (hide_materials: ["M_H2_Billboard"]): the scattered grass replaces them. A decorator placement is ground cover, not scenery the grass keeps clear of or a boulder to swap (decorator in placement.json): Coagulation's 218 decal fields cleared 20 m circles of grass until the scatter skipped them. Trees. Coagulation's trees are instanced BSP geometry, which placement.json never names. mjolnir cache stage writes every instance's name, frame, shaders and bounds to bsp/instances.json, and instance_swap: {"redcedar": "tree_pine"} has tools/level/instance_scenery.py turn the instances with such a shader into scenery entries for the swap: its three red cedars stand as A30's pines, sized to each cedar's height, their Halo 2 slots hidden. Chunk 1001. Halo 2 remasters take numbers from 1001 up (docs/chunk_numbering.md). The landscape container's library holds the same two shader maps as every CE remaster's, so a textured landscape on a machine with a CE remaster installed does not prove library 1001 opened. Desert biome ("biome": "desert").

Coagulation's dirt and cliff feet are dressed from the game's dry-country plants and Poly Haven's Namaqualand pack (flowers, succulents, granite stones) instead of the beach's shells and driftwood: docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md. The pack cooks into the map's landscape container, so the map needs it in the editor project and a credit when published. Zanzibar (ZAN, chunk 1002, "biome": "coast"). A Fluid Flux coast at the fog plane's height, since the conversion has no water surface; sea life on the bed, sea campion, small palms at the walls' feet and the beach bushes as young palms. Its ground shaders list grass before sand, the reverse of CE: the bake and the mesh ground slots turn that over (docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md). Containment (CNT, chunk 1003, landscape LCN, "biome": "snow", 2026-11-16). Ice Fields' and Sidewinder's snow: B40's glacial rock on the cliffs (containment_cliff_a and the boulders' containment_rock_medium), Sidewinder's ground look, snowy stones and rubble scattered, the game's falling snow kept out of the bases (11,755 roof cells). Its terrain shader is not a blend, so it would have baked as one flat snow; with real_base the ground keeps its base map's own colour, which paints the tyre tracks and the dirt by the bases. Its bases are Forerunner, so the Forerunner plate stays on their metal (no structure_metal: false).

Swap and collision are skipped: its scenery is 8 brambles and twig decals (the twigs are M_H2_Billboard, hidden). Its gates and switches come from the conversion's own machines, as a fresh conversion places them; the install takes their actors (pakchunk987-MJOLNIRACT) from the conversion's machines folder (tools/level/machine_containers.py). In game, solo and in two networked copies: all 8 machines start shut, a switch group opens its own gate in both simulations, and the 8 part slots draw their cooked instances. Ascension (ASC, chunk 1004, landscape LAS, "biome": "desert", 2026-11-16). Its ground is a blend of bare slate and pale sandstone paths, so both detail maps are sand (stones and dry plants): taking the slate for grass grew 2.3 million clumps on bare rock. Grass stays on the cliffs' up-facing faces, where the cliff master draws its turf, which greens the rock pillars' tops. Blood Gulch's look, as Coagulation's. Reconverted first (ASC_flags) so its machines carry their own placement flags. Its three antennas are the conversion's turning machines, cooked. In game, solo and in two networked copies: the antennas turn in step and draw their cooked instances; a frame takes a median 11 ms at 4K. A ground with no grass class had crashed the scatter where a cliff's turf met it (scatter_foliage.py). Cladding only within reach.

Ascension first loaded in 4.2 s solo and 7.3 s on a client (the hub copy: 0.7 and 2.3 s). The loader dresses each cladding rock, a mesh actor, with its group's material, and Ascension had 120,427 of them: its pillars fall 150 m under the lowest spawn, and their walls took 80,000. The scatter now puts no rock more than 30 m under the map's lowest player spawn (--clad-floor, upgrade_ce_map.py's CLAD_BELOW_SPAWNS), which of all the remasters trims only Ascension and Gephyrophobia's chasm (3,905). Ascension: 40,390 rocks, 2.3 s solo, 3.5 s on a client. The loader's log now lists the queued jobs' time by kind (load timing: queued jobs:). Structure surfaces (structure_surfaces). Zanzibar's concrete and steel draw in Poly Haven PBR surfaces through the cliffs' master, each wall's Halo 2 base map kept as its colour and its lightmap as shade (docs/remaster_asset_inventory.md). The surfaces cook into the runtime container, so they too need a runtime release. Still CE-runtime bound. The cliffs' tessellated meshes cook into the trial masters' container (983), as for the CE remasters, and Halo 2's masters are in 981: publishing a Halo 2 remaster needs a runtime release with both. Measured on PC 1 at 4K, standing in the grass: 13.9 ms a frame, 2.5 ms of it the foliage. Not done: the pines against Halo 2's cedar collision is unchecked; no side-by-side from fixed cameras;
instance_swap replaces the conversion's own scenery list for the swap, so a map with both kinds swaps only its instances.

Status: 2026-10-21. Format v1 is proven with Blood Gulch: a pack built by mjolnir map pack, installed as the launcher will install it and registered by mjolnir level register, plays CTF. Phases 1 to 4 are done, but for the tag editor's map publishing: the hub takes map packs with a review queue, the launcher installs them with their dependencies and registers them (apps/launcher/src-tauri/src/maps.rs), and the 19 classic maps and the CE runtime pack are published, the remastered maps as 2.x releases of the same listings. The tag editor's map publishing and the Rust cook (Phase 5) remain: see Phases. Update 2026-11-21: Halo 2 maps, Custom Edition conversions, Forge maps and Pelican Warfare are published the same way. Converted Halo CE maps (ce_map_conversion.md) reach players the way texture swaps and tag edits do. Each map is baked ahead of time, uploaded through the mod hub, stored in R2, and installed by the launcher. Players can publish their own maps the same way. Three rules shape everything below:

No game-derived bytes in git. A baked map clones shipped tags (the canvas scenario, the donor BSP, object definitions) and carries CE's geometry, textures and sounds. These bytes live only in R2, behind the hub. The repository holds the tools, the code mods and the design. No Unreal Editor on a player's machine. Baking needs the editor today (the materials and sounds cook), so maps ship pre-baked. Player publishing waits on the Rust cook (Phase 5). Anything executable still ships only from signed CI. A map pack is data: containers, JSON, textures and Megalo variants (bytecode the game's own interpreter runs, sandboxed like a game type). The loader and lobby that read it are code mods, released by release-mods.yml as before.

Piece Kind Published by Holds A map, e.g. ce-blood-gulch hub content, with a map listing map author the map's containers, level file, registration record mjolnir-ce-runtime hub content us everything every converted map shares MJOLNIRLevelLoader, MJOLNIRLobby code mods signed CI the loader, the multiplayer menu, the game types (.mglo)

A .mjolnir archive (mjolnir_format.md) of type map: mjolnir.json manifest: type "map", plus the map block below signature.json added by mjolnir map pack --sign (below) content/ pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-_P.utoc the scenario, its BSP, and the map's own world pakchunk997-MJOLNIRMAP-_P.ucas pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMESH-_P.utoc the terrain mesh pakchunk986-MJOLNIRMESH-_P.ucas pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-_P.utoc the map's cooked CE textures, lightmaps and pakchunk985-MJOLNIRCOOK-_P.ucas ambient sounds pakchunk-MJOLNIRLAND-_P.utoc a remastered map's landscape world, with a pakchunk-MJOLNIRLAND-_P.ucas shader library the launcher renumbers with it pakchunk996-MJOLNIRBANK-_P/.bnk a vehicle's Wwise banks (below), beside that container's .utoc and .ucas map/ level.json the level file the loader reads registration.json the bake's registration record (below) bots.json where the bot squads stand, for MJOLNIRHud (a map with bots; docs/bots.md) vehicle_sounds.json a custom vehicle's sounds and lights, for the loader (docs/custom_vehicles.md) the foliage placements the level file names decals/*.png its decals' textures docs/README.md optional Format rules (version 1):

Every package a map adds lives under /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/, so two maps never claim the same package. The level file names only /Game paths: either the map's own, or the runtime pack's. A map cooks into a chunk of its own, 10000 + int(CODE, 36) (Blood Gulch, BGL, is 24853). A PrimaryAssetLabel at the map's root sets it, so the map's cook never mixes with the runtime pack's chunk 988. No .mglo and no code. The only loose files are the level's own data under map/, which the mods read beside the level file: the foliage file the level names (a remastered map's foliage.bin), its decals' textures, and a map with bots' bots.json (mjolnir map pack takes it from the bake's <CODE>.bots.json). A map's preview is its hub listing's cover image, not a file in the pack. The manifest's map block: { "schema_version": 1, "name": "Blood Gulch", "version": "1.0.0", "type": "map", "map": { "code": "BGL", "title": "Blood Gulch", "modes": ["slayer", "ctf"], "size": "large", "players": { "min": 4, "max": 16 }, "vehicles": true, "game": "halo1" }, "compat": { "min_build": "2026.08.11.1121610.2" }, "deps": [{ "slug": "mjolnir-ce-runtime", "range": "^1.0.0" }] }

code is the three-character scenario codename. It is unique across the hub, which rejects a second map claiming a code someone else's map holds, whether that map is listed or waiting for review. modes lists the game types the multiplayer menu offers. Each one must be a variant the loader ships (slayer, ctf, ...). size, players, vehicles, origin and game are optional catalog metadata, what players filter the hub's map list by (below). A release that leaves one out keeps the value the listing already has. origin is custom_edition or original; classic is set by moderators only. game is the game the map comes from, halo1 (Halo CE) or halo2 (Halo 2). Field rules are in mjolnir_format.md. The registration record is what mjolnir level bake --standalone writes beside its output as <CODE>.registration.json: the codename, the canvas scenario it was cloned from, the title, the description and the world path. The launcher builds the shared registration container from these records (below). A map pack carries no .mglo. Game types are code-reviewed scripts the loader ships, so a map can only name them. Custom game types per map are Phase 6.

A vehicle built by tools/level/ce_vehicle_audio.py plays through Wwise banks. A .pak can hold any file in the game, so an archive never carries one. map pack takes the banks out of the .pak the build left beside the container and writes them as bare members, content/<container>/<id>.bnk. The launcher builds the .pak itself under its own mount name, so a bank can only land at Meteorite/Content/WwiseAudio/<id>.bnk. The hub's scan (hub/src/lib/api/banks.ts) and the launcher (crates/ue-iostore/src/bank.rs) apply the same rules, and map pack holds each bank to them as it writes the archive: A member sits at exactly content/<container>/<id>.bnk. The container is a plain name with its .utoc in the same archive, and the id is written as a plain number. The id is not in defs/hce/shipped_banks.json. A map pack must not change the sound of a stock vehicle on every other map. The bank is version 150 and its header's id is the one in its name. BKHD comes first, the sections are only BKHD, DIDX, DATA and HIRC, each once, and every section, media entry and HIRC record stays in bounds. A bank is at most 16 MiB, and a release at most 32 banks and 48 MiB of them. The scan holds them in memory.

These rules keep a member to being a bank. They don't prove Wwise reads one safely: the record bodies go to Wwise's own parser, in every player's game. So anyone may publish banks, but a new author's wait for a moderator, whatever the release's type (review). Nothing checks two packs for the same id. Ids hash from names carrying the map's code, so only a copied id collides, and then one map's bank shadows the other's. Installing. The launcher keeps a release's banks at <release>/banks/<container>/<id>.bnk in its cache and records each one's hash beside the containers', so verify and repair cover them. Every write to Paks builds the .pak again from the cache, so an update, a reorder or a repair keeps the banks, and uninstall removes it with the rest of the triple. A bank gone from the cache counts as a damaged install: it never turns into a silent stub. Older launchers. Launcher 0.22.0 and older skip a .bnk under content/, as they skip any member that isn't a container, and write a stub .pak. The map installs and plays, and the vehicle has no engine or horn. Nothing warns the player: the hub has no gate on launcher version, and launcher_features.txt is the game asking about the launcher, not the hub. Release order.

Release the launcher that takes banks, and let players update to it. Deploy the hub with the scan (ts-5). Until then the hub refuses .bnk as a forbidden kind. Apply migrations 0025 and 0026 first: /complete writes banks_json and map_json, so without them every publish fails. Publish maps with banks, and approve the ones waiting for review. Step 2 lets authors upload banks, so moderators leave those releases pending until step 1 is done. The other way round, players on an older launcher get a silent vehicle with no error.
The pieces › The CE runtime pack
This pack is published by us and updated when a shared piece changes (1.19.0 as of mods 0.46.1). It holds everything converted maps share. tools/level/build_ce_runtime.sh builds most of it:
The pieces › The CE runtime pack

Container Holds pakchunk988-MJOLNIRMAT-Windows the CE material masters (/Game/MJOLNIR/CE/M_CE_*) and their shader library; the CTF flag's textures (/Game/MJOLNIR/CE/CTF); the announcer and event sounds (/Game/MJOLNIR/Sounds/Events) pakchunk990-MJOLNIRCTFMESH_P the CE flag mesh (/Game/MJOLNIR/CTF/SM_CE_Flag) pakchunk990-MJOLNIRFLAG_P, -FLAGB_P, -STAND_P, -MOTL_P the red and blue CTF flag weapons (model variants default and blue, which the loader colours them by), their stand, and the object-type-list override that adds them as entries 18 and 20 pakchunk994-MJOLNIRSPAWN_P, 993-MJOLNIRTELES_P, 992-MJOLNIRTELER_P, 991-MJOLNIRTELE2_P the spawn point and the teleporter sender, receiver and 2-way pakchunk990-MJOLNIRHPACK_P, -HPSPOT_P, -HPMESH_P the health pack, its spawn spot and its mesh pakchunk990-MJOLNIRSPARTAN_P the Spartan model with its body material on the body damage section (shipped on the head section, every bullet hit was a headshot) pakchunk990-MJOLNIRFLUX_P Fluid Flux's infinite sea (NS_InfiniteSurfaceMesh) with fixed bounds 10 km tall: the shipped ones are 50 m round Z 0, and a sea far below it (Yoyorast's, -256 m) was culled whole when the top of the view was level. Byte offsets, so it is rebuilt for every game update pakchunk980-MJOLNIRFORGEUI-Windows the Forge HUD and its glyphs;

MJOLNIRForge shows its text panel without it pakchunk990-MJOLNIRFORGEMON_P Forge's monitor, the editor model the simulation creates; MJOLNIRLobby offers FORGE only with it installed pakchunk995-MJOLNIRBOT-<kind>-<level>_P (15) the bots' characters, which every map with bots requires (from 1.16.0; bots.md) pakchunk984-MJOLNIRUI-Windows the multiplayer screens and HUD widgets (custom_ui.md) pakchunk981-MJOLNIRH2-Windows the Halo 2 masters (/Game/MJOLNIR/H2, Scripts/build_h2_materials.py): M_H2_PlasmaAlpha, which converted Halo 2 maps' plasma draws with (h2_map_conversion.md) pakchunk966-MJOLNIRKOTH-Windows King's hill materials (koth_visuals.md) and the CTF flag's cloth master (/Game/MJOLNIR/Cloth/M_CE_FlagCloth, Scripts/build_flag_cloth.py), with their shader library: the GPU waves the cloth from the material's Time, so the loader moves nothing per frame. Without it, the loader moves the cloth's strips from Lua pakchunk985-MJOLNIRMENU_P the main menu with its own MULTIPLAYER button (multiplayer_menu.md). It replaces the shipped menu, so it is rebuilt for every game update pakchunk983-MJOLNIRCETRIAL-Windows the trial masters the remastered maps draw with (/Game/MJOLNIR/CETrial, Scripts/build_ce_materials.py) and their tessellated cliffs (Scripts/build_ce_cliffs.py).
The pieces › The CE runtime pack

tools/level/upgrade_ce_map.py cooks it, not build_ce_runtime.sh, and looks it up among the installed runtime's containers tools/level/pack_remastered.py leaves the water masters (M_CE_Ocean, chunk 982, Scripts/build_ce_water.py) out of the map packs: like the trial masters, they go in the runtime pack. A map's ambient sounds are not shared. They cook into the map's own chunk, under /Game/MJOLNIR/Maps/<CODE>/Sounds, so a map ships only the sounds it plays. Its containers are content containers, so they install like any content mod. Its version moves when a shared piece changes; maps depend on a compatible range. mjolnir map runtime <out dir> --version X --sign packages the builder's output as the mjolnir-ce-runtime content mod. The CTF variant the loader ships names the object types it creates, and the simulation wipes a variant naming one the installed object type list lacks (0x409c40 -> 0x40a310): CTF then has no rules at all. So the runtime release that adds -FLAGB_P and the list's entry 20 goes out before, or with, the mods release whose ctf.mglo creates the blue flag (type 20). The lobby offers CTF only when the blue flag's container is installed, and mjolnir megalo write --mode ctf --single-flag still writes the one-type script for a list without entry 20 (game_modes.md, 2.2).

What Where Map and runtime containers Meteorite/Content/Paks, named by the launcher (pakchunk<N>-MJOLNIRHUB-<slug>-<j>_<v>_P, with N from 10000 and v from 1000: chunk_numbering.md), with .pak siblings: a stub, or a vehicle's banks Map data (map/) Binaries/<Win64\ WinGDK>/ue4ss/MJOLNIRMaps/<CODE>/ The map list ue4ss/MJOLNIRMaps/maps.json, generated The registration container Paks/pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P.{utoc,ucas,pak}, generated Map-owned authored PBR masters also carry a shader library. Their conversion container therefore keeps cook_chunk(CODE) (TST: pakchunk48621-MJOLNIRCOOK-TST_P) instead of the legacy texture-only pakchunk985 name. Local installation and archive staging read materials.spec.json and reject missing correctly named outputs; a stale 985 container cannot substitute for the authored cook.

Before launcher 0.24.0, a container that carried a shader library kept its own chunk number in the name the launcher gave it (pakchunk988-MJOLNIRHUB-…), not a load order number. Launcher 0.24.0 and newer give every container a number of its own and rename its shader library to match; only the runtime containers listed in config/fixed_chunks.json keep their cooked number (chunk_numbering.md). The reason either is needed: UE opens a mounted pak's shader library by the number it reads off the file name (ShaderCodeLibrary.cpp, OnPakFileMounted), so the CE material masters renamed to pakchunk9NN would mount without their shaders. Map data lives outside Mods/MJOLNIRLevelLoader. The launcher digests each code mod's folder to detect tampering, so files written into the loader's folder would make it read as "Modified". The loader reads ue4ss/MJOLNIRMaps first and still falls back to its own levels/ folder, so maps converted locally with --install keep working.

The simulation builds its map list at boot from the cooked DT_Scenarios table and the campaign's ScenarioList (new_scenario_loading.md). So one container must list every installed map. A map cannot ship its own copy: two maps would claim the same chunks, and only one would win. The container is also a modified copy of shipped data. The launcher therefore builds it locally after every map install, uninstall, enable or disable. The build is mjolnir level register: read every enabled map's registration.json; clone DT_Scenarios and DA_FirstPlayableCampaign from the player's own game files, and add one row and one handle per map (blam_pack::scenario::register); write pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P and maps.json. The launcher links blam-pack for this, so it never runs the CLI. It rebuilds only when the set of enabled maps, a map's registration.json or the game build changed since the last rebuild, which it records in MJOLNIRMaps/.mjolnirhub-registered.json. The game build is a fingerprint of the shipped containers' names, sizes and times. Launching the game checks it, so a game update gets a new registration before the game reads the old one. A rebuild takes about a second. A registration built by hand (mjolnir level register, no record) is left alone until the launcher has a map to register.

maps.json also carries each map's game types, which come from its level.json, not its registration. When an update to an installed map changes only its level file (new game types, for one), the registration stands and the launcher writes maps.json alone again. The record keeps the size and time of every enabled map's level.json for this. A record written before launcher 0.24.3 has neither fingerprint, so the first launch after that update rebuilds once. Map folders the launcher writes carry a .mjolnirhub marker. It removes only those. Uninstalling UE4SS from the launcher also removes the registration container it built.

Installing a map installs what it depends on first. Its manifest's deps come from the hub (the CE runtime pack, at its newest release). Only a range's floor is enforced: since launcher 0.14.0 a dependency that is installed but older than the floor (the 1.8.0 of a ^1.8.0) is updated first. The code mods are implied by type map: MJOLNIRCore, MJOLNIRLevelLoader, MJOLNIRLobby and MJOLNIRHud. Each is installed when missing, updated when the launcher installed it and nobody edited it, and switched on in mods.txt. A map whose code another installed map holds is refused. Install multiplayer (the launcher's Multiplayer page, hub::install_multiplayer) runs this for every official map of a game (GET /maps?official=1&game=<game>), then materializes and registers once. Maps already at their newest release are skipped, so running it again is an update. Since launcher 0.14.1 a map whose cache lacks a file its level names (its foliage file, decals/) is fetched again rather than skipped.

A map whose shader library is cooked under a number outside 900 to 999, or under a number another mod's library already uses, needs a launcher with local chunk numbers. The hub works this out when it scans the release (requires: ["local-chunk-numbers"]) and keeps the release from older launchers. The launcher ships, then the hub change deploys, and only then is such a map published. The order and what each launcher does are in chunk_numbering.md.

tools/level/convert_ce_map.sh maps/bloodgulch.map BGL out/bgl mjolnir map pack out/bgl --code BGL --version 1.0.0 --sign map pack collects the conversion's containers (*-<CODE>_P), its level file and its registration record into the archive, and writes the manifest. --sign signs it with this machine's device key (the tag editor's, under DPAPI), which the hub requires. A map's own machines and controls (tags under objects\mjolnir\<code>\) ship in -MJOLNIRMACH-<CODE>- containers, from the folder's machines/. map pack stops if the level places one no container holds. The map would still load, with no error and those objects gone, and a PC with the containers loose in its Paks folder would never show it, as Yoyorast 2.6.0 and 2.7.0 didn't. The tag editor publishes it, as it publishes content mods: it signs the archive with the publisher's device key, then creates or updates the hub mod and uploads the release (POST /mods, POST /mods/{slug}/releases, PUT /releases/{id}/archive, POST /releases/{id}/complete). CI cannot bake, since it has no copy of the game, so maps are published from a maintainer's machine.

Update 2026-10-21: the tag editor still publishes only its own project (project_publish), and no tool in this repository uploads a map pack or uses the hub's upload in parts (below). The remastered maps are staged and packed by tools/level/pack_remastered.py <CODES> --version 2.x.y --runtime <range> --sign, which takes each map's cooked textures from its installed hub release and hands the folder to mjolnir map pack.

Players publish the same way. Until the Rust cook lands, they need the Unreal Editor and the MJOLNIRMaterials project, which in practice means us. Review. A map release from a new author does not go live on a passing scan, and neither does any release carrying banks. The release stays pending with a row in release_reviews until a moderator approves it (/moderation/releases), because a map carries game-derived bytes and names game types the loader will run, and a bank goes to Wwise's own parser. Moderators and authors at trust level 2 or higher skip the queue. Content releases without banks keep auto-publishing. Moderators work the queue in the Releases tab of /moderation, which shows each release's banks and scan findings. A rejection needs a reason, and the author reads it on the mod's manage page, /mods/{slug}/manage, which lists every release of the mod whatever its status (GET /mods/{slug}/releases/all), wherever it was published from. A review is of one archive. Uploading a new one takes the release out of the queue until /complete scans it, and the page sends the hash of the archive it showed, so a decision on a replaced archive is refused.

A held release changes nothing players see. Its map block waits on the release (mod_releases.map_json, migration 0026) and reaches the listing on approval; a rejection leaves the listing as it was. The listing follows the newest published release, so one approved after a newer one publishes without taking the listing back. A release in the queue holds its code against other mods, as a listing does: the scan refuses a second map claiming it, whoever the author is, until a moderator decides. Rejection frees the code. Only the queue holds one, so a release a new archive took out of it holds nothing until /complete scans it, and an abandoned upload can't keep a code where no moderator can see it. Two scans in the same instant can't see each other, so both can reach the queue. Then the first approval takes the code and the other is refused with a 409, which is a moderator's cue to reject it.

A map is a content mod. mods.type is a trust tier and stays content; what makes a mod a map is its row in map_listings (migration 0012), keyed by the mod and holding the code, title, game types, whether it is an official classic, and the catalog metadata (migration 0017). GET /mods/{slug} reports a map pack as type: "map" with its map_code.

The scanner, for a manifest of type map: requires the map block, and only a map archive may carry one; requires map/level.json and map/registration.json, as valid JSON; warns about containers not named for the map (-<CODE>_P); rejects a code another mod's listing or held release has (map_code_taken). The archive limits are those of any content release. One request (PUT /releases/{id}/archive) takes up to 90 MiB, under Cloudflare's 100 MB request body. A bigger archive, up to 1 GiB, goes up in parts: POST /releases/{id}/archive/multipart, parts of 5 to 64 MiB, then .../multipart/{upload_id}/complete joins them. The release's POST /releases/{id}/complete then scans the stored archive from R2 as a stream. A remastered map with its foliage runs past one request (Timberland 2.1.0 is 117 MiB). A map release writes its map_listings row when it publishes: at the scan, or on approval if it was held (review). A first release that's held has no row yet, because lobbies, matches and leaderboards read titles from the listing by code. deps are recorded in release_deps.

GET /api/v1/maps lists published maps with their newest release, cover image, and metadata: Field Values size small, medium, large, or null players_min, players_max 1 to 16, or null vehicles true, false, or null origin classic (the converted stock maps), custom_edition, original, or null game halo1 (Halo CE), halo2 (Halo 2), or null Migration 0017 fills these for the 19 Halo CE classics, and migration 0023 sets game to halo1 on every map published before it. Authors set them in the manifest, and the mod's owner, its authors and moderators change them with PATCH /api/v1/maps/{code} (only moderators may set or change classic). With no parameters, /maps returns every map (up to 500), from every game, in one list: the official classics first, then by title. The game's map list relies on that form, so filters and paging are opt-in. The launcher's Install multiplayer asks for /maps?official=1&game=halo1, the official Halo CE maps, and its optional Install Halo 2 maps for /maps?official=1&game=halo2. An older launcher asks for /maps?official=1, which lists the official maps of both games.

Parameter Effect official 1 official maps only, 0 community maps only mode maps offering this game type q title, code or summary contains this (up to 80 characters) size, vehicles, origin, game exact match; a map that never declared the field is left out players maps whose player range includes this count; a map with no range is kept sort newest, downloads, rating or title; absent keeps official first, then title limit, cursor page size 1 to 100, and the next_cursor of the previous page The response is { maps, next_cursor }. next_cursor is null on the last page. The website's /maps page is built on the same query. GET /mods takes map=0 to leave map packs out (the website's /mods page does) and map=1 to list only them; every mod carries cover_url and map_code for its card.

The website hands off to the desktop launcher through the mjolnir:// scheme, which launcher 0.13.0 and newer register: Link Opens mjolnir://map/<CODE> the map, ready to install (map cards and map pages) mjolnir://mod/<slug> a mod's page in the launcher (mod pages) mjolnir://join/<lobby id> joins a listed game (/games, and the live strip on /matches)

Map data outside the loader. The loader and the lobby read ue4ss/MJOLNIRMaps; mjolnir level register builds the registration container and maps.json from the records there. Map packs. mjolnir map pack; the tag editor's map publishing; the hub's map listings, scanner rules and review queue. The launcher (done). It installs maps, resolves dependencies, and builds the registration container on every change. The CE runtime pack, and our maps (done). The shared containers move into the runtime pack, and each map's textures and sounds cook into a chunk of its own. Then we publish Blood Gulch, Gephyrophobia and the rest of the stock maps. The Rust cook. Textures and sounds are written as cooked packages by rewriting shipped ones, as meshes already are (ue_mesh_write.md). mjolnir map build <ce.map> then converts a map end to end with no Unreal Editor, and players can publish their own. Later. Custom game types per map (reviewed .mglo in a map pack), map previews (map/preview.png) in the menu and on the hub, and collections ("CE classics"). Map previews landed another way: the game and the launcher show each map's hub cover image (cover_url; PR #165 and #166), and nothing reads a map/preview.png.

Before launcher 0.24.0: TST reserved shader chunk 968, because older launchers classify only pakchunk9NN-MJOLNIR... as supported and an authored shader cook had to keep its actual chunk. Launcher 0.24.0 and newer accept any number and renumber on install (chunk_numbering.md).

Status: the engine behaviour proven in game on 2026-11-11 (PC 1, Steam CU4); rollout steps 1 to 4 built in the launcher the same day (see What was built). Steps 5 and 6 and the shared-library move remain (see Remaining).

A container's file name starts pakchunk<N>. Today that one number does three jobs: Shader library name. The engine opens a mounted pak's shader library by the number in the file name: pakchunk978… opens Meteorite_Chunk978. A container with a library has to keep the number it was cooked with. Load order. The launcher names hub containers pakchunk9NN, with NN the mod's place in the profile's load order, on the assumption that a higher number wins. Ownership. The launcher treats pakchunk9NN-MJOLNIR… as ours and sets every other non-game container aside as an unsupported mod. That gives every author, every tool and every installed mod one shared space of 100 numbers: 966 to 999 are taken by our own shipped containers, and 969 to 979 by the eleven CE remasters. There is no number left for a twelfth. Hub load-order numbers start at 900 and PC 1 is at 965. The next installs reuse numbers our shipped libraries own. order_number clamps at 999, so every mod past the hundredth gets the same number. Two authors who cook a library under the same number cannot be installed together, and nothing tells them which numbers are free.

Read from UE 5.5 source, then checked in game. Fact Source In game The number after pakchunk can have any number of digits. GenericPlatformMisc.cpp GetPakchunkIndexFromPakFile A container named pakchunk20001… mounts and its library opens. A library's chunk ID is CityHash64 of lower-cased UTF-16 <Project>_Chunk<N>-<format>. Shader code chunks are keyed by content hash and do not depend on N. ShaderCodeArchive.cpp GetShaderCodeArchiveChunkId The computed ID matches the library chunk in all eleven remaster containers (format PCD3D_SM6-PCD3D_SM6). So a library can be renamed to another number by rewriting one chunk ID in the .utoc. The .ucas is untouched. n/a TST's library renamed 968 → 20001 and mounted as pakchunk20001…: the map draws fully. The same file mounted as pakchunk20002… draws the default checker material on the same building. Blood Gulch's library cannot show this: its shader maps are in other installed libraries too. Load priority is the folder's base order plus 100 × (v + 1) for a name ending _<v>_P (plain _P counts as v = 0). The same value orders the IoStore containers. IPlatformFilePak.cpp FPakPlatformFile::Mount Two containers holding the same map: the one with the higher suffix loads, whichever has the higher chunk number: _9_P over _P both ways round, and _3000_P over _2000_P with the loser being the name that wins a plain tie.

With equal priority, the container mounted last wins, and files mount in reverse name order. So the name that sorts lower wins. Design › 1. Load order is the _<v>_P suffix

The launcher names each hub container …_<v>_P, where v comes from the profile's load order: later in the list, higher v. This is the engine's own priority field and it does not depend on name sorting. Thousands of mods fit. Our shipped overrides (990 to 999: registration, flags, spawns, teleporters) were to get suffixes chosen to reproduce what wins today. What wins today was measured (next section) before choosing.
Design › 2. The chunk number is assigned on the player's machine

When the launcher writes a profile into Paks it gives every container a number of its own from a wide local range (for example 10000 upward), and for a container with a shader library rewrites the library's chunk ID to match (ue_iostore::shader_library::renumber). The number an author cooked with stops mattering once the container is installed: No registry, no reserved bands for authors, no coordination between games. Two mods cooked under the same number install side by side. A container without a library can share one number; it has nothing to open. Uniqueness only has to hold among the containers mounted on one machine, and the launcher sees all of them. Our own runtime containers that Lua or tools name by number (980, 984, 985, 988 and the rest) keep their numbers. Those are a short fixed list in the repo, checked by a test for duplicates.
Design › 3. Ownership is the MJOLNIR marker
is_mjolnir_container accepts any chunk number, and keeps requiring the -MJOLNIR marker.
Design › 4. Remasters stop shipping duplicate libraries

Measured on PC 1: the eleven remaster libraries (969 to 979) hold two shader maps between them. One is in all eleven, the other in five. Neither is in a runtime container today. Shipping those two once in the runtime pack would leave a remaster whose materials add nothing new with no library and no number at all. Whether a Halo 2 remaster cooks to the same two maps has not been checked. shader_lib_overlap reports this for any Paks folder.

Measured 2026-11-11 on PC 1's active profile (55 entries, 582 cached containers) plus every loose MJOLNIR container in Paks: every chunk two containers share, with the bytes compared, and the winner by the rule above (equal _P priority, lower name wins). Where the shipped overrides live. On a player's machine the flag, spawn, teleporter, bot and menu containers (990 to 995, 985) are not loose: they are containers of the mjolnir-ce-runtime hub mod, written into Paks as pakchunk900-MJOLNIRHUB-mjolnir-ce-runtime-<j>_P (libraries at their cooked 966, 981, 982, 983, 988). The only loose 99x container the launcher writes is the registration, pakchunk996-MJOLNIRREG_P (maps.rs). The other 99x writers (build_ce_runtime.sh, convert_ce_map.sh, upgrade_ce_map.py local installs, build_spawn_point.sh, build_ctf_flag.sh, blam-cli ue and level commands) install loose files on developer machines only.

The launcher gate and release order

Decided 2026-11-11: content that only works with local chunk numbers must not reach a player on an older launcher silently; they get "update your launcher" instead. What needs a newer launcher. A release carrying a shader library cooked under a number outside 900 to 999 (launchers before local numbers set that container aside as unsupported), or under the same number as another mod's library (they open only one of the two). The hub measures this when it scans a release and records it as the release's requires list, entry local-chunk-numbers; authors do not declare it. A library number already used by another mod's ungated release gates the newcomer, never the original. What each launcher does.
The launcher gate and release order

This launcher and later send User-Agent: MJOLNIR-Launcher/<version>, X-MJOLNIR-Launcher: <version> and X-MJOLNIR-Features: local-chunk-numbers on every hub request (hub.rs, launcher_headers). A release whose requires names a feature the launcher lacks is never chosen, never offered as an update, and refused at install or enable with "needs a newer MJOLNIR launcher … Update the launcher, then try again" (needs_newer_launcher). The feature list is compiled in (LAUNCHER_FEATURES), as Forge packs' requires is. Launchers up to 0.23.0 send no User-Agent and no headers, which is how the hub tells them from browsers. The hub leaves gated releases out of their release lists and map listings, so they install the newest release they can use. When a mod has nothing else, the newest gated release stays listed and GET /releases/{id} reports its status as a sentence telling them to update the launcher, which they show as "Release is …, not published"; the download itself is refused. Browsers and other clients with a User-Agent see everything as before. Not covered. A player on an old launcher who joins a host running a gated release by its exact id reads "That release is not published". The test for an old launcher is the missing User-Agent: anything else that calls the hub without one is treated the same way.
The launcher gate and release order

Releases scanned before the hub change is deployed carry no requires until scanned again. Release order, for content cooked under a new number (Halo 2, Reach and later remasters, community maps with their own libraries): Ship this launcher (launcher-v*) and let it be adopted. Which version number that is, is the release's call; nothing stores it. Deploy the hub with the requires scan and filtering. Only then publish such content. Content cooked under 900 to 999 with a number nobody else uses needs no gate and works on every launcher.
